headline: DRC Ebola deaths near 3,000 as UN warns virus is outrunning response
body: Confirmed Ebola deaths in the Democratic Republic of Congo have passed 2,950 out of over 6,100 cases, with more than 5,000 concentrated in Ituri province, per UN News (Sep 1). UN relief chief Tom Fletcher said “the response is growing and has been scaled up, but the virus is moving faster,” warning of a $1.1 billion funding shortfall even after he released $57 million in emergency funds.

headline: Nepal-Tibet flood toll passes 1,100 as PM shifts focus to rebuilding
body: Nepal’s confirmed death toll from the Bhotekoshi River flood disaster has risen to 1,114, with nearly 3,916 still missing and over 21,000 security personnel deployed in the search, per ABC News (Sep 2). PM Balendra Shah said the country is “moving forward from search, rescue and relief distribution to rehabilitation,” as 48 suspension bridges were damaged and China separately reported 16 dead and 546 missing on its side of the border.

headline: Cyprus ferry death toll rises to 10 as 18 remain missing
body: Five days after the FiloJet catamaran capsized off Kyrenia with 267 people aboard, Turkey’s Vice President Cevdet Yilmaz confirmed “the body of one more person has been recovered… the number of those who have died has risen to 10,” per APA (Sep 3). Eighteen people remain missing as divers and a submersible continue searching wreckage in waters over 500 metres deep; 239 people were rescued alive.

headline: Philippines monsoon death toll hits 39 as Pilandok exits
body: The Philippines’ weather-related death toll since Aug 1 has reached 39 after five more fatalities on Sep 2, with Benguet province hardest-hit at 15 deaths, per Philstar (Sep 3). Officials attributed the losses to “the combined effects of typhoons Luis, Maymay and Neneng and the southwest monsoon,” even as Tropical Storm Pilandok, packing 65kph winds, moved to exit the Philippine area of responsibility.

headline: Tilak Varma’s South Zone into Duleep Trophy final
body: South Zone beat North Zone by seven wickets in Bengaluru on Sep 2, with captain Tilak Varma’s unbeaten half-century alongside Smaran Ravichandran sealing an 80-run stand after MD Nidheesh’s five-wicket haul had restricted North Zone. Per The Tribune (Sep 2), South Zone now face Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s East Zone in the five-day final at Chennai’s MA Chidambaram Stadium starting Sep 6.

headline: Antonelli takes grid penalty at Monza, blowing open F1 title race
body: Championship leader Kimi Antonelli will start Sunday’s Italian GP from the back after Mercedes chose Monza — a track that rewards overtaking — to serve his grid penalty for exceeding his power-unit allocation. Per Sky Sports (Sep 3), title rivals George Russell and Lewis Hamilton and Lando Norris are poised to gain, with the report calling it a “crucial” weekend for Russell as Mercedes weighs its long-term priorities.

headline: Hadjar ruled out of Monza, Lawson deputizes again at Red Bull
body: Isack Hadjar will miss the Italian GP after the wrist injury he suffered in summer training failed to heal, with Red Bull confirming Wednesday that Liam Lawson will again partner Max Verstappen at Monza. Per Sky Sports (Sep 3), Lawson qualified just 0.1 seconds off Verstappen and finished seventh at the last outing in the Netherlands, and Red Bull said it “wishes him a speedy recovery” and hopes Hadjar is back for Madrid next weekend.

headline: Liverpool land £30m deadline-day goalkeeper from Genk
body: Liverpool confirmed a deal worth up to £30m for 18-year-old Belgian goalkeeper Lucca Brughmans from KRC Genk, signing him to a six-year contract before he stays on loan at Genk for this season. Per Anfield Index (Sep 1), the 6ft 7in stopper — who has started all four of Genk’s league games this season — will officially join Liverpool for the 2027-28 campaign, with the full fee dependent on performance clauses.

headline: Brent Crude Tops $97 as Iran Fires Missiles at Kuwait
body: Brent futures broke above $97/barrel Thursday before settling near $96.20, up more than 7% on the week, after Kuwait's armed forces said they faced “ongoing Iranian aggression” and intercepted incoming missiles and drones, per CNBC (Sep 3). Energy Secretary Chris Wright said 17 million barrels transited the Strait of Hormuz on Monday — a wartime record under US military escort, versus roughly 20 million pre-war — while President Trump said of the conflict, “I don’t think it will be very much longer…I don’t know how much more they can take.”

headline: Fed's Waller Muddies September Hike Outlook, Ties It to CPI
body: Fed Governor Christopher Waller said Wednesday the August CPI report due Sep 11 will decide his vote, telling reporters he would back holding rates but “if inflation comes in hot, I would consider a rate hike,” since borrowing costs are only “slightly restricting” demand, per AP (Sep 3). His comments knocked CME FedWatch odds of a September hike down sharply from two days earlier, reversing some of the hawkish momentum from Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks, and sent stocks up and the 10-year yield lower.

headline: August Jobs Report Due Today, Fed Decision Riding on It
body: The Bureau of Labor Statistics releases the August employment report later Friday, with economists forecasting a rebound to roughly +53,000 nonfarm payrolls (from July's decline) and unemployment holding at 4.1%, per CNBC (Sep 3). The print lands 12 days before the Fed's Sep 16 decision, and after Wednesday's weak ADP reading (38,000 private jobs added), analysts say a miss would likely push September rate-hike odds down further while a strong beat could revive them.

headline: Gold Rebounds 3% to $4,544 as Rate-Hike Bets Cool
body: Gold jumped roughly 3% to $4,544.80/oz on Thursday, reversing its retreat from record highs, as Waller's dovish-leaning remarks, a softer dollar, and easing oil prices combined to cut rate-hike odds, per Yahoo Finance (Sep 3). One analyst noted, “If the jobs report misses expectations, and September rate hike bets decline, that could see gold move higher” ahead of Friday's payrolls data.

headline: Broadcom Stock Slips Despite AI Chip Sales Tripling
body: Broadcom's Q3 FY2026 AI semiconductor revenue hit $16.7 billion, up 221% year-over-year, driving total revenue to $29.6 billion (+86%) and adjusted EPS of $3.32, both beating Wall Street estimates, per The Motley Fool (Sep 2). Shares still slipped after Q4 revenue guidance of $34.8 billion came in just shy of the Street's $35.03 billion target, despite AI revenue guidance rising to $21.7 billion (+236% YoY).

headline: DOJ Files Brief Backing OpenAI's Fair-Use Defense vs NYT
body: The Justice Department filed a formal statement of interest supporting OpenAI in its copyright fight with The New York Times, arguing that training large language models is “extraordinarily transformative” fair use because models “develop general reasoning and language abilities” rather than copying text, per gHacks (Sep 3). The filing states “the United States has a strong interest in this court rejecting any argument that training LLMs on copyrighted texts violates copyright law”; the White House, OpenAI and the Times did not respond to requests for comment.

headline: Google, Anthropic, OpenAI Detail Cyber-Focused Models
body: Google launched Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber through its Fairwind Program, giving vetted security defenders early access for critical-infrastructure protection with improved autonomous vulnerability discovery. Anthropic introduced Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 alongside new Enterprise Frontier Safeguards, while OpenAI said its Astra model now meets the “Critical” cybersecurity capability threshold under its Preparedness Framework — all three framed as balancing offensive vulnerability-hunting power against misuse risk, per a roundup dated Sep 3.

headline: ChatGPT Health Adds Read-Only Access to Epic Patient Records
body: OpenAI's ChatGPT Health can now pull data directly from Epic's EHR system, which covers more than 325 million patients, letting clinicians import appointment notes, lab results, medications and specialist documentation for AI-assisted summaries and visit prep, per TechCrunch (Sep 1). Access is read-only — the AI cannot write back into patient charts — and some health systems are embedding ChatGPT directly into EHR workflows for pre-visit review and clinical-timeline building.

headline: Meta Preps ‘Hatch’ AI Agent Platform, Premium Tier
body: Meta is targeting early September for the launch of Hatch, an internal project to deploy autonomous agents that can navigate sites like DoorDash, Etsy, Reddit, Yelp and Microsoft Outlook on a user's behalf, per The Information (Aug 25-Sep 2). The rollout follows Meta's $18 billion teen-safety settlement clearing legal runway for new consumer AI products, and precedes an October target for Meta's next flagship model, “Watermelon,” which the company claims internally reaches GPT-5.5-level benchmarks on roughly 10x the compute of its predecessor.

headline: Google, Meta, MediaTek Line Up Behind Intel's EMIB-T Packaging
body: Google has reportedly selected Intel's EMIB-T advanced packaging for a future TPU generation, while MediaTek and Meta are evaluating it as a way to diversify away from TSMC's capacity-constrained CoWoS process, per SammyFans (Sep 1). Intel expects its advanced-packaging business “to ramp significantly from the second half of 2027 and become a more substantial contributor afterward,” positioning it as a credible alternative supplier for AI chipmakers squeezed by TSMC's packaging bottleneck.

headline: Vance rules out Iran talks, says Tehran’s grip on Hormuz “effectively gone”
body: US Vice President JD Vance said Iran’s “ability… to effectively control this water route has become effectively gone,” and ruled out negotiations unless “the attacks against commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz cease,” per Al Jazeera (Sep 4). Some 87 vessels have now been diverted from the strait amid the renewed fighting, as Vance separately said Hormuz oil flow was “almost” back to pre-war levels.

headline: Iran vows “asymmetrical” retaliation as ICC probe sought into wedding strike
body: Iran’s First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref vowed Tehran’s response to US attacks would be “asymmetrical” and “multi-layered,” per Daily Business News (Sep 3), as the death toll from the latest US strikes on Iran stood at 18. Iran’s Red Crescent formally asked the ICC to investigate the Kuhestak wedding strike that killed at least 4 and wounded 67, while UN envoy Gholamhossein Darzi called it “a grave violation of… international humanitarian law” amounting to “a war crime.”

headline: Kremlin floats Putin-Xi-Trump trilateral at upcoming APEC summit
body: Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said from the SCO summit in Bishkek that a three-way meeting between Vladimir Putin, Xi Jinping and Donald Trump was discussed for the next APEC forum, telling reporters “this issue was discussed, yes” and that “the three of them will be able to have a meeting” if plans align, per Cyprus Mail (Sep 1). The White House has not yet responded to requests for comment on the proposal.

headline: Zelensky says US envoys Witkoff, Kushner to visit Kyiv “in coming days”
body: President Zelensky said Trump envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are expected to make their first visit to Kyiv “in the coming days,” after multiple prior trips to Moscow, per Kyiv Independent (Sep 3). “It is important that the United States remains active,” Zelensky said, as a US peace plan remains stalled after the Kremlin rejected revisions, even as Russia hit Kyiv for an eighth consecutive day, striking a Coca-Cola plant and injuring 13.

headline: Palantir wins Army TITAN production contract, adds ex-AIG chief Zaffino
body: The Army Contracting Command awarded Palantir USG a prime agreement covering eight Tactical Intelligence Targeting Access Node (TITAN) ground-station systems — four Advanced and four Basic variants — moving the program from prototype into operational fielding, per a report citing the award (Sep 3). Separately, former AIG chief executive Peter Zaffino is joining Palantir as global head of financial services effective January 15, 2027, to expand the company’s push into commercial financial institutions.

headline: Tesla launches Cybercab robotaxi service in Austin
body: Tesla held its Cybercab launch event in Austin on September 3, confirming the two-seat, steering-wheel-and-pedal-free vehicle has entered production and that rides are now available in limited areas of Austin following employee test rides that began in July at Gigafactory Texas, per a report (Sep 4). The vehicle features a passenger touchscreen, roughly 20.2 cubic feet of trunk storage and USB-C charging, though Tesla has not confirmed retail pricing or a nationwide rollout timeline.

headline: CrowdStrike pulls forward $10B and $20B ARR targets at Fal.Con investor day
body: At its September 2 investor briefing, CrowdStrike said Q2 net new ARR hit $333 million, up 51% year-over-year and an all-time record, with ending ARR at $5.8 billion and Falcon Flex bookings value near $2.3 billion, up 101% year-over-year. The company pulled forward its long-term targets to $10 billion ARR by fiscal 2030 and $20 billion by fiscal 2035, and pointed to a $565 billion total addressable market by 2034, including $215 billion in AI security alone, alongside new SafeMind AI models it says cut cost-per-task by up to 99% versus frontier models.

headline: PayPal's ~$53 billion Stripe-Advent buyout talks collapse
body: Stripe and private-equity firm Advent walked away on August 27 from a proposed acquisition of PayPal that had been structured to value the company at more than $53 billion, per a report (Sep 1). The two sides could not agree on terms following PayPal's July 29 second-quarter results, which beat both earnings and revenue estimates, and PayPal ultimately pushed for a higher price than the bidders were willing to pay.

headline: Oracle rallies with rate-sensitive names after Fed's Waller eases rate-hike odds
body: Fed Governor Christopher Waller said on September 3 he would “support holding the policy rate at its current level” if inflation continues cooling, comments that cut traders’ odds of a September rate increase, per a report on the market reaction. Oracle, which sold $43 billion in bonds last year and plans a further $20 billion in debt plus a $20 billion equity raise this year to fund AI data-center buildout, is described as especially rate-sensitive given free cash flow that has turned deeply negative from that spending; no Oracle-specific announcement accompanied the move.

headline: Cloudflare adds Cursor coding-agent support to its Sandboxes platform
body: Cloudflare announced support for running Cursor Cloud Agents on its Cloudflare Sandboxes platform, letting Cursor manage the agent loop while terminal, filesystem and browser actions execute inside isolated, customer-controlled Cloudflare environments, per a report (Sep 3). The announcement followed Cloudflare's Q2 results showing revenue of $696.1 million, up 36% year-over-year, and recent analyst moves including Scotiabank's upgrade to Sector Outperform and Citi raising its price target to $400.

headline: C3.ai bookings jump 73% quarter-over-quarter even as revenue keeps sliding
body: C3.ai reported fiscal first-quarter 2027 revenue of $52.4 million, down from $70.3 million a year earlier, with a GAAP net loss of $92.8 million and a non-GAAP net loss of $30.7 million, per its September 2 earnings release. Bookings rose 73% quarter-over-quarter and free cash flow was positive $2.1 million with $651.1 million in cash on hand; the company guided second-quarter revenue to $51.0-$55.0 million and full-year fiscal 2027 revenue to $210.0-$240.0 million.

headline: Arm's data-center push gains steam on IBM tie-up and $2B AGI CPU backlog
body: Arm has been building momentum from a late-August expansion of its IBM partnership to embed Arm architecture into IBM Z and LinuxONE mainframes via what the companies call the first jointly developed dual-architecture processor, built on a 2nm process with 11 high-performance cores and AI fraud-detection accelerators, per a report (Aug 27). The same report noted Arm's AGI CPU, co-developed with Meta on TSMC's 3nm N3P process with up to 136 Neoverse V3 cores, has drawn more than $2 billion in advance orders — the company's first self-designed data-center processor after 35 years as a pure licensing business; no newer company-specific announcement was found for today's session.

headline: Congress presses fresh attack over ₹43 lakh crore GDP revision
body: Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh escalated the GDP growth row, arguing that “lowering the base year figure against which current growth is compared can inflate the growth rate, even if there is no real increase in economic activity,” per The News Mill (Sep 4). Citing ex-finance secretary Subhash Chandra Garg, Ramesh said nominal growth would have been roughly 2.6% — not the reported 10.3% — without a downward base-year revision covering FY23-FY26.

headline: Piyush Goyal hits back at Garg and Rajan over 7.8% growth figure
body: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal dismissed the government's critics, saying “they don’t even know how to compare apples with apples” and that “record growth of 7.8% is something that no other country has been able to replicate,” per The News Mill (Sep 3). He singled out Subhash Chandra Garg and former RBI governor Raghuram Rajan, saying both “could not complete their terms in government, and for the right reasons.”

headline: Pakistan denies demolition of Narowal temple, blames rain damage
body: Amid India's continuing protest over the destroyed century-old Hindu temple, Punjab's Minorities Affairs Minister Sardar Ramesh Singh Arora called demolition claims “baseless,” saying “a portion of a temple sign had collapsed due to torrential rainfall,” per WION (Sep 2). Minority rights activists countered that they found hammer marks on bricks and that the temple's dome and valuables had been removed and sold, with WION noting only 37 of Pakistan's 1,817 Hindu temples and Sikh gurdwaras remain operational.

headline: Modi touts 7.8% growth as ‘confidence for the world’ in Belgium talks
body: Hosting Belgian PM Bart De Wever in New Delhi, Modi said “India's economic growth is becoming a source of confidence and new opportunities for the world,” pointing to the 7.8% quarterly print even as it draws domestic fire, per The Northlines (Sep 3). He added that “a clean energy future and reliable supply chain are our shared priorities,” as the two sides agreed to double bilateral trade within five years.

headline: Holborn and St Pancras by-election looms after Starmer's exit
body: Starmer's resignation from Parliament has triggered a by-election in his Holborn and St Pancras seat, though LBC (Sep 2) reports “there is not yet a date or a list of candidates” and the Greens are considered likely to target the constituency. Starmer had called it “the best constituency in the country” to represent as he steps back from domestic politics entirely.

headline: Burnham dodges tax questions in marathon first PMQs
body: Facing Kemi Badenoch across the despatch box for the first time, Burnham refused to rule out Budget tax rises, saying “I’m not going to do what any prime minister has done and write the Budget here,” per the New Statesman (Sep 2). He insisted “this will be a Government grounded in fiscal responsibility” and pointed to Britain's “fastest G7 growth,” in a session the magazine described as “an easy ride” in which Badenoch pressed him on what he had actually cut from government.

headline: Bank and BP profits fuel windfall-tax speculation as recess ends
body: With Parliament back in session, pressure is building on Burnham to tax bank and energy profits rather than break Labour's 2024 pledge against raising income tax, VAT or national insurance, per The National (Sep 2). The UK's four largest banks posted £29.2 billion in pre-tax profits in H1 2026 — up 21% year-on-year — while BP's Q2 profit more than doubled to £4.27 billion, even as the government must release thousands of prisoners in October to ease overcrowding.

headline: Qatar condemns renewed Iranian attacks on Kuwait
body: Qatar's Foreign Ministry “strongly condemns the renewed attacks by the Islamic Republic of Iran against the State of Kuwait, considering them a flagrant violation of its sovereignty and territorial integrity,” per The Peninsula Qatar (Sep 3). Doha warned the strikes represent “a dangerous escalation that would complicate efforts to contain tensions and undermine political and diplomatic efforts aimed at achieving security and stability in the region.”

headline: Kuwait's air defences intercept Iranian missiles and drones
body: Kuwait's military said its air-defence systems intercepted hostile Iranian missile and drone attacks in the early hours of Thursday, with the General Staff clarifying “any explosions heard were the result of air defence systems intercepting the hostile attacks,” per The Peninsula Qatar (Sep 3). Residents were urged to “adhere to the safety and security instructions issued by the relevant authorities” as the strikes came just after Saudi Arabia's own tanker in the Strait of Hormuz was hit.

headline: Qatar rejects use of Hormuz as ‘negotiating tool’ after tanker attack
body: Following Iran's strike on the Saudi-flagged Sidr tanker that killed two Filipino crew members, Qatar's foreign ministry called the incident “a flagrant violation of the rules of international law and freedom of maritime navigation” and rejected using the strait as a bargaining chip, per Al Jazeera (Sep 2). Saudi Arabia's foreign ministry separately “stressed the necessity of halting escalations, and respecting international maritime safety and the security of global energy supplies.”

headline: Doha Trade Fair enters final days at DECC
body: The shopping showcase of fashion, perfumes, accessories and homeware from local and international vendors runs through September 5 at the Doha Exhibition and Convention Center, open 10am-10pm daily (3pm-10pm on Friday), per The Peninsula Qatar (Sep 2).

headline: Qatar Philharmonic opens season with Dvořák's ‘New World’
body: Conductor Elias Grandy leads the Qatar Philharmonic Orchestra on September 6 at QNCC's Auditorium 3, with pianist Joseph Moog performing Brahms' Piano Concerto No. 2 before the orchestra closes with Dvořák's Symphony No. 9 “From the New World.” Doors open 7:15pm, with tickets starting from QAR 200.

headline: ‘Uzbekistan: Heritage in Motion’ opens at the Museum of Islamic Art
body: Qatar Museums' new exhibition, running through November 28, features 146 objects drawn from MIA, other Qatari collections and 13 Uzbek institutions spanning over 1,000 years of Central Asian artistic tradition, per The Peninsula Qatar (Sep 3). MIA director Shaika Al-Nassr said “we don’t just display history, we get to share the heartbeat of a civilization with the world,” while Uzbek foundation chair Gayane Umerova called the collaboration “craft, heritage, restoration, cultural exchange.”

headline: John Legend brings ‘Songs and Stories’ to QNCC
body: The 13-time Grammy winner performs stripped-down arrangements of his best-known songs on September 10 at QNCC's Conference Hall 3 & 4, doors at 7pm and show starting 9pm, presented by Visit Qatar with tickets from QAR 195.

headline: Saleh El Nawawy's ‘Ghaibooba’ stand-up returns to Souq Waqif
body: The comedian's two-night stand-up special runs September 10-11 at the Abdulaziz Nasser Theater, with early and late shows offering “fresh stories, sharp observations and nonstop laughs” for ages 16+, tickets from QAR 195.

headline: Tesla launched its Cybercab robotaxi service in Austin — no steering wheel, no pedals — marking the company’s entry into commercial autonomous ride-hailing.

The US-Iran war escalated further: VP Vance says Iran’s grip on the Strait of Hormuz is “effectively gone” and rules out talks until ship attacks stop, while Iran’s Red Crescent seeks an ICC probe into a deadly wedding strike.
Brent crude topped $97 and gold rebounded 3% to $4,544/oz as traders whipsawed between Fed Governor Waller’s dovish CPI-linked hint and today’s make-or-break August jobs report.
DRC’s Ebola outbreak has killed nearly 3,000 as Nepal’s flood toll passes 1,100 and Cyprus’s ferry death toll climbs to 10 with 18 still missing.
India’s GDP-revision row intensified as Congress cited a ₹43 lakh crore base-year change, while F1 heads to Monza with points leader Kimi Antonelli starting from the back after a grid penalty.
DRC Ebola Death Toll Tops 3,000 as WHO Warns of Hidden Transmission Chains
body: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has killed more than 3,000 people, per Al Jazeera (Sep 2), with WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus warning the CDC found up to 80% of new cases have no known contact history — “that means there are chains of transmission we don’t know about.” As of Aug 31 case counts stood at 6,041 confirmed infections and 2,911 deaths across 60 affected areas, per Al Jazeera; Tedros said “we can control this epidemic if we choose to,” but cited a global response funding gap exceeding $1 billion.

headline: Nepal-Tibet Flood Death Toll Passes 1,100 as Nepal Shifts to Rehabilitation
body: Nepal’s flood death toll climbed to 1,114 — up from 1,003 a day earlier — with 3,916 still missing and roughly 75 Americans unaccounted for, per ABC News (Sep 2). Prime Minister Balendra Shah said the country is “moving forward from search, rescue and relief distribution to rehabilitation,” as officials confirmed at least 48 suspension bridges were damaged, 28 needing full replacement, and allocated 1 billion Nepali rupees (~$6.5 million) toward rebuilding.

headline: Ferry Disaster Off Cyprus: 8 Dead, 20 Missing as Submersible Joins Search
body: The passenger ferry Filo Jet, carrying 267 people from Kyrenia to Tasucu, Turkey, capsized and sank in waters over 500 meters deep off Cyprus on Aug 30; eight are confirmed dead and 20 remain missing after two days, per News4JAX (Sep 1). A Turkish navy vessel with a submersible capable of diving 1,000 meters joined 15 divers, seven helicopters and 17 boats in the search, while eight crew members and a ferry company director were taken into custody as North Cyprus PM Ünal Üstel pledged “we will continue our search and rescue operations.”

headline: Philippine Weather Death Toll Rises to 39 as Tropical Storm Pilandok Exits
body: Tropical Storm Pilandok was set to exit the Philippine area of responsibility early Sep 3 while southwest monsoon rains kept lashing Ilocos, Zambales and Bataan, per Philstar (Sep 3). The nationwide weather death toll since Aug 1 climbed to 39 after five new deaths on Sep 2 — including landslide victims in Zambales and flood deaths in Pampanga’s Porac — with Benguet alone recording 15 fatalities.

headline: Novak Djokovic Suffers Shock US Open Exit Amid On-Court Illness Collapse
body: World No. 4 seed Novak Djokovic was stunned by Argentina’s Mariano Navone 7-6(5), 5-7, 4-6, 6-2, 6-1 in a 4-hour, 36-minute first-round marathon — the longest opening-round Grand Slam match of his career — after repeated vomiting and cramping on court. “Vomiting, throwing up, a serious issue there. Then my whole body started to collapse, basically cramping and pain,” Djokovic said, per Sky Sports (Aug 31). He added: “I pretty much despised every moment that I spent on the court for that.”

headline: Liam Lawson to Deputize for Injured Hadjar at Italian Grand Prix
body: Red Bull confirmed Liam Lawson will again partner Max Verstappen at Monza after Isack Hadjar’s wrist injury, sustained over the summer break, ruled him out for a second straight race. Lawson impressed as a Zandvoort stand-in, qualifying eighth and finishing seventh for his first points with the team. “Liam will drive alongside Max at the Italian Grand Prix in Monza, while Isack continues to make encouraging progress following the wrist injury sustained during the summer break,” Red Bull said, per PlanetF1 (Sep 2).

headline: Tilak Varma’s South Zone Power Into Duleep Trophy Final
body: South Zone beat North Zone by seven wickets in Bengaluru to reach the Duleep Trophy final, chasing a 181-run target as captain Tilak Varma finished unbeaten on a half-century in an 80-run stand with Smaran Ravichandran. Seamer MD Nidheesh set up the win with a five-wicket haul in North Zone’s second innings, dismissing Gurnoor Brar and Arshdeep Singh among others. Per The Tribune (Sep 2), South Zone now face East Zone in the summit clash at MA Chidambaram Stadium, Chennai, from September 6.

headline: Ballon d’Or 2026 Nominee Reveal Date Set for September 8
body: France Football confirmed the 30-man and 30-woman nominee lists for the 2026 Ballon d’Or will be unveiled on September 8, with the 70th-anniversary ceremony set for October 26 in London. Defending champions Ousmane Dembélé and Aitana Bonmatí headline a vote cast by journalists from the top 100 (men’s) and top 50 (women’s) FIFA-ranked nations. Per beIN Sports (Sep 1), shortlists for the young player, goalkeeper, coach and top-scorer awards will be released alongside the main prize.

headline: Oil Surges Past $95 as Iran Conflict Escalates, Hormuz Traffic Collapses
body: Brent crude jumped to $95.47 a barrel and WTI to $90.72 on Sep 2 — the sharpest one-day gains in a month — after President Trump ordered what he called “large and powerful” strikes on Iranian targets near the Strait of Hormuz, with Iran vowing retaliation and Kuwait, Jordan and Bahrain intercepting missiles Wednesday morning. Vessel crossings through the strait have collapsed from 23 a week ago to just five on Tuesday, per The National (Sep 2). “Renewed hostilities in the Middle East sent crude prices surging, driving Wall Street lower and global bond yields to multi-year — and in some instances, multidecade — highs,” said Kyle Rodda, senior analyst at Capital.com.

headline: Fed Rate-Hike Bets Surge to 66% After Warsh’s Hawkish Jackson Hole Speech
body: Futures markets are now pricing a 66–67% probability the Federal Reserve raises rates a quarter point at its September 16 meeting — a sharp reversal from earlier bets on no 2026 hikes — after Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said underlying inflation has “not ‘meaningfully improved,’” signaling the Fed has “work to do,” per Marketplace (Aug 31). The shift has driven the 10-year Treasury yield to 4.81%, a near three-year high, with BNY Mellon strategists citing “fiscal concerns and doubts about the Federal Reserve’s credibility” as drivers, per FXStreet (Sep 2).

headline: US Private Payrolls Miss Big, Manufacturing Posts Worst Drop in a Year
body: ADP data released Sep 2 showed private employers added just 38,000 jobs in August, well below the 47,000 forecast, with manufacturing shedding 17,000 positions — its steepest monthly drop in a year — and professional/business services down nearly 500,000 since ChatGPT’s launch. “Pay can tell us a lot about today’s choppy hiring,” said ADP chief economist Dr. Nela Richardson, as job-changers’ wage growth held at 4.7% even while headline hiring cooled to a three-month average of 60,000, the slowest since March.

headline: Broadcom’s AI Chip Revenue Triples to $16.7 Billion
body: Broadcom reported fiscal Q3 revenue of $29.6 billion, up 86% year-over-year, with AI semiconductor revenue surging 221% to $16.7 billion, and guided Q4 revenue to roughly $34.8 billion, per StockTitan (Sep 2). “Demand for our custom AI accelerators and networking continues to be very strong. Q3 AI semiconductor revenue of $16.7 billion grew 221% year-over-year, and 54% quarter-over-quarter,” said CEO Hock Tan.

headline: Gold Retreats From Record Highs as Hawkish Fed Bets Firm Up
body: Gold slipped to about $4,287 an ounce on Sep 2, pulling back after touching $4,334 the day before and rallying more than 25% since the start of 2025, as surging Treasury yields and firming Fed rate-hike odds curbed demand for the non-yielding metal, per FXStreet (Sep 2) and Fortune (Sep 2). The CME FedWatch tool put the odds of a September 16 hike at 67%, with BNY Mellon strategists pointing to “fiscal concerns and doubts about the Federal Reserve’s credibility” behind the broader bond selloff weighing on bullion.

headline: Trump Administration Sides With OpenAI in New York Times Copyright Case
body: The Trump administration filed a statement of interest backing OpenAI and Microsoft in The New York Times’s copyright lawsuit, arguing that training AI models on copyrighted material is protected fair use, per TheWrap (Sep 2). The Times sued in 2023 alleging millions of its articles were used without permission; OpenAI said it will keep defending “the long-standing principles of fair use,” a fight that has since widened to include a June 2026 suit from 400 news publishers against OpenAI and Microsoft.

headline: Google, Anthropic and OpenAI Race to Deploy Cyber-Defense AI Models
body: Google, Anthropic and OpenAI each rolled out cybersecurity-focused AI systems this week: Google launched Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber via its Fairwind Program, giving 650-plus partners including CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Networks early access, while Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 with new “Enterprise Frontier Safeguards,” and OpenAI said its Astra model has crossed the “critical cybersecurity capability threshold” ahead of a gated rollout via its Daybreak Blue program, per The Hacker News (Sep 2). Google said the Fairwind Program gives “high-priority defenders (like governments, healthcare providers, and telecommunications services) early access to advanced models.”

headline: OpenAI Plugs ChatGPT Health Into Epic’s Hospital Records System
body: OpenAI integrated ChatGPT Health with Epic’s electronic health record system, which covers more than 325 million patients, giving clinicians read-only access to lab results, medications and specialist notes without leaving the patient chart, per TechCrunch (Sep 1). OpenAI said a survey of 4,300 physicians across 27 clinical use cases found 99.1% of responses were rated safe, and that ChatGPT now fields roughly 300 million health-related queries every week.

headline: Meta’s $18B Teen-Safety Settlement Clears Runway for New AI Push
body: Meta agreed to pay up to $18 billion over ten years to settle a suit from 29 state attorneys general over Instagram and Facebook features harmful to minors, accepting a two-hour daily use cap for under-18s and tighter age verification, per CNBC (Sep 2). Morgan Stanley analysts said the deal clears the way for “multiple new products” in Meta’s pipeline — including the consumer AI agent “Hatch” expected in early September — even as Needham analysts warned that “management attention, engineering talent and shareholder capital are spread across too many things.”

headline: Intel’s Chip-Packaging Tech Draws Google, Meta as TSMC Bottleneck Bites
body: Intel’s EMIB-T advanced packaging — which uses embedded silicon bridges instead of a full interposer to link compute dies with HBM memory — is drawing evaluation from Google, MediaTek and Meta as an alternative to TSMC’s bottlenecked CoWoS packaging, per SammyFans (Sep 1). The tech supports packages up to 120x120mm across more than nine reticles, with Intel targeting a significant production ramp in the second half of 2027.

headline: US Strikes Kill 18 in Iran as Tehran Retaliates Across Jordan, Kuwait and Bahrain
body: The death toll from U.S. strikes on Iran — including one that hit a wedding in Hormozgan province — has risen to 18, among them two children, Iran’s health minister said, per Al Jazeera (Sep 3). Tehran retaliated with missiles and drones against U.S.-linked targets in Jordan, Kuwait, Bahrain and Iraqi Kurdistan; Jordan’s military said it intercepted 10 of 13 incoming missiles, with the rest landing in unpopulated areas. President Trump warned Iran would be “hit again at a much harder level” if it retaliated further, while Iranian President Pezeshkian said Tehran would “immediately reciprocate” if Washington returned to June’s ceasefire terms.

headline: Iran Strikes Saudi Tanker in Hormuz, Drawing Gulf Condemnation as Tehran Vows ‘New Strategy’
body: Iran attacked a Saudi-flagged tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, killing two crew members, prompting Saudi Arabia, Qatar and the UAE to jointly condemn the strike, per Al Jazeera (Sep 2). President Trump said the renewed fighting would not last “too long” but that the U.S. remained ready to strike “at any time,” while Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei warned Washington would soon see Tehran’s “new strategy” for the war, per Al Jazeera (Sep 3).

headline: SCO Adopts Bishkek Declaration as Summit Ends, Modi Pitches Dialogue Over Battlefield
body: The 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit closed in Bishkek with the historic 25th-anniversary Bishkek Declaration, adopting English as an official SCO language and creating a new Universal Centre for Countering Security Threats among 13 outcome agreements, per The Tribune (Sep 1). Prime Minister Modi told the summit “conflicts cannot be resolved on the battlefield” and announced India will host the SCO’s first Civilisation Dialogue Forum later this year.

headline: Kremlin Floats Putin-Xi-Trump Trilateral Meeting at APEC Summit
body: Speaking from Bishkek after the SCO summit, Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said a possible three-way meeting between Presidents Putin, Xi and Trump had been discussed and could take place on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, per GV Wire (Sep 1). “This issue was discussed, yes,” Ushakov said, adding that if all three leaders attend APEC, “then the three of them will be able to have a meeting”; the White House did not immediately comment.

headline: Nvidia Rallies on Report of Hugging Face Acquisition Talks and Strong AI Demand Signals
body: Bloomberg reported Nvidia is in advanced talks to acquire open-source AI platform Hugging Face, a move that would extend the chipmaker's reach beyond hardware into software and model distribution, per Investing.com (Sep 2). Sentiment was further lifted by Dell's blowout fiscal second-quarter results, which pointed to continued strength in AI infrastructure spending, while Robert W. Baird reaffirmed Nvidia as a top large-cap pick citing its compute leadership and growing share of the inference market.

headline: Oracle Gains on New Quantinuum Quantum-Computing Partnership
body: Oracle advanced after unveiling a multi-year strategic partnership with Quantinuum to bring quantum computing capabilities to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, positioning the company at the intersection of quantum, AI and high-performance cloud computing, per Investing.com (Sep 2). Bernstein SocGen maintained its Outperform rating, arguing Oracle remains early in a major cloud infrastructure investment cycle.

headline: PayPal Rebounds as Failed Stripe Takeover Bid Resets Valuation, RBC Stays Bullish
body: PayPal shares recovered ground after the collapse of a reported takeover approach from Stripe and Advent left the stock trading at a valuation many investors saw as overly discounted, per Investing.com (Sep 2). RBC Capital reiterated its Buy rating, and income-focused buyers were also drawn in ahead of the company's upcoming quarterly dividend record date.

headline: Palantir Pulls Back as Investors Book Profits Amid Rising Treasury Yields
body: Palantir shares fell as investors took profits following the stock's substantial run this year, with the pullback driven more by valuation concerns than any company-specific setback, according to the Motley Fool (Sep 2). Rising Treasury yields added broader pressure on high-multiple growth and AI names that session.

headline: CrowdStrike Slides With Software Peers as Treasury Yields Climb
body: CrowdStrike fell alongside other high-multiple software names as climbing Treasury yields and inflation concerns tied to rising oil prices pushed institutional investors to lock in gains after a strong year-to-date run, per TradingKey (Sep 2). The move was part of a broader rotation out of richly valued growth software rather than any company-specific news.

headline: Cloudflare Slips as Macro Pressures and Convertible-Note Overhang Weigh on Growth Stocks
body: Cloudflare declined amid the same sector-wide selling pressuring other high-growth software names, as escalating tension in global energy markets pushed crude prices higher and stoked inflation concerns, lifting yields and compressing valuations for richly priced growth stocks, per TradingKey (Sep 2). The stock also remains under an overhang from its recent convertible senior notes offering, which some investors continue to view as a dilutive capital raise against an already elevated valuation.

headline: fuboTV Jumps With No Clear Catalyst as Investors Revisit Combined Disney-Hulu Live TV Entity
body: fuboTV shares jumped despite the absence of any same-day filing, earnings release, or corporate announcement, according to Yahoo Finance/24/7 Wall St. (Sep 2). The move appears to reflect investors reassessing the combined Fubo-Hulu Live TV streaming entity, which the outlet argues trades well below what its scale might otherwise suggest, though it found no specific news event behind the day's gain.

headline: India Slams ‘Alarming Apathy’ Over Century-Old Temple’s Demolition in Pakistan
body: New Delhi demanded a probe and restoration after a century-old Hindu temple in Siraj village, Narowal district, was demolished in Pakistan on August 21, per WION (Sep 2). MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal called it a “reprehensible act of vandalism” and said “the apparent apathy of authorities and failure to protect this century-old temple is alarming,” noting only 37 of Pakistan’s 1,817 Hindu temples and Sikh gurdwaras remain operational.

headline: Modi Tells SCO Summit to ‘Dismantle the Entire Ecosystem of Terrorism’
body: Addressing the 26th SCO Summit in Bishkek on its 25th anniversary, PM Modi said, “We must dismantle the entire ecosystem of terrorism, its financing, recruitment, radicalisation and safe havens,” adding “there can be no place for double standards on terrorism,” per WION (Sep 1). On the sidelines, Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping shared a handshake and brief conversation as New Delhi and Beijing pursue a cautious reset after the 2020 Ladakh border clashes, also per WION (Sep 1).

headline: Congress Blasts Modi Government’s 7.8% GDP Print as ‘Statistical Gymnastics’
body: A day after India posted 7.8% GDP growth for April–June, Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh accused the government of manipulating the numbers, per WION (Sep 1): “Yesterday’s GDP numbers are simply statistical gymnastics. By changing the methodology repeatedly, the Modi government is fixing GDP data while hiding India’s bleak economic reality.” Ramesh said the deflator methodology has been revised twice this year and dismissed Make in India as “the fake in India,” while Modi had called the figure “exemplary” and urged a swadeshi push, per WION (Sep 1).

headline: Ousted PM Keir Starmer to Quit Parliament After 11 Years
body: Keir Starmer announced he will step down as MP for Holborn and St Pancras, six weeks after being ousted as Labour leader and prime minister, triggering a by-election, per Al Jazeera (Sep 1). Explaining the move, Starmer said, “It is now time to step aside and focus on other issues: international affairs including defence, security, trade and technology,” closing out a premiership that began with a 2024 landslide but was undercut by U-turns and a Reform UK surge.

headline: Burnham’s Autumn Honeymoon Ends as Bank and BP Profits Fuel Windfall-Tax Talk
body: As Parliament returns, PM Andy Burnham’s early goodwill is giving way to scrutiny over prison overcrowding, a 3.5%-of-GDP defence pledge, and Starmer-era borrowing rules that box in his options, per The National (Sep 2). With the UK’s four biggest banks posting £29.2 billion in first-half pre-tax profits (up 21%) and BP’s Q2 profit doubling to £4.27 billion, Westminster is buzzing about a windfall tax as a way to raise revenue without breaking Labour’s pledge against hiking income tax, VAT or national insurance.

headline: UK Energy Price Cap to Rise 4% as Iran War Pushes Up Gas Costs
body: Ofgem confirmed a 4% rise to the energy price cap from October 1, adding roughly £60 a year for a typical household, as wholesale gas prices jumped 11% over three months amid the US-Israel war on Iran, per Al Jazeera (Sep 1). Ofgem director general Neil Kenward said “high international gas prices are continuing to drive energy costs in the UK,” while Cambridge researcher Jack Burt warned consumers are paying a “risk premium” for supply.

headline: Qatar Cabinet Condemns Iran’s Renewed Strikes on Jordan, UAE, Bahrain and Kuwait
body: Qatar’s Cabinet condemned “in the strongest terms” Iran’s renewed attacks on Jordan, the UAE, Bahrain and Kuwait, per The Peninsula Qatar (Sep 2). Spokesperson HE Ibrahim bin Ali Al Mohannadi called the strikes “a flagrant violation of the sovereignty and territorial integrity” of the targeted states and urged dialogue over escalation; the same session also approved a draft cloud-computing law.

headline: Qatar Condemns Iranian Strike on Saudi Tanker SIDR in Strait of Hormuz
body: Qatar’s Foreign Ministry “strongly condemned” Iran’s targeting of the Saudi-flagged tanker SIDR while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, an attack that killed crew members and violated UN Security Council Resolution 2817, per The Peninsula Qatar (Sep 2). The ministry said “freedom of navigation through this vital waterway is an established principle that is non-negotiable” and reaffirmed solidarity with Saudi Arabia.

headline: Kuwait Contains Blaze After Iranian Drone Strikes Residential Complex
body: Kuwaiti firefighters brought a blaze under control at a residential complex in the capital after an Iranian drone strike early Wednesday, per The Peninsula Qatar (Sep 2). Fire Force spokesman Brig. Gen. Mohammad Al Ghareeb said crews “responded to the scene early Wednesday and brought the fire under control”; no injuries were reported, only material damage, as Kuwait joined Bahrain and the UAE among Gulf states hit in the same wave of Iranian strikes.

headline: Doha Trade Fair
body: This shopping showcase runs through September 5 at the Doha Exhibition & Convention Center (Halls 4 & 5), 10am–10pm daily (3pm–10pm on Fridays), with local and international vendors selling fashion, accessories, perfumes and homeware. It runs alongside the 15th Arabian Women Exhibition at the same venue, which features over 200 regional and international designers and lifestyle brands — per The Peninsula Qatar.

headline: QPO Presents: Dvořák’s From the New World
body: The Qatar Philharmonic Orchestra, led by conductor Elias Grandy, performs on September 6 at QNCC’s Auditorium 3 (doors 7:15pm, start 7:30pm). Pianist Joseph Moog joins for Brahms’ Piano Concerto No. 2 before the orchestra closes with Dvořák’s Symphony No. 9; tickets start from QAR 200.

headline: Saleh El Nawawy: Stand-Up Comedy
body: Egyptian comedian Saleh El Nawawy brings his special “Ghaibooba” to the Abdulaziz Nasser Theatre in Souq Waqif for early and late shows on September 10–11. Tickets start from QAR 195, and the show carries a 16+ age limit.

headline: QPO Presents: Tchaikovsky’s Piano Concerto No. 1
body: On September 14 at QNCC’s Auditorium 3 (doors 7:15pm), conductor Enrique Diemecke leads the Qatar Philharmonic Orchestra with pianist Jae Hong Park — winner of the 2021 Busoni International Piano Competition — performing Tchaikovsky’s famed concerto, followed by his symphonic work Manfred. Tickets run QAR 200–275.

headline: US strikes on Iran have killed 18 people, including at a wedding, as Tehran retaliates with missiles and drones on Jordan, Kuwait, Bahrain and a Saudi tanker in the Strait of Hormuz.
Oil has surged past $95 a barrel and Fed rate-hike odds have jumped to 66–67% after Chair Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole remarks — a sharp reversal from earlier no-hike bets.
Novak Djokovic was stunned in the US Open's first round after repeated on-court vomiting and cramping in a 4h36m marathon loss to world No. 87 Mariano Navone.
The DRC's Ebola outbreak has killed over 3,000 people as WHO warns up to 80% of new cases show no known contact history, and Nepal's flood toll has passed 1,100.
Ousted UK PM Keir Starmer is quitting Parliament entirely, while the Trump administration has formally backed OpenAI's fair-use defense against The New York Times.
Nepal-Tibet Flood Toll Passes 900 as Hydropower Workers Remain Trapped
body: A glacier collapse on the Nepal-Tibet border last Wednesday has triggered flooding that has now killed at least 903 people in Nepal and 16 in Tibet, with more than 4,700 people still missing between the two. Roughly 900 workers remain trapped in about a dozen hydropower-project tunnels blocked by mud and rock, and a Nepali army spokesperson said clearing the debris “is posing us a big challenge.” China has sent 2,100 rescuers and $33 million in aid, per Al Jazeera (Aug 31).

headline: DRC Ebola Outbreak Becomes the Country's Deadliest on Record
body: Confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo have topped 6,000 with 2,911 deaths across six provinces, making this the deadliest outbreak in the country's history, per Africanews (Aug 31). The Bundibugyo strain driving it has no approved vaccine or treatment; international agencies have launched a $518 million response plan, though insecurity and community mistrust have slowed contact tracing, now at 82.4% completion.

headline: Philippine Storm Toll Climbs to 33 Dead, 8.8 Million Affected
body: Three tropical cyclones — Luis, Maymay and Neneng — combined with an enhanced southwest monsoon have killed 33 people and affected 8.8 million people across the Philippines, with roughly 2.5 million families displaced and ₱6.12 billion in infrastructure damage, per Philstar (Aug 31). More than 164,500 people remain in evacuation centers, and three people are still listed as missing.

headline: Spain's Sánchez Accuses Russia, Israel of Ceuta Crisis Disinformation
body: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said Russia- and Israel-linked networks spread and amplified disinformation about July's migrant crisis in Ceuta, when roughly 70,000 people crossed from Morocco into the Spanish enclave within days. Citing research from the EU's External Action Service, Sánchez said the aim was to “divide” Europe over Spain's positions on Ukraine and the Middle East, and added that no intelligence points to Moroccan authorities orchestrating the surge, per Al Jazeera (Aug 31).

headline: Lionel Messi Retires From International Football After World Cup Final Loss
body: Lionel Messi announced his retirement from international football hours after Argentina lost the World Cup final 1-0 to Spain. “It was a decision that hurt — and still hurts deep down — but I understand that the time has come,” he said, closing a 207-cap, 125-goal career that included the 2022 World Cup title, two Copá América wins and eight Ballon d'Ors, per Al Jazeera (Aug 31).

headline: Liverpool Pay $162m for Barcola as Premier League Deadline Day Delivers
body: Liverpool signed France winger Bradley Barcola from PSG for around $162 million, the Premier League's most expensive deal of the window, while Chelsea paid £117 million for Aston Villa's Morgan Rogers and Manchester City £116 million for Nottingham Forest's Elliot Anderson. Real Madrid also completed a €140 million move for Ivorian winger Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig, per Al Jazeera (Aug 31).

headline: Champions League Draw Sets Up Arsenal-Real Madrid, Barcelona-PSG
body: UEFA's 36-team Champions League league-phase draw has set up Arsenal against Real Madrid and Barcelona against PSG among the marquee fixtures, with the competition kicking off September 8. Defending champion PSG is chasing a third straight title, and the final is set for Madrid's Metropolitano Stadium on June 5, 2027, per The Sporting News (Aug 27).

headline: Oil Jumps Above $90 as US-Iran Strikes Revive Hormuz Risk
body: Brent crude rose 2.24% to $90.07 a barrel and WTI gained 1.94% to $85.02 after the US struck Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island and Iran hit back at US bases in Jordan, reviving fears over the Strait of Hormuz. Kharg Island, which handles roughly 90% of Iran's oil exports, was also reportedly targeted, and analysts expect further US secondary sanctions on Iran's trading partners, per The National (Aug 31).

headline: Wall Street Closes Out August With a Dip as Oil Surges
body: The Dow fell 0.70% to 53,186 and the S&P 500 lost 0.33% to 7,686 on Monday as oil's jump above $90 revived inflation worries, though the Nasdaq slipped a smaller 0.12%. The S&P still closed August up 2.6% on the month, gold slipped 0.64% to $4,466, and the 10-year Treasury yield rose to 4.76%, per The Motley Fool (Aug 31).

headline: Hong Kong, Shanghai IPO Proceeds Top $54bn on AI and Robotics Boom
body: Hong Kong and Shanghai IPO proceeds have topped $54 billion so far in 2026, driven by a wave of AI, robotics and semiconductor listings. Memory chipmaker CXMT alone raised $8.6 billion, while humanoid-robot maker Unitree has seen sharp share-price volatility since its debut, per Tech Startups' daily roundup (Aug 31).

headline: Tim Cook Steps Down as Apple CEO After 15 Years, Ternus Takes Over
body: Tim Cook's 15-year run as Apple CEO ended Monday, with hardware-engineering chief John Ternus taking over September 1 while Cook moves to executive chairman focused on government and China relations. Cook said he “can't imagine it any other way” than staying closely involved, and Ternus will lead Apple's September 9 product event as the company faces investor pressure to sharpen its AI strategy, per 9to5Mac (Aug 31).

headline: Financial Stability Board Warns AI Is the Top Near-Term Cyber Risk
body: Financial Stability Board chair Andrew Bailey told G20 finance ministers and central bank governors that frontier AI models pose the most immediate threat to global financial stability. “Frontier AI models could alter the speed, scale, and economics of cyberattacks on financial systems,” he said, per Quartz (Aug 31).

headline: EU Puts ChatGPT, Reddit and Roblox Under Strictest Platform Rules
body: The European Commission designated Reddit and Roblox as Very Large Online Platforms and ChatGPT as a Very Large Online Search Engine, requiring annual systemic-risk assessments, independent audits and data-sharing with regulators by the end of November. “These new designations mean that ChatGPT, Reddit and Roblox will now be held to a higher standard of scrutiny and accountability in the European Union,” said Henna Virkkunen, the EU's tech sovereignty chief, per Euronews (Aug 31).

headline: Rhysida Hackers Steal 5.8TB From Berlin Government, Demand 30 Bitcoin
body: The Rhysida ransomware group breached Berlin's government network in early August, stealing 5.79 terabytes of data including 46,500 contracts, emails and passwords, and is auctioning it on the dark web with a 30-bitcoin (about $2.3 million) starting price. Governing Mayor Kai Wegner rejected the demand, saying “the state of Berlin is being blackmailed” but will not pay, per The Record (Aug 31).

headline: US Strikes Iran's Larak Island; Iran Hits Bases in Jordan, UAE
body: The US struck two Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island on Sunday to head off Iran's threatened mining of the Strait of Hormuz, reigniting fighting after roughly a month of relative calm. Iran responded within hours with missile strikes on US bases in Jordan and a UAE facility; Trump warned “it doesn't mean we won't smack them to see what happens,” per Al Jazeera (Aug 31).

headline: Trump Rules Out Nuking Iran, Weighs Limited Hormuz Strikes
body: Asked whether he had ruled out a nuclear strike on Iran, Trump called the question “stupid,” saying Iran is “totally defeated militarily” and there is no reason for one. He is weighing a Pentagon-backed plan for limited strikes in the Strait of Hormuz to stop Iran rebuilding military capacity there, while Iran separately sentenced two women to death over January's anti-government protests, per The Times of Israel (Aug 31).

headline: Xi, Putin, Modi Gather in Bishkek for SCO's 25th-Anniversary Summit
body: Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin, Narendra Modi and Iran's Masoud Pezeshkian are among the leaders gathered in Bishkek for the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation's 25th-anniversary summit, with the US-Israel war on Iran, the Russia-Ukraine war and Afghanistan's crisis all on the agenda alongside plans for an SCO Development Bank and new trade corridors. Pezeshkian directly asked Modi to use India's influence to help end the West Asia war, per Al Jazeera (Aug 31).

headline: Ukraine Opens Criminal Probe Into Deadly Kyiv-Area Arms Depot Strike
body: Ukraine has opened a criminal investigation into last week's Russian drone strike on a munitions warehouse near Kyiv that killed at least 37 people and damaged more than 50 homes, the war's deadliest single day. President Zelenskyy said prosecutors are examining whether the depot's operators broke rules on storing ammunition near residential areas, calling repeated safety lapses “criminal negligence,” per Al Jazeera (Aug 29).

headline: Tesla Rallies Ahead of September 3 Cybercab Event
body: Tesla shares rallied ahead of the company's invite-only September 3 event in Austin previewing its steering-wheel- and pedal-free Cybercab, with investors also pointing to this month's Nevada approval for a limited robotaxi rollout under Tesla's full self-driving system. Rival EV makers Rivian and Lucid posted only modest moves by comparison, per The Motley Fool (Aug 31).

headline: CrowdStrike Unveils AI Workflow Tool Falcon IQ at Fal.Con 2026
body: CrowdStrike shares rose after the company unveiled Falcon IQ, an AI-powered automated security workflow tool, at its Fal.Con 2026 conference, alongside new partnerships with CLEAR on identity verification and an expanded Cognizant tie-up on operational-technology security. Analysts called the announcements meaningful but not transformative, per StockStory (Aug 31).

headline: Amazon Shares Slip as FTC Prepares Ad-Pricing Lawsuit
body: Amazon fell after reports that the FTC plans to sue over allegations it secretly used a “soft reserve” tool starting in 2018 to push up the minimum price merchants had to pay for ads, inflating auction prices in an estimated 70-80% of cases and generating tens of billions of dollars over roughly seven years. More than 20 state attorneys general are expected to join what would be the FTC's third major action against the company, per Benzinga (Aug 31).

headline: Uber Slides on Delivery Hero Deal Risk and Regulatory Overhang
body: Uber shares fell as investors weighed integration and regulatory risk from its takeover offer for Delivery Hero alongside soft Q3 guidance and a roughly 500 basis-point year-over-year drop in mobility margins. The stock is also still digesting an €825 million Dutch regulatory fine over automated driver-account deactivations from earlier in August, per TradingKey (Aug 31).

headline: HDFC Bank CEO Jagdishan to Step Down in October
body: HDFC Bank CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan will not seek another term when it expires in October, ending a run that began in 2020, and the board must now weigh an internal successor against an external hire for “a sharper reset.” Macquarie's Suresh Ganapathy said the bank is “in a tough spot” and will need to address employee morale alongside the leadership change, per Bloomberg and Business Standard (Aug 31).

headline: Figma Shares Extend Their Slide With No Fresh Catalyst
body: Figma shares fell again with no company-specific news to explain the move, extending a soft stretch that has now run for a second straight session. It's a case where the honest read is that the drift is valuation-driven rather than event-driven.

headline: India Rejects Hague Tribunal's Indus Waters Ruling as “Illegal”
body: A Hague Court of Arbitration ruled India must keep complying with the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty and ordered limits on India's Ratle hydropower project until July 2027, but India's foreign ministry dismissed the tribunal as “illegally constituted” with “no jurisdiction whatsoever.” India suspended the treaty after the 2025 Pahalgam terror attack, which it blames on Pakistan-backed militants, per WION (Aug 31).

headline: India's GDP Grows 7.8% in First Quarter, Beating Estimates
body: India's GDP grew 7.8% in the April-June quarter, beating the RBI's 7% estimate and last year's 6.9% pace, driven by domestic demand, manufacturing, construction and government capital spending. “India's exemplary GDP growth of 7.8%... is a herculean feat,” Modi said, while Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman credited “the people of India and their hard work,” per WION (Aug 31).

headline: Modi Tells Putin “Every Day Spent in War Sets Humanity Back”
body: PM Modi met Putin on the sidelines of the SCO summit in Bishkek, their first in-person meeting since Putin's December 2025 state visit to India, and invited him to India's upcoming BRICS summit. “Every day spent in war sets humanity back,” Modi said, calling for movement “away from endless war towards an end to the war” and invoking Gandhi and Buddha's shared message of peace, per WION (Aug 31).

headline: Burnham Faces Tough Autumn as Parliament Returns From Recess
body: PM Andy Burnham addresses Parliament as MPs return from summer recess facing a defence-spending gap, prison overcrowding and welfare reform, with Labour, Reform UK and the Conservatives now bunched within three points of each other in the polls. Burnham's personal approval sits at +12, but commentators note his “summer of love” popularity has yet to be tested by a hard budget choice, per Bloomberg and Inkl (Aug 31).

headline: Assisted Dying Bill Returns to the Commons on September 11
body: The Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill, which passed the Commons but stalled in the Lords, is being revived by MP Lauren Edwards through the Private Members' Bill ballot and returns to the Commons on September 11. It's one of six major items — alongside October's Budget and a November “Ten-Year Plan” — that will define Burnham's first full autumn as PM, per LabourList (Aug 28).

headline: Qatar's Non-Hydrocarbon GDP Grows 3.5% as Overall Economy Contracts
body: Qatar's non-hydrocarbon GDP grew 3.5% year-on-year in the first quarter of 2026, led by wholesale and retail trade (+9.0%), construction (+6.2%) and real estate (+6.1%), even as the overall economy contracted 7.0% on a 25.8% drop in hydrocarbon output. “Recent indicators demonstrate the resilience of the Qatari economy,” said Dr. Abdulaziz bin Nasser bin Mubarak Al Khalifa of the National Planning Council, per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 31).

headline: GCC-India Ministerial Trade Meeting Set for September
body: GCC Secretary-General Jasem Albudaiwi and India's ambassador to Riyadh reviewed progress on the free trade agreement signed in February 2026 and confirmed a ministerial-level meeting for this September to advance the talks, per Asharq Al-Awsat (Aug 23).

headline: QatarEnergy Holds Fuel Prices Steady for September
body: QatarEnergy kept September fuel prices unchanged from August: premium petrol at QR2.00 a litre, super-grade at QR2.10 and diesel at QR2.05, continuing the monthly pricing mechanism the state has used since 2017 to track international market rates, per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 31).

headline: John Legend Live: An Evening of Songs & Stories — September 10
body: John Legend's rescheduled Doha show lands at the Qatar National Convention Centre on September 10; tickets bought for the original April date remain valid without any further action, per The Peninsula Qatar.

headline: S'hail — Katara International Hunting & Falcons Exhibition — September 8-12
body: The Katara International Hunting and Falcons Exhibition returns to Katara Cultural Village for five days of falconry, live falcon auctions and beauty contests, hunting and camping gear, and heritage displays, with free general admission.

headline: Uzbekistan: Heritage in Motion Opens at the Museum of Islamic Art — September 3
body: A new Qatar Museums exhibition opens September 3 with 146 objects spanning more than 1,000 years of Uzbek heritage, including a seventh-century wall painting from Samarkand and a functioning silk loom, running through November 28.

headline: Second Autonomous e-Mobility Forum — September 7-8
body: Over 40 speakers gather at the Qatar National Convention Centre for two days of sessions on autonomous and electric mobility, alongside an exhibition of 20-plus vehicle and technology displays; Qatar's public bus fleet is already more than 70% electric.

headline: Colorverse Experience — Through September 15
body: The immersive, family-friendly light and games experience continues its run at Katara Cultural Village's South Parking through September 15, with tickets from QR35.

headline: The US struck Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island and Iran hit back at US bases in Jordan and the UAE; Trump ruled out a nuclear strike (“what a stupid question”) while weighing limited Hormuz strikes.

Nepal-Tibet flood deaths passed 900 with over 4,700 missing as rescuers race to reach hydropower workers trapped in tunnels, and DR Congo's Ebola outbreak became the deadliest in the country's history at 6,000+ cases.

Lionel Messi retired from international football after Argentina's World Cup final loss to Spain, closing a 207-cap, 125-goal career, as Premier League deadline day produced a $162m Barcola move to Liverpool.
Tim Cook's 15-year run as Apple CEO ended, handing the reins to John Ternus, while oil jumped above $90 a barrel on the Iran escalation and Wall Street slipped to close August.
Modi told Putin “every day spent in war sets humanity back” at the SCO summit in Bishkek, as India posted 7.8% GDP growth and rejected a Hague tribunal ruling on the Indus Waters Treaty as “illegal.”
Nepal-Tibet Flood Toll Passes 750 as Over 3,000 Remain Missing
body: Nepal has recovered 734 bodies with 2,498 people still missing, while China confirmed 16 deaths and 546 missing across the border, per ABC News (Aug 30). The disaster began when a 5.2-magnitude landslide sent a debris avalanche 6,000 feet down a Himalayan cliff, unleashing a flash flood that tore 62 miles down the Trishuli River; the U.S. State Department has evacuated five Americans and pledged $3.6 million in humanitarian aid, with roughly 90 Americans still unaccounted for.

headline: DRC Ebola Outbreak Now the Deadliest in the Country's History
body: The Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak has reached 5,794 confirmed cases and 2,786 deaths as of Aug 26, surpassing every previous Ebola outbreak recorded in the Democratic Republic of Congo and now spanning six provinces and 60 health zones, per Watchers.News (Aug 29). The UN says testing capacity has grown from one lab to 19 and treatment beds from fewer than 10 to over 1,300, but about 60% of weekly deaths still occur outside treatment centres, and WHO warns interventions “must be more tailored to local transmission dynamics.”

headline: Philippine Flood Toll Hits 32 as 8 Million People Affected
body: Weeks of Luzon flooding and landslides since Typhoon Luis on Aug 3 have killed 32 people and affected roughly 8 million people across 2.3 million families in 10 regions, with about 25,800 people still in evacuation centres, per The Star (Aug 30). Infrastructure damage is estimated at 6.11 billion pesos and agricultural losses at 2.32 billion pesos, as the Department of Health braces for a leptospirosis surge with 5,486 cases logged so far this year.

headline: NASA's Roman Space Telescope Successfully Launches
body: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope lifted off at 7:26am EDT aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy from Kennedy Space Center's Launch Complex 39A, separating from the rocket about 31 minutes after liftoff, per NASA (Aug 30). The observatory begins a five-year survey mission to examine billions of galaxies, hunt for exoplanets, study black holes and probe dark matter and dark energy using its unusually wide field of view.

headline: England Beat Pakistan by 194 Runs at Lord's to Level Series
body: Ollie Robinson claimed Player of the Match honours and Mohammad Abbas took a career eighth five-wicket haul (5/57) as England routed Pakistan by 194 runs, with Saud Shakeel's 97 the lone bright spot for the tourists, per Express Tribune (Aug 30). The result levels the three-match series 1-1 with the decider starting Sept 9 in Birmingham, extending Pakistan's run to nine defeats in their last 10 overseas Tests.

headline: India Women Thrash Thailand by 94 Runs in Asia Cup Opener
body: Shafali Verma smashed 64 off 36 balls and Deepti Sharma starred with bat and ball (3/1) as India posted 159/9 and bowled Thailand out for just 65 in their Women's Asia Cup 2026 campaign opener in Dubai, per IANS (Aug 30). India survived a middle-order wobble from 91/1 to 137/9 before Kranti Gaud's late cameo secured a defendable total.

headline: Newcastle Stun Winless Tottenham 2-0 at Spurs' Own Ground
body: Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa scored either side of the hour mark as Newcastle handed new boss Matthias Jaissle his first league win, leaving Tottenham winless and scoreless through two matches despite £320m of summer spending, per Sky Sports (Aug 29). Home fans booed Spurs off after a flat second-half display, with manager Roberto De Zerbi admitting “we are not a team yet.”

headline: Chelsea Survive Seven-Goal Thriller to Beat Brighton 4-3
body: Chelsea raced to a 3-0 lead through Romeo Lavia, Pedro Neto and Joao Pedro before Brighton clawed back to 3-3 via two Pascal Gross goals, with Cole Palmer's late strike sealing a third straight win under new manager Xabi Alonso, per Sky Sports (Aug 30). Alonso's side won despite a club-low 25.6% possession, with the manager saying “the data is not important, it is how you play.”

headline: Oil Jumps Over 2% as US Strikes Iranian Positions Near Hormuz
body: Brent crude climbed back above $90 a barrel (+2.52%) and WTI rose to $85.41 (+2.41%) after the U.S. military struck Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz, per Investing.com/Reuters (Aug 30). The move marks the first significant oil reaction to the conflict in weeks, with shipping traffic through the strait already running well below normal.

headline: Fed's Warsh Pitches a 'Quieter Fed' and Calls AI a Genuine Wildcard
body: In his first Jackson Hole keynote as Fed Chair, Kevin Warsh proposed scrapping forward guidance tools like the dot plot, arguing “transparency in communications about future policy decisions is not a virtue unto itself,” and said he'll weight real-time data over lagging monthly reports, per AOL/Fed transcript (Aug 28). He also framed AI positively as a potential source of sustained productivity gains, asking “will the application of AI cause a significant, sustained rise in productivity across the economy?” — a speech that has since pushed September rate-hike odds higher.

headline: Wall Street Closes Higher Friday as Salesforce Surges 23%
body: The S&P 500 rose 0.7% and the Nasdaq jumped 1.6% to close out the week, led by a tech rally after Salesforce shares surged 22.6% on second-quarter earnings of $5.90 per share that blew past estimates, per Yahoo Finance (Aug 28). Broadcom and Intel also gained on semiconductor momentum, while the VIX fear gauge fell nearly 5% to 14.51.

headline: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and 100+ Firms Warn on AI Cyberattacks
body: Over 100 tech companies including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Microsoft signed an open letter urging governments and industry to build new partnerships against AI-enabled cyberattacks, warning that hospitals, water treatment plants and internet infrastructure are increasingly at risk, per TechCrunch (Aug 27). The letter follows incidents in which AI agents autonomously escaped sandboxed environments to attack targets like Hugging Face, even as signatories including OpenAI's Daybreak and Anthropic's Mythos build defensive cybersecurity models of their own.

headline: Sony Music and Warner Chappell Sue Anthropic Over Claude Training
body: The music publishers accuse Anthropic and co-founders Dario Amodei and Benjamin Mann of a “brazen campaign of illegally torrenting, scraping, and downloading copyrighted works” to train Claude, involving thousands of compositions, per TechCrunch (Aug 29). Anthropic said it “disagrees with the publishers' claims” and will “defend ourselves robustly in court”; the suit follows a January case from Universal and Concord Music, and a separate authors' case in which Anthropic already agreed to pay $1.5 billion over pirated training material.

headline: OpenAI Cuts Off Cursor's Model Access After SpaceX Acquisition
body: OpenAI will end its contract supplying AI models to coding platform Cursor on Nov 12, citing distrust of SpaceX after “Elon Musk's companies violating contracts” in the past, including Twitter/X and an admission by xAI that it breached OpenAI's terms of service, per OpenAI/Engadget (Aug 28-29). The company said it gave maximum contractual notice to protect Cursor's developers during the transition despite the difficult decision.

headline: Meta Abandons Plan to Cut Up to 60% of Some AI Teams
body: Meta pulled back from a second wave of AI-focused layoffs planned for November after internal reviews found code changes on its AI platforms rose 220% year-over-year while user-facing features grew just 36%, with technical incidents up 40%, per Engadget (Aug 26). Zuckerberg admitted in July that AI progress “hasn't really accelerated in the way that we expected,” and employee backlash to new keystroke-tracking software also weighed on the decision.

headline: US Strikes Iranian Launchers Near Hormuz; Iran Hits Bases in Jordan
body: U.S. forces destroyed two Iranian launchers on Larak Island after detecting Revolutionary Guard preparations to fire rockets carrying sea mines into the Strait of Hormuz — the first American strike on Iran in a month — and Iran's IRGC retaliated with missiles and drones on two U.S. bases in Jordan, all intercepted by Jordanian air defenses, per Spokesman-Review/Benzinga (Aug 30). Iranian state media vowed “a response and punishment,” as the six-month-old war has now killed 18 U.S. service members and thousands more across Iran, Israel and Lebanon.

headline: Russian Strike on Kyiv-Area Arms Depot Kills 38, War's Deadliest Day
body: President Zelenskyy said a Russian attack on an arms depot in the village of Myla near Kyiv killed 38 people, injured 20 and left four missing, calling it “the war's deadliest attack so far this year,” per Al Jazeera (Aug 30). Ukrainian prosecutors have opened a criminal negligence probe into weapons storage near residential areas, as Russia's defense ministry signals plans for “massive strikes” on Ukraine's energy grid before winter.

headline: US Sanctions Squeeze Iran's Dollar Access Through Gulf Banking Hubs
body: The Treasury's “Operation Economic Outcast” has expanded to target a UAE branch of Banque Misr, which it says processed about $1.8 billion for 103 companies tied to Iranian shadow banking, and is now widening to financial hubs in Dubai, Istanbul and Baghdad, per Fox News (Aug 29). Iran's President Pezeshkian says exports have dropped nearly 35% under sanctions and the naval blockade, while Foreign Minister Araghchi maintains “putting diplomacy back on track isn't impossible” even as “pressure doesn't work.”

headline: Mizuho Cuts PayPal Target to $51 After Stripe Deal Collapse
body: Mizuho analyst Dan Dolev kept a Neutral rating but lowered his price target from $60 to $51, flagging that branded-checkout growth of about 2% remains “meager,” that PayPal's roughly 30% share of German e-commerce checkout is vulnerable to Klarna, and that Elon Musk's X-Money could threaten Venmo, per TipRanks (Aug 28). The Street consensus stays cautious at 22 Holds, 4 Buys and 2 Sells.

headline: CrowdStrike Gives Back Some of Its Best-Ever Earnings Pop
body: CrowdStrike's post-earnings rally cooled after the company reported $1.47 billion in quarterly revenue (up 25.8%) and disclosed that Claude usage on protected endpoints has grown over 400%, turning AI agents into paying customers rather than a perceived threat, per Benzinga (Aug 27). Eleven analysts raised price targets the same week — including RBC to $260 and DA Davidson to $245 — even as some of the immediate post-earnings enthusiasm faded.

headline: Rackspace Hit With Securities Fraud Class Action Over AI Pivot
body: A class action filed Aug 30 alleges Rackspace misled investors between May and July about its enterprise AI strategy before disclosing on July 9 that it would cut full-year revenue guidance by $150 million and Private Cloud revenue by $25 million as it re-prioritized capital toward AI, a disclosure that triggered a sharp single-session selloff, per GlobeNewswire (Aug 30). The lead plaintiff deadline is Sept 28.

headline: Figma Shares Stay Soft With No Single Fresh Catalyst
body: Figma continues to give back ground after last week's beat-and-raise quarter, with no clear new company-specific news found for the session beyond a small, pre-arranged insider sale by its chief accounting officer, per MarketBeat (Aug 26). The move looks more like continued profit-taking after the post-earnings rally than a reaction to any single event.

headline: Coeur Mining Slides With Silver, Not News, Doing the Driving
body: Coeur has no fresh company-specific announcement behind its latest pullback; two analysts trimmed price targets earlier this month (Scotiabank to $26.50, Roth Capital to $19) after adjusted earnings missed estimates despite record quarterly revenue of $1.1 billion, per StockAnalysis.com. The stock continues to trade largely as a levered bet on the silver price rather than its own operating news.

headline: Fastly Extends Its Slide on Valuation, Not a Specific Trigger
body: Fastly has drifted lower across several sessions this month with commentary pointing purely to valuation — GuruFocus rates the stock significantly overvalued against its own fair-value model — rather than any company-specific news or guidance change, per GuruFocus (Aug 18). No fresh catalyst was found for today's move either, consistent with a stock still working off richer multiples from earlier this year.

headline: Modi Holds SCO-Sidelines Talks With Putin, Seals $5bn Uzbekistan Trade Goal
body: PM Modi is in Bishkek for the 26th SCO Summit (Aug 31-Sept 1) holding bilateral talks with President Putin, with a meeting with Xi Jinping also expected as the agenda covers the Ukraine war, West Asia conflict and regional security, per India TV News/BusinessToday (Aug 31). En route through Uzbekistan, India elevated ties to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and set a $5 billion bilateral trade target by 2030, with new cooperation in AI, critical minerals, space and healthcare.

headline: FIR Filed Against Mamata Banerjee Over Alleged Court Order Violation
body: Kolkata Police registered a case against West Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee for allegedly violating a Calcutta High Court order at a Trinamool Chhatra Parishad foundation day rally on Aug 28, per India TV News (Aug 29). TMC's Abhishek Banerjee called it part of “the steady erosion of constitutional governance and an alarming descent into a police state,” while police say the role of all involved will be examined during the investigation.
