headline: Ex-Army Chief Naravane: Sindoor Marked a Deep-Strike Shift on Pakistan
body: Former Army Chief General M.M. Naravane said Operation Sindoor broke from past practice of hitting border-area terror camps by striking supporters and backers “wherever they may be,” including deep inside Pakistan at Muridke and Bahawalpur, per The Week (Aug 29). Asked if Pakistan could confront India militarily, Naravane said simply no, while noting Indian forces are closely watching Pakistan's Sir Creek activity.

headline: Burnham Excludes More Offenders From Early-Release Sentencing Rules
body: PM Burnham added manslaughter, death by dangerous or drunk driving, historic child sexual abuse, and killing of emergency workers to the list of offences excluded from an inherited early-release scheme meant to ease prison overcrowding, per North Edinburgh News (Aug 30). Burnham said he had “pushed the system to the very limits of what's possible without risking the prison system collapsing,” while promising tougher post-release tagging and exclusion zones.

headline: BoE's Bailey Sees Only 'Subdued' Inflation Effects So Far From Iran War
body: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said at Jackson Hole that he is seeing “quite subdued second-round effects” on UK inflation from the energy-price surge tied to the US-Iran conflict, crediting a weak labour market that limits workers' wage-bargaining power, per AOL/Bloomberg TV (Aug 28). Markets are still pricing a possible quarter-point BoE rate rise before year-end, a backdrop to yesterday's report of UK inflation expectations jumping to 3.9%.

headline: Qatar to Host UNCTAD's World Investment Forum in October
body: Qatar will host the ninth World Investment Forum on Oct 25-27 under the theme “Investing in the Future,” bringing together around 20 government ministers and 20 heads of international organisations to discuss AI, infrastructure, energy and sustainable finance, per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 30). The forum will highlight UNCTAD's World Investment Report 2026 finding that global FDI reached $1.6 trillion in 2025, concentrated disproportionately in developed markets.

headline: GCC Welcomes Syria's Removal From US Terrorism Sponsor List
body: GCC Secretary-General Jasem Mohamed Albudaiwi said Syria's delisting “supports efforts aimed at enhancing Syria's security and stability” and creates room for recovery and development, per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 25). The bloc reaffirmed its commitment to Syria's sovereignty and territorial integrity and called for continued international support for Syria's leadership and citizens.

headline: John Legend Live: An Evening of Songs & Stories
body: The Grammy-winning artist performs stripped-down versions of his hits at QNCC on Sept 10, after the concert was rescheduled from its original April date; tickets bought for the earlier date remain valid, per The Peninsula Qatar.

headline: S'hail — Katara International Hunting & Falcons Exhibition
body: The 10th edition runs Sept 8-12 at Katara Cultural Village and adds AI and 3D-modelling workshops for the first time, aimed at engaging younger generations with falconry heritage, per Gulf Times.

headline: Colorverse Experience
body: This immersive family attraction at Katara Cultural Village runs through Sept 15, with visitors acting as “Restorers” completing challenges across seven themed zones to bring colour back to a fictional world; suitable for ages four and up.

headline: Doha Jewellery and Watches Exhibition (DJWE)
body: The region's largest jewellery and watch fair returns to DECC from Sept 28 to Oct 3, typically drawing about 30,000 visitors from over 175 countries with free admission, per Qatar Tourism.

headline: US forces struck Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island near the Strait of Hormuz — Washington's first attack on Iran in a month — and Tehran retaliated within hours with missiles and drones on two U.S. bases in Jordan, all intercepted.
Nepal-Tibet flood deaths passed 750 with over 3,000 still missing, and Ebola in DR Congo became the deadliest outbreak in the country's history at 2,786 dead across 5,794 cases.
England beat Pakistan by 194 runs at Lord's to level the Test series 1-1 ahead of a Birmingham decider, while India's women thrashed Thailand by 94 runs to open their Asia Cup title defence.
PM Modi held SCO-sidelines talks with Putin in Bishkek and sealed a $5 billion India-Uzbekistan trade target, as Sony Music and Warner Chappell sued Anthropic over Claude's training data.
Fed Chair Warsh called AI-driven productivity a genuine wildcard for the economy as rate-hike odds firmed, and oil jumped over 2% on the Hormuz strikes.
Nepal-Tibet Flood Toll Passes 540, Over 2,000 Still Missing
body: A Himalayan glacier collapse that unleashed catastrophic flash flooding along the Nepal-Tibet border on Aug 26 — a surge powerful enough to register as a magnitude 5.2 seismic event — has now killed at least 543 people, with more than 2,000 still missing across both countries, including 90 Americans and hundreds of foreign trekkers, per ABC News (Aug 28). “They were like excited for this trip. It was like a spiritual, religious like trek they’d been looking forward to,” said Siddarth Venkatachalam, whose mother is among the missing.

headline: DRC Ebola Outbreak Now the Deadliest On Record
body: WHO data through Aug 26 confirms the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has become the largest ever recorded, with 5,794 confirmed cases and 2,786 deaths — a 48.1% case-fatality ratio — spread across 60 health zones in six provinces, per The Watchers (Aug 29). Only 1,293 patients have recovered so far as treatment centres race to contain the spread.

headline: Philippine Storms Kill 32, Displace Millions as Leptospirosis Tops 5,000 Cases
body: The Philippines’ Office of Civil Defense says tropical cyclones Luis, Maymay and Neneng combined with the seasonal habagat monsoon have killed 32 people and affected roughly 8 million people across 2.3 million families, with 117 local governments under a state of calamity, per Philstar (Aug 29). The flooding has fuelled a nationwide leptospirosis outbreak that reached 5,486 cases as of Aug 26; DOH Secretary Edwin Mercado said “we expect cases to increase in the next two weeks following the rains and flooding,” per Manila Bulletin (Aug 28).

headline: NASA’s Roman Space Telescope Set for Sunday Launch
body: A SpaceX Falcon Heavy carrying NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope rolled out to Kennedy Space Center’s Launch Complex 39A ahead of a targeted 7:26am EDT liftoff on Aug 30, per NASA (Aug 29). The school-bus-sized observatory will travel over a million miles from Earth to, in the words of NASA’s Shawn Domagal-Goldman, help astronomers “explore dark matter, dark energy, exoplanets, and almost anything from our own solar system to galaxies at the edge of the observable universe.”

headline: India Close Out Sri Lanka Series 1–0 After Colombo Stalemate
body: Sri Lanka salvaged an “epic draw” in the second Test at Colombo as Sonal Dinusha’s twin centuries (103 and an unbeaten 133) denied India a series sweep, per Gulf News (Aug 27). India, built on Devdutt Padikkal’s 328 series runs, had declared at 503-9 but could not bowl out Sri Lanka a second time as the hosts closed on 429-9; captain Shubman Gill still called it a job well done, saying “Test cricket won today.” India take the two-match series 1-0.

headline: England Tighten Grip on Lord’s Test as Pakistan Reel
body: Babar Azam’s comeback has done little to arrest Pakistan’s slide at Lord’s, where England built a 261-run lead by the close of a rain-hit day three, per The Express Tribune (Aug 29). Pakistan were skittled for 110 in their first innings — Ollie Robinson taking 4-11 and Jofra Archer three — before England’s reply, anchored by Emilio Gay, weathered further weather delays. Pakistan already trail 1-0 in the three-match series, leaving little margin left to level it.

headline: Harmanpreet’s India Open Asia Cup Title Bid Against Thailand
body: The Women’s T20 Asia Cup is underway in Dubai, with India — the competition’s most successful side historically — opening their campaign against Thailand on Aug 30 under fresh scrutiny after nine defeats in 16 T20Is this year and a group-stage World Cup exit, per Rozana Spokesman (Aug 29). Middle-order worries have deepened with Jemimah Rodrigues ruled out, bringing Pratika Rawal into the squad as cover. The tournament runs through Sept 13 and builds toward the blockbuster India-Pakistan meeting on Sept 5.

headline: Arsenal Draw Real Madrid, Barcelona Face PSG in Champions League Draw
body: Thursday’s 36-team Champions League league-phase draw in Monaco threw up heavyweight fixtures for 2026-27: Arsenal host Real Madrid but travel to Bayern Munich, while Barcelona face both PSG and Manchester City at home, per NBC Sports/Yahoo Sports (Aug 27). Liverpool were paired at home with Atletico Madrid, and City must also make the trip to Paris to face PSG. The league phase runs into January, building toward the final at Atletico Madrid’s Estadio Metropolitano on June 5, 2027.

headline: Norris Cuts Into Antonelli’s Lead With Zandvoort Double
body: Lando Norris’s back-to-back Zandvoort wins trimmed his title deficit to championship leader Kimi Antonelli to 83 points with 11 races left, per Sky Sports (Aug 24). McLaren boss Andrea Stella credited a Budapest upgrade package, saying Norris is “driving and operating at a very high level,” though the Briton stayed cautious: “I need more than what I have now,” he said. Attention now turns to Monza, where Antonelli is set to carry a grid penalty into the Italian Grand Prix.

headline: Fed Chief Warsh Turns Hawkish at Jackson Hole
body: In his first Jackson Hole address as Fed chair, Kevin Warsh warned that recent inflation reports “do not tell me that underlying trends have meaningfully improved,” and said the Fed “may have to raise interest rates in the coming months” unless price growth moves toward target “clearly and at sufficient speed,” per PBS NewsHour (Aug 28). The hawkish tone pushed the two-year Treasury yield from 4.22% to 4.30% and lifted market-implied odds of a September rate hike from roughly a third to near 50-50, rattling gold, bitcoin and equities.

headline: Gold Slides 3% as Dollar Rallies on Warsh’s Hawkish Turn
body: Gold retreated roughly 3% after Warsh’s speech as the dollar rebounded and September rate-hike odds jumped to 57.5% from 35.4% a day earlier, per XTB (Aug 28). “Assets that tend to be negatively correlated with the dollar are pulling back today, including EURUSD, gold, Bitcoin and even Wall Street equities,” XTB analysts wrote, pausing the metal’s multi-week climb that had carried it above $4,700/oz on Fed bond-buyback optimism.

headline: Bitcoin Tumbles From 3-Month High After Warsh Remarks
body: Bitcoin fell 3.3% to $77,678, erasing most of Thursday’s run to a three-month high near $81,330, after Warsh’s hawkish remarks pushed September rate-hike odds on Polymarket to 68%, per Eastern Herald (Aug 29). “Higher expected rates strengthen the dollar and lift real yields, reducing demand for non-yielding assets including Bitcoin,” the outlet noted, adding that a $6.4 billion options expiry at CME that morning amplified the selloff by removing hedging buffers.

headline: Crude Holds Near 2026 Highs Despite Dollar Swings
body: WTI crude traded at $83.40 a barrel on Aug 29, per ConvexTrade, with Brent near $90.55 a day earlier per Fortune (Aug 28), both holding close to the year’s highs even as the dollar firmed on Warsh’s hawkish tilt. Prices remain supported after OPEC+ completed its rollback of 1.65 million barrels per day in voluntary output cuts with a further September hike, removing a supply overhang that had weighed on the market.

headline: Wall Street Hits Records Ahead of Fed Speech
body: The Dow closed at 53,569.44 (+0.2%), the S&P 500 at 7,730.99 (+0.7%) and the Nasdaq at 26,541.35 (+1.6%) on Thursday, led by a tech-earnings rally after strong results from several large names, per Yahoo Finance (Aug 28). The records came just ahead of Warsh’s Jackson Hole address, which investors were watching closely for clarity on the Fed’s rate path.

headline: Nvidia’s Blowout Quarter Silences Bubble Skeptics — For Now
body: Nvidia posted Q2 revenue of $96.2 billion (up 106% year-over-year) and data-center revenue of $89 billion, then guided to roughly 70% sales growth through fiscal 2028, per Yahoo Finance (Aug 28). “AI has reached its inflection point. It’s doing useful work,” CEO Jensen Huang said, though supply-chain commitments doubled to $279 billion, underscoring that capacity — not demand — is now the bottleneck.

headline: OpenAI’s New Jalapeño Chip Fires a Warning Shot at Nvidia
body: OpenAI unveiled Jalapeño, its first custom inference chip, claiming 1.5-1.9x more AI work per watt and up to 4.1x better performance on interactive workloads than Nvidia’s GB200/GB300 while drawing far less power (550W vs. 1,200-1,400W), per 24/7 Wall St. (Aug 26). OpenAI added it “will continue to widely deploy accelerators from NVIDIA and other partners for both training and inference workloads,” but analysts said the disclosure itself signals rising competitive pressure on Nvidia’s margins from custom silicon.

headline: Meta Preps ‘Hatch’ AI Agents and $199.99 Premium Tier
body: Meta is finalizing its consumer AI agent platform, Hatch, for launch as soon as late August or early September, built on its OpenClaw technology and integrating with DoorDash, Etsy, Reddit, Yelp and Microsoft Outlook, per Forkast News via Yahoo Finance (Aug 25). A premium subscription could run up to $199.99 a month, while a new flagship model, “Watermelon,” targeting GPT-5.5-level performance on internal benchmarks, is slated for October as part of Mark Zuckerberg’s push to monetize AI beyond advertising.

headline: Anthropic Weighs Letting Early Shareholders Cash Out in IPO
body: Anthropic plans to unveil its IPO prospectus after Labor Day with a potential listing in late September or early October, per The Information (via The Daily Guardian, Aug 27), and is now considering letting some existing shareholders sell stock in the offering, The Information’s Jessica Lessin said on CNBC’s Squawk Box (Aug 28). The filing follows reports the company is targeting a valuation north of $2 trillion — which would make it the largest IPO on record, eclipsing SpaceX’s $1.77 trillion June debut.

headline: Moonshot AI Presses Microsoft, Amazon, Google for Kimi K3 Cut
body: China’s Moonshot AI is negotiating for up to a 30% revenue share from Microsoft Azure, Amazon AWS and Google Cloud on services built atop its 2.8-trillion-parameter, 1-million-token-context Kimi K3 model, per TradingKey (Aug 26). “Moonshot AI is seeking up to a 30% cut of the revenue generated from K3-related services on the three major cloud platforms,” the report said, noting talks remain early-stage with revenue mechanisms, data access and token audits still unresolved — the news comes after Moonshot raised a $3.5 billion Series F at a $35 billion valuation.

headline: Ukraine Strikes Force Shutdown of Russia’s Fourth-Largest Refinery
body: A Ukrainian drone strike on Aug 26 forced Russia’s NORSI refinery in Nizhny Novgorod — the country’s fourth-largest and second-biggest gasoline producer — to halt crude processing for the fifth time in five months, per Euromaidan Press (Aug 27). With Lukoil’s Perm and Volgograd plants also down, Russia has reinstated gasoline rationing in Moscow and St Petersburg and extended its diesel export ban, while Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov promised a “harsh response.”

headline: Iran Sets Terms for Reopening Hormuz as Qatar Joins Mediation
body: Iran says it will formally lay out conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz — including a lifted port blockade, war-damage compensation and sanctions relief — after Qatar’s prime minister became the third mediator, following Pakistan and Oman, to visit Tehran in a week, per Al Jazeera (Aug 28). “The US must first take practical steps to fulfil Iran’s conditions, and then Iran will proceed to open the Strait of Hormuz,” said Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, while Trump said “I have no time schedule, none. I’m not in a hurry.”

headline: Mossad Chief, Syrian FM Meet Again in Jordan Over Turkey Tensions
body: Mossad chief Roman Gofman met Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani in Jordan for further US-mediated talks aimed at defusing tensions that flared after Israel bombed Syria’s Abu al-Duhur airbase on Aug 18, claiming it was being readied for Turkish forces, per Turkish Minute (Aug 26). Damascus is pushing for an Israeli withdrawal to pre-Assad positions and a restored 1974 buffer-zone deal, while Defence Minister Israel Katz said Israeli forces would stay on Mount Hermon, citing what he called jihadist threats.

headline: Xi-Trump Summit Set for Sept 24, Trade Truce Extension “Almost Certain”
body: Xi Jinping is expected to meet Donald Trump in Washington on Sep 24, with the year-long trade truce reached in Busan last October likely to be extended, per South China Morning Post (Aug 28). Chinese and US officials are still deciding whether business leaders will join Xi’s delegation to reciprocate Trump’s May visit to Beijing; US Ambassador David Perdue called that trip “very successful” and said Washington is preparing for “important high-level interactions.”

headline: PayPal’s Buyout Talks With Stripe and Advent Collapse
body: Stripe and private-equity firm Advent International have abandoned their reported $50 billion approach to acquire PayPal, per Yahoo Finance (Aug 28), ending weeks of takeover speculation that had been propping up the stock. Analyst Josh Kohn-Lindquist argued PayPal “still trades at only 7.5 times free cash flow,” suggesting underlying value remains even without a deal. No new operating issue was cited — the move reflects the loss of acquisition-premium speculation rather than any change to PayPal’s business.

headline: Nvidia Beats on Revenue but Guides to Thinner Margins
body: Nvidia posted fiscal second-quarter revenue of $96.2 billion, more than doubling year-over-year and beating Wall Street’s $92.2 billion estimate, with data-center revenue up 117% to $89 billion, per Yahoo Finance (Aug 27). CFO Colette Kress guided gross margins down toward 71–72% by fiscal Q4 from the current 75%, saying “memory scarcity today is being driven in large part by the AI buildout itself.” Forward supply commitments more than doubled to $279 billion, underscoring how much capacity Nvidia has locked in to meet AI demand.

headline: CrowdStrike Notches a Record Quarter, Then Gives Some Back
body: CrowdStrike reported fiscal second-quarter revenue of $1.47 billion, up 26% year-over-year and above the $1.44 billion consensus, with net-new annual recurring revenue of $332.8 million marking a company record, per Vantage Markets (Aug 28). The company raised full-year revenue guidance to $5.99–$6.01 billion, with CEO George Kurtz crediting demand for the Falcon Flex platform, though a newly disclosed $13.1 million legal accrual tied to last year’s July outage drew attention, per TradingKey (Aug 28).

headline: Amazon Leans Further Into AI Infrastructure and Clean Power
body: Amazon signed new renewable-energy power purchase agreements in Europe, including offshore wind commitments in Germany and wind-farm deals in Sweden, to support its expanding AWS and AI data-center footprint, per TradingKey (Aug 28). Analysts reiterated buy ratings and lifted price targets to an average near $320, citing “accelerating enterprise demand for cloud migration, higher adoption of custom data center processors alongside expanded GPU integrations, and robust underlying retail fundamentals,” though some investors flagged Amazon’s roughly $220 billion 2026 capital-expenditure plan as a capital-efficiency question.

headline: Figma Posts a Third Straight Quarter of Accelerating Growth
body: Figma reported second-quarter revenue of $370.1 million, up 48% year-over-year, and raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance by $40 million to $1.463–$1.467 billion, per StockTitan (Aug 11). CEO Dylan Field called it “Figma’s third straight quarter of accelerated revenue growth,” pointing to AI credit monetization and a new Figma agent that more than half of its largest customers now use weekly. Net dollar retention held at 136%, with customers paying $10,000-plus in annual recurring revenue up 34% year-over-year to nearly 16,000.

headline: Rackspace Cuts Its Outlook as It Pivots Toward AI Compute
body: Rackspace Technology lowered its full-year revenue guidance to $2.45–$2.55 billion, roughly a 7% cut at the midpoint, as it exits lower-margin public-cloud resale business in favor of AI compute, per Yahoo Finance (Aug 11). The company detailed new AI partnerships, including with Palantir, and said it expects $15–$20 million of revenue per megawatt of deployed AI compute capacity, though margin benefits aren’t expected until 2027. It also announced a $250 million at-the-market equity offering to fund the GPU buildout, adding near-term dilution on top of the guidance cut.

headline: Arm Holdings Cools Off After a Multi-Week AI Rally
body: Arm Holdings pulled back after a strong multi-day advance driven by positive semiconductor earnings and an expanded partnership with IBM on enterprise workloads, per TradingKey (Aug 28). With shares trading near 100 times forward earnings, the report characterized the pullback as valuation-driven consolidation rather than a reaction to fresh company news, compounded by routine executive share sales disclosed in SEC filings. Arm’s longer-term case — adoption of its v9 architecture and custom AI CPU designs among cloud hyperscalers — was described as intact.

headline: Coeur Mining Slides With No Clear Catalyst Behind It
body: No company-specific announcement accompanied Coeur Mining’s decline, per GuruFocus (Aug 28); the piece instead flagged valuation concerns and noted that insiders had sold about $5.6 million of stock over the prior year, calling that pattern a potential “red flag.” Coeur is a small-cap silver and gold miner with high sensitivity to metals prices and broader risk sentiment, and no company-specific news was found to explain the session’s move.

headline: Modi Lands in Tashkent, Sets Up Xi Meeting at SCO Summit
body: PM Modi arrived in Uzbekistan Aug 29 to begin a four-day Central Asia trip, greeted personally by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev — his fourth visit since 2015. “Landed in Tashkent to a warm welcome by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. Grateful to him for the special gesture,” Modi posted, per Organiser (Aug 29). He heads next to Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan for the 26th SCO Summit (Aug 31–Sept 1), where a brief bilateral with Xi Jinping is expected ahead of Xi’s full state visit to Delhi for the Sept 12–13 BRICS summit.

headline: Ex-CDS Chauhan: Modi Gave Forces ‘Complete Freedom’ Before Sindoor
body: Former Chief of Defence Staff Gen Anil Chauhan detailed PM Modi’s April 29 directive ahead of Operation Sindoor, per WION (Aug 26): “The Prime Minister told us only one thing: that he is not under any kind of political pressure to do it immediately,” with orders to leave “no reason for failure, either human or because of technical reasons.” Chauhan said India’s escalation doctrine ensured “the winning note will always be delivered by us and not by the Pakistanis” during the operation, launched May 7 and paused May 10 after Pakistan sought a ceasefire.

headline: US Sanctions Four India-Based Firms Over $119mn Iran Oil Trade
body: Washington sanctioned four India-based companies and three individuals for allegedly moving $119 million in Iranian petroleum products, per Business Today (Aug 26). Sadashiva Overseas Limited was flagged for roughly $69 million in imports between February 2024 and June 2025, alongside PP Softtech, Prakrutees Infra Impex and customs broker Portease Partners; nearly 60 entities, individuals and vessels — including about 20 China/Hong Kong-based firms — were hit in the same action. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called it part of an effort to “tighten the noose” on Iran, describing it as an “economic D-Day.”

headline: Burnham Eyes September US Trip to Press Trump on Ukraine
body: PM Andy Burnham said he is “looking forward to going to New York” next month for the UN General Assembly to lobby President Trump for more Patriot missiles for Ukraine, per ITV News (Aug 25). Speaking after visiting Kyiv for Ukraine's 35th independence anniversary, Burnham noted “there are other players who could help in the mix who we have influence with” and pledged the UK would share Scalp missile production blueprints, as European allies scramble to plug gaps left by Middle East conflicts diverting US air-defence stock.

headline: UK Inflation Expectations Jump to 3.9%, Complicating BoE Path
body: A Citi/YouGov survey found British households' 12-month inflation expectations jumped to 3.9% in August from 3.4% in July, with longer-term expectations rising to 4.1% — the highest since April — per Yahoo Finance/Reuters (Aug 25). Citi called the reversal “hawkish,” warning that energy prices tied to the Iran conflict could feed sustained price pressure, though it cautioned against reading too much into a single report as the Bank of England weighs its next move.

headline: Reform UK Sinks to 18-Month Polling Low Amid Infighting
body: Reform UK has fallen to 23% in the latest More in Common poll, its lowest level in over 18 months, level with a resurgent Labour on 27% and the Conservatives on 22%, per Left Foot Forward (Aug 26). The slide follows Nigel Farage's undeclared £5 million crypto-donor gift now facing a Standards Committee review, candidates' far-right remarks, and local-government infighting — support has fallen from roughly 30% a year ago into the low twenties now.

headline: Qatar Condemns Israeli Storming of UNRWA Training Center
body: Qatar's Foreign Ministry strongly condemned Israeli occupation forces for entering the Qalandiya Training Center run by UNRWA in occupied East Jerusalem, calling it “a blatant violation of international humanitarian law,” per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 26). Doha warned the move appears aimed at dismantling UNRWA and cutting services to millions of Palestinians across Gaza, the West Bank, Jordan, Syria and Lebanon, and urged the international community to take “immediate protective measures” for UNRWA facilities.

headline: Qatar Hosts Iran for Hormuz De-Escalation Talks
body: Qatari PM Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani met Iranian officials to discuss reopening the Strait of Hormuz, floating a temporary shipping corridor and a possible “joint project” to clear the strait of mines, per Al Jazeera (Aug 27). Tehran, which has controlled the waterway since the February 28 war began, is demanding Washington lift its naval blockade and oil sanctions before reopening it; Qatar and Pakistan are mediating alongside Oman, with no deal yet reached.

headline: GCC Agrees Joint Cybersecurity Framework Amid Regional Tensions
body: Qatar's NCSA chief Eng. Abdulrahman bin Ali Al Farahid Al Malki joined the fifth GCC Ministerial Committee for Cybersecurity in Manama, which formally adopted joint frameworks to harmonize Gulf defence protocols, per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 28). Ministers authorized the sixth and seventh Gulf Cyber Drills to test resilience against multi-vector attacks, with officials saying “safeguarding the Gulf's interconnected digital economy requires synchronised regional action rather than isolated defence models” as regional tensions escalate.

headline: Doha Trade Fair
body: A wide-ranging shopping fair with retailers spanning multiple product categories, running Aug 24–Sept 4 at the Doha Exhibition & Convention Center; free entry.

headline: Discover the World Behind Kalila wa Dimna
body: A long-running exhibition at the Museum of Islamic Art Library exploring the classic fable collection through manuscript replicas and architectural models, on view Aug 25–Dec 30; free entry.

headline: Rouda Al Malki Exhibition
body: A curated pop-up of women's fashion and lifestyle essentials at the Qatar National Convention Center, Aug 28–Sept 2; free entry.

headline: ORBIT Arabian Night ft. Cheba Souad
body: A live Rai music performance by Algerian singer Cheba Souad at Cielo Hotel, Lusail, on Aug 28; 21+, tickets from QAR 100 via Q-Tickets.

headline: Travancore Fest: Mentalist Anandhu — The Secret Letter
body: An interactive mentalism and storytelling show at Regency Hall on Aug 28, blending illusion with audience participation; tickets from QAR 100.

headline: A Himalayan glacier collapse violent enough to register as a 5.2-magnitude earthquake unleashed the Nepal-Tibet flash flood, whose toll has now climbed past 540 dead with over 2,000 still missing.
New Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish first Jackson Hole speech reversed gold's rally, knocked bitcoin down 3.3% to $77,678, and pushed September rate-hike odds toward 50-50.
Nvidia's blowout Q2 (revenue up 106% to $96.2 billion) drew a rival jab from OpenAI's new in-house Jalapeño chip, unveiled the same week as a warning shot at Nvidia's margins.

PM Modi opened a four-day Central Asia trip in Tashkent ahead of the SCO summit in Bishkek, where a brief Modi-Xi meeting is expected before Xi's full state visit to Delhi for the Sept 12-13 BRICS summit.

Iran named its terms for reopening the Strait of Hormuz as Qatar's PM joined Pakistan and Oman as a third mediator, while England tightened its grip on the Lord's Test and India's Women's T20 Asia Cup bid opened in Dubai.
Nepal-Tibet Border Flash Flood Kills 100+, Leaves 403 Missing Including Dozens of Foreign Tourists
body: A flash flood and mudslide tore through the Bhote Koshi river valley on the Nepal-Tibet border on Aug 25-26, killing more than 100 people and leaving 403 missing, including 34 Australians, 47 Americans, 33 Britons and 133 Indian pilgrims, per ABC News (Aug 27). Rescue teams have been unable to reach the hardest-hit villages of Syapru Besi and Timure by helicopter because of narrow gorges, and Nepal’s president Ramachandra Paudel said he was “extremely saddened” by the “loss of lives and property caused by the sudden flood.”

headline: Dolly Parton, Country Music Icon, Dies at 80 After Brief Cancer Battle
body: Dolly Parton died on Aug 25 at Vanderbilt-Ingram Cancer Center in Nashville after a brief battle with cancer, surrounded by loved ones, per CBS News (Aug 26). Over a six-decade career she sold more than 100 million records, won 10 Grammys and set a Guinness World Record for the longest span of No. 1 country hits; President Trump said “there has never been anyone like her, and never will,” while actress Sally Field said “if there are truly angels on earth, then we have just lost one.”

headline: DRC’s Ebola Outbreak Becomes the Largest Ever Recorded in the Country
body: The Bundibugyo-virus Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has reached 4,686 confirmed cases and 2,186 deaths — a 46.8% fatality rate — across 54 health zones in six provinces, with cases also confirmed in Uganda and France, per the World Health Organization (Aug 14). WHO calls it “the largest Ebola outbreak ever reported in the country and expanding faster than any previous Ebola outbreak,” rating the risk to the DRC as very high.

headline: Manila Leptospirosis Cases Top 4,285 as Hospitals Hit 500% of ER Capacity
body: Metro Manila’s leptospirosis count has climbed to 4,285 patients as of Aug 22 — 845 new cases in two weeks and already well past last year’s full-season record of 3,440 — as Habagat rains keep floodwaters standing, per Philstar (Aug 25). San Lazaro Hospital is running at 300-500% of emergency-room capacity, and the Department of Health says it is “ensuring adequate bed and medicine availability for admitted patients through surge capacity management.”

headline: India Close In on Series Sweep as Colombo Test Reaches Final Day
body: India head into the final day of the second Test in Colombo well on top after a century from Devdutt Padikkal and an unbeaten 115 from Dhruv Jurel powered a first-innings declaration on 503/9, per ESPNcricinfo. Sri Lanka have fought back through fifties from Pasindu Sooriyabandara and Kamindu Mendis, but India lead the series 1-0 and are chasing the win that would complete a 2-0 sweep.

headline: Babar Azam Returns as Pakistan Chase a Series Level at Lord’s
body: Pakistan captain Babar Azam is back in the side for today’s second Test against England at Lord’s after recovering from a finger injury and declaring himself “90% fit,” per ANI (Aug 25). Pakistan trail 1-0 after an innings defeat at Headingley and need a win to square the series; bowling coach Umar Gul said the squad trained “with full intensity” and is confident of a “bounce back.”

headline: Champions League League-Phase Draw Sets 36 Clubs’ Opponents
body: UEFA holds today’s league-phase draw for the 2026-27 Champions League, sorting all 36 clubs into four seeding pots and assigning each side eight opponents — four home, four away — ahead of matchday one on Sept 8-10, per beIN Sports. It is the last major fixture before Europe’s revamped league-table format kicks off in earnest next month.

headline: Manchester City Complete Five-Year Deal for Lille’s Teenage Midfielder Bouaddi
body: Manchester City have signed 18-year-old Morocco international Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille on a five-year contract, per Goal.com/Yahoo Sports (Aug 26). “This is a very special day for me and my family — they are, for me, the best club in the world,” Bouaddi said, while director of football Hugo Viana called his potential “extremely high.”

headline: Gold Tops $4,700 as Markets Brace for Fed Chair Warsh’s First Jackson Hole Speech
body: Gold has rallied more than 14% since the start of August, with COMEX futures settling above $4,700/oz, after the Treasury doubled its long-term bond buyback program to at least $4 billion a session to cap surging long-end yields, per Kitco/NAI 500 (Aug 24). Markets are now bracing for Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s first Jackson Hole keynote on Aug 28, his first since taking office in May.

headline: Bitcoin Surges Toward $81,000, Its Highest Level in Three Months
body: Bitcoin opened near $79,000 and touched an intraday high above $81,000 — up roughly 22% over the past week — after the Treasury’s expanded bond buyback and a White House meeting between President Trump and executives from Coinbase and Robinhood on crypto policy, per Yahoo Finance (Aug 25). Ethereum also gained, trading near $2,480.

headline: Oil Edges Down as Traders Await Fresh Supply and Demand Signals
body: WTI crude slipped roughly 0.8% to $80.42 a barrel and Brent eased to $86.32, per Forbes Advisor (Aug 26), with no single catalyst cited beyond traders positioning ahead of the next OPEC+ decision and US inventory data.

headline: Nvidia Posts Record $96.2B Quarter, But Stock Slips on AI-Bubble Worries
body: Nvidia’s fiscal Q2 revenue more than doubled year-over-year to $96.2 billion, with data-center sales of $89 billion, adjusted EPS of $2.22 beating estimates, and Q3 guidance of $108 billion, per an Investing.com earnings transcript and Invezz (Aug 26). CEO Jensen Huang said “AI has reached its inflection point… now, compute is revenue,” but shares still slipped as investors weighed “circular” AI-investment deals and stretched valuations across the sector.

headline: Meta to Launch ‘Hatch’ AI Agent Platform With a $199.99 Premium Tier
body: Meta plans to launch a consumer AI-agent platform called Hatch within weeks, with a premium subscription priced up to $199.99 a month as the company pivots from ad-monetization toward paid AI tools, per The Information via Investing.com (Aug 24). Evercore ISI raised its price target on Meta to $860 from $820 citing the AI push, above the Street’s $746 average target.

headline: Anthropic Pitches IPO Investors on a $30 Trillion Market Opportunity
body: Anthropic is preparing to tell prospective IPO investors its addressable market is worth more than $30 trillion — bigger than SpaceX’s record $28.5 trillion pitch — as it seeks a valuation near $2 trillion, per Yahoo Finance/Fortune (Aug 25). The company posted $11.6 billion in Q2 revenue, with the $30 trillion figure meant to capture “the full scope of work that could be completed using AI models.”

headline: Amazon Shuts Down Mechanical Turk After 21 Years as AI Replaces Crowdsourced Work
body: Amazon will close Mechanical Turk — the crowdsourced-labor platform Jeff Bezos once called “artificial artificial intelligence” — on Sept 30, along with SageMaker Ground Truth and Augmented AI, per CNBC/TechStartups (Aug 25-26). The platform once relied on more than 500,000 workers for tasks like image-labeling and transcription that AI systems now handle directly.

headline: China’s Moonshot AI in Talks With Microsoft, Amazon and Google Over Kimi K3 Revenue Share
body: Moonshot AI is negotiating with Microsoft Azure, AWS and Google Cloud for revenue-sharing deals worth up to 30% on services built around its open-weight Kimi K3 model, per Reuters via Yahoo Finance (Aug 26). Sticking points include how revenue is split, data access, and auditing token usage; all three US cloud providers declined to comment.

headline: Ukrainian Drones Set Russia’s Fourth-Largest Refinery Ablaze Overnight
body: A drone strike sparked a fire overnight at the NORSI refinery in Kstovo, Russia — the country’s fourth-largest, processing 15-17 million tonnes of crude a year for military fuel — marking Ukraine’s fifth confirmed hit on the plant in 2026, per the Kyiv Independent (Aug 26). No casualties were reported and Russian authorities had not commented by publication.

headline: Pakistan Says ‘Significant Progress’ Made in Tehran Talks to Reopen Hormuz
body: Pakistan’s interior minister Mohsin Naqvi said talks in Tehran on reopening the Strait of Hormuz and reviving the expired Islamabad ceasefire framework “concluded on a highly positive note,” per Al Jazeera (Aug 25). Iran’s president Masoud Pezeshkian said the “United States must correct its tone,” as Washington threatens fresh economic penalties on Iran and Tehran threatens to choke Gulf oil exports.

headline: Syria’s Foreign Minister and Israel’s Mossad Chief Meet in Jordan to Ease Tensions
body: Syrian FM Asaad al-Shaibani met Mossad chief Roman Gofman in Jordan on Aug 23 after an Israeli strike on the Abu Duhur airbase, discussing a halt to Israeli strikes and reviving a security agreement, per Al Jazeera (Aug 24). Damascus wants Israel back to pre-December-2024 positions under the 1974 disengagement pact, while Israel is seeking to block Turkish military activity in Syria and protect the Druze community; analyst Hassan Mneimneh called the talks “unlikely to de-escalate tensions given Israel’s track record.”

headline: Trump Prepares 7.5% China Tariff Ahead of Late-September Xi Summit
body: The Trump administration is finalizing a new 7.5% tariff on Chinese goods to punish Beijing for a flood of cheap exports, on top of the 10-12.5% tariffs already imposed on 60 economies, per Fortune (Aug 24). Officials believe the level is calibrated to avoid derailing the one-year US-China trade truce or the planned late-September White House summit between Trump and Xi Jinping.

headline: Nvidia’s Record Quarter Meets AI-Bubble Skepticism
body: Nvidia posted fiscal Q2 revenue of $96.2 billion, more than double a year earlier, with data-center sales of $89 billion and Q3 guidance of $108 billion, beating estimates on both lines, per Investing.com (Aug 26). Shares still slipped as investors weighed a gross-margin dip to roughly 74% and growing worry that circular financing deals across the AI ecosystem could leave the industry exposed if spending momentum slows.

headline: Oracle Jumps on Citigroup Call After Its Sharpest-Ever Drawdown
body: Oracle rose about 4.5% after Citigroup called the recent selloff “one of the most extreme dislocations and drawdowns in the stock’s history” and set a $330 price target, arguing its $85 billion AI-services backlog could push 2030 earnings to $22 a share, per The Motley Fool (Aug 26).

headline: Arm Rallies on New AGI CPU Launch With Meta as Lead Partner
body: Arm Holdings gained after unveiling its first production chip design in 35 years, the AGI CPU, with Meta as lead partner and a stated $15 billion annual revenue target, alongside roughly 20% revenue and 12% profit growth last quarter, per TradersUnion (Aug 25). One analyst cautioned the rally “looks overstated against persistent bearish technicals.”

headline: Zoom Slides as Soft Q3 Guidance Overshadows a Beat
body: Zoom beat Q2 estimates with $1.28 billion in revenue and $1.55 adjusted EPS, but shares fell as Q3 guidance of $1.275-1.28 billion and $1.46-1.48 EPS came in below consensus, per Yahoo Finance (Aug 26). CEO Eric Yuan pointed to 7.8% enterprise-revenue growth, “its strongest growth rate in three years,” but investors focused on the softer outlook.

headline: fuboTV Slides as an HD Upgrade Fails to Quiet Cash-Flow Worries
body: fuboTV shares fell after an announced 1080p HD streaming upgrade for sports channels failed to address investor concern over cash flow, with adjusted EBITDA down 38% to $19.1 million and margin compressed to 1.29% even as subscribers grew 2% to 5.75 million, per ts2.tech (Aug 22).

headline: Hydrofarm Continues to Slide With No Fresh Company-Specific Trigger
body: Hydrofarm shares fell again with no new company-specific news found for the session; the hydroponics supplier is still digesting the wider-than-expected Q2 loss and 41% revenue decline it disclosed earlier this month amid industry oversupply.

headline: China, India Agree to 8 Steps to Ease Border Tensions Before Xi’s Delhi Visit
body: China and India have agreed to eight steps to ease border tensions ahead of Xi Jinping’s first visit to India in seven years, with a brief Modi-Xi meeting expected at the SCO summit in Bishkek on Aug 31-Sept 1 and a full state visit for the BRICS summit in New Delhi on Sept 12-13 with a roughly 400-person delegation, per the South China Morning Post (Aug 27). Agenda items include border disputes, trade, investment and visa access, though “sources and experts caution against overplaying expectations” of a breakthrough.

headline: Ex-Army Chief Reveals Modi Gave Military ‘Complete Freedom of Action’ Before Operation Sindoor
body: Former Chief of Defence Staff Gen Anil Chauhan said PM Modi told the armed forces before Operation Sindoor to “do it at your own time, but ensure there is no reason for failure,” adding there was no political pressure to strike immediately, per ANI (Aug 26). Chauhan said the clear political direction was “nothing better” the military could ask for.

headline: US Sanctions Four India-Based Firms Over $119M in Iranian Oil Trade
body: The US Treasury sanctioned four India-based firms — Sadashiva Overseas, PP Softtech, Prakrutees Infra Impex and Portease Partners — and three Indian nationals over roughly $119 million in Iranian oil and petrochemical trade, per Business Today (Aug 26). Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent framed the campaign as an effort to “tighten the noose on Iran.”

headline: PM Andy Burnham to Lobby Trump on Ukraine Patriot Missiles in September
body: Prime Minister Andy Burnham is likely to travel to the US in September, around the UN General Assembly, to press for more Patriot interceptor missiles for Ukraine, in what would be his first US visit since taking office in July, per ITV News (Aug 25). “Really confident” the missile shortage was “fixable,” Burnham told Bloomberg, adding he was “looking forward to going to New York.”

headline: UK Household Inflation Expectations Jump to 3.9%, Complicating BoE Path
body: A Citi/YouGov survey found UK households now expect 3.9% inflation over the next 12 months, up from 3.4% in July, with longer-term expectations rising to 4.1% versus actual inflation of 2.9%, per Citi (Aug 25). Citi economist Callum McLaren-Stewart called the reversal of a months-long downtrend “a hawkish and significant development” for the Bank of England.

headline: Reform UK’s Internal Feuds Blunt Farage’s Push to Ready the Party for Government
body: Reform UK is now tied with Labour at roughly 24% in Bloomberg’s composite poll, having lost its lead since Andy Burnham became PM, even as infighting over aide Zia Yusuf and a suspended adviser who said Farage is “surrounded by people who tell him what he wants to hear” sidetracks efforts to professionalize the party, per Bloomberg via the Union-Bulletin (Aug 24).

headline: Qatar Condemns Israeli Storming of UNRWA Training Center in East Jerusalem
body: Qatar’s Foreign Ministry condemned Israeli forces’ entry into UNRWA’s Qalandiya training center in East Jerusalem as “a blatant violation of international humanitarian law,” warning it aims to dismantle the agency that serves millions of Palestinian refugees, per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 26). Doha again called for an independent Palestinian state on 1967 borders with East Jerusalem as its capital.

headline: Qatar Airways Becomes First Airline With a Starlink-Equipped 787 in Service
body: Qatar Airways has completed Starlink installations across its entire 787-8 fleet and now has 83% of its widebody aircraft equipped with the satellite internet system, becoming the first carrier to fly a Starlink-fitted 787-9 commercially since July 5, per AirlineGeeks (Aug 26). The airline aims to have every Dreamliner equipped by the end of 2026.

headline: Penumbral Lunar Eclipse Visible Over Qatar Friday Dawn
body: A brief penumbral lunar eclipse will be visible from Qatar in the pre-dawn hours of Friday, Aug 28, peaking around 4:57-5:11am, per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 26). Sheikh Salman bin Jabor Al Thani of the Qatar Center for Space Sciences and Astronomy said the moon “will not enter Earth’s direct shadow, but rather the edge of Earth’s shadow,” and urged the public to ignore circulating eclipse myths.

headline: Qatar Face China in FIBA World Cup Qualifier
body: Qatar’s national basketball team hosts China at Al Janoub Stadium today in a FIBA Basketball World Cup 2027 Asian Qualifiers fixture, part of Qatar’s qualifying campaign, per Qatar Living.

headline: Doha Trade Fair Opens at DECC
body: A shopping exhibition featuring a wide range of products under one roof runs at the Doha Exhibition and Convention Center from Aug 24 through Sept 4, per Qatar Living.

headline: Run the Dome Brings Indoor Racing to Aspire Dome
body: A competition offering competitive speed races and fun runs for all skill levels takes place at the Aspire Dome on Aug 28-29, per Qatar Living.

headline: Rouda Al Malki Fashion Exhibition Opens at QNCC
body: A showcase of women’s fashion, essentials and lifestyle products runs at the Qatar National Convention Center from Aug 28 through Sept 2, per Qatar Living.

headline: ORBIT Arabian Night Brings Raï Music to Lusail
body: A live performance of Algerian Raï music takes place at Cielo Hotel in Lusail on Aug 28, per Qatar Living.

headline: A flash flood on the Nepal-Tibet border has killed more than 100 people and left 403 missing, including dozens of foreign tourists, as rescuers struggle to reach gorge villages cut off by the terrain.

Nvidia posted a record $96.2 billion quarter and beat estimates on every line, but its stock still slipped as investors fretted about AI-bubble valuations and circular financing deals across the sector.
Country music icon Dolly Parton died at 80 after a brief cancer battle, with tributes pouring in from President Trump, Sally Field and fellow musicians.
New UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham plans a September trip to lobby Trump for more Patriot missiles for Ukraine, as Reform UK's internal feuds pull the party level with Labour in the polls.
India closed in on a series-sweeping win in Colombo as Pakistan's Babar Azam returned for a series-levelling Lord's Test and UEFA drew the Champions League's revamped league phase.
Indonesia’s Flores Quake Toll Climbs Past 100 as Aftershocks Persist
body: The death toll from the magnitude-7.7 earthquake that struck Indonesia’s Flores region on Aug 15 has climbed to at least 103, with more than 180,000 people displaced and 1,603 injured, per CGTN and other reports (Aug 25). Disaster agency chief Suharyanto said some victims “had initially survived with serious injuries but later died while receiving treatment,” as authorities logged 6,409 aftershocks — 33 of them above magnitude 5.0 — expected to keep rattling the region for three to four more weeks.

headline: Indonesia Prays for Rain as Sumatra, Kalimantan Wildfires Choke Region
body: Indonesia is battling a worsening haze crisis as forest fires rage across South Sumatra and Kalimantan, with more than 1,400 hot spots detected in South Sumatra alone and nearly 940 square kilometers burned in July, per NPR (Aug 25). About 3,000 residents gathered in Palembang for a Muslim rain prayer, salat istisqa, as authorities deployed 30 aircraft for cloud-seeding and water-bombing and arrested 72 people suspected of starting fires; Governor Herman Deru said officials “have done everything we can and worked closely with all relevant parties.”

headline: Manila Floods Trigger Leptospirosis Surge, Fury Over Flood-Control Funds
body: Nearly 8 inches of rain fell on metro Manila in just five hours, turning streets into canals, and health authorities have now logged more than 3,000 cases of leptospirosis from the floodwaters, per Circle of Blue (Aug 25). Public anger is mounting over a flood-control corruption scandal after reports the government spent $32.4 billion on flood-control projects since 2011 that proved inadequate or nonexistent — underscored by a dam overtopping in Manila this month — with residents asking, “Where did all the money that was meant to protect them actually go?”

headline: Tokayev-Backed Party Confirmed Winner of Kazakhstan’s Parliamentary Vote
body: Kazakhstan’s electoral commission has finalized results from Sunday’s parliamentary vote: the newly formed, Tokayev-backed Adilet party won just over 71% support on 74% turnout, cementing the president’s grip on the restructured, single-chamber 145-seat Kurultai, per Al Jazeera (Aug 24). Four other pro-Tokayev blocs — Respublika, Ak Zhol, the Nationwide Social Democratic Party and Auyl — also entered parliament, with the commission calling the outcome likely to “consolidate the power of President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev.”

headline: Colombia Earthquake Death Toll Rises to 331 Two Weeks After Disaster
body: Colombia’s confirmed death toll from the magnitude-7.4 earthquake that struck near San Jose del Palmar on Aug 10 has risen to 331, with 4,439 injured, 240 still missing and 364 rescued, per Colombia One (Aug 25). The government has declared an “economic, social and ecological emergency” as more than 220 tons of humanitarian aid arrive to help the 361,000-plus people affected across 494 municipalities, where over 31,500 homes were completely destroyed and 603 buildings collapsed.

headline: Celtic Blow Four-Goal Aggregate Lead, Crash Out of Champions League to LASK Linz
body: Celtic suffered a historic Champions League playoff collapse, losing 5-1 to LASK Linz at Raiffeisen Arena to go out 5-4 on aggregate after leading 4-0 following the first leg. Callum McGregor’s early strike put the Hoops ahead before Samuel Adeniran’s extra-time double, either side of goals from Moses Usor, Robert Ljubicic and Florian Flecker, completed the turnaround; McGregor admitted, “We got what we deserved. I thought we were passive all night,” per Sky Sports (Aug 25). Celtic now drop into the Europa League group stage instead.

headline: India Tighten Grip on Colombo Test as Sri Lanka Fight Into Day 4 Under Rain Threat
body: India, having declared their first innings on 503/9, reduced Sri Lanka to 265/8 at stumps on a rain-hit Day 3 in Colombo, with Prasidh Krishna (3/47) and Manav Suthar (3/83) sharing six wickets; Sonal Dinusha stood unbeaten on 85 as the hosts trail by 238, still 39 short of avoiding the follow-on, per WION (Aug 25). Sri Lanka’s Prabath Jayasuriya was also handed an ICC reprimand and a demerit point for striking the boundary boards after being given lbw on Day 2, while Colombo faces a 97% chance of rain disrupting Day 4 of the series decider, per Prokerala (Aug 25).

headline: Babar Azam Puts in High-Intent Net Session at Lord’s Ahead of Comeback Test
body: Pakistan captain Babar Azam trained hard in an intense indoor net session at Lord’s on Tuesday, a positive sign for his recovery from the middle-finger injury that ruled him out of the innings-and-103-run defeat at Headingley under stand-in skipper Salman Ali Agha, per Yardbarker (Aug 25). Babar averages 65.75 across four Tests on English soil, and his return would be a significant boost as Pakistan look to level the series at Lord’s from Thursday.

headline: Norris Emerges as Antonelli’s Chief Title Threat After Second Straight Zandvoort Win
body: Lando Norris passed championship leader Kimi Antonelli on track to win the Dutch Grand Prix, his second consecutive victory, cutting Antonelli’s lead to 59 points over both Mercedes’ George Russell and Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton, with Norris himself now 83 back in fourth; “I feel like I’m doing a better job than everyone, and I think that can make a difference,” Norris said, per Sky Sports (Aug 24). McLaren boss Andrea Stella said Norris was “driving and operating at a very high level… in relation to a Formula 1 world champion,” while Antonelli conceded, “We’re clearly not the fastest car anymore on the grid.”

headline: Oil Slides to One-Week Low as Traders Shrug Off New Iran Sanctions
body: Oil prices tumbled to a one-week low on Tuesday as traders concluded Washington’s newly unveiled sanctions on Iran amount to economic pressure rather than a decisive escalation. Brent crude slid more than 3% to around $89 a barrel and WTI fell a similar margin to near $82, both the softest levels since mid-August, per Quartz (Aug 25). Saxo Bank’s Ole Hansen said the shift “from active military confrontation to economic coercion” had calmed nerves, while strategists at BBH called the sanctions package “more of a warning shot than a decisive blow”; only two vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, the lowest daily count since early May.

headline: Gold Extends Rally to Three-Month High Ahead of Jackson Hole
body: Gold pushed to a fresh three-month high on Tuesday, with spot prices opening at $4,710.10 an ounce before easing to about $4,697.60, up 6.7% over the past week and nearly 40% over the past year, per Yahoo Finance (Aug 25). The rally is being driven by a weaker dollar, expanded U.S. Treasury bond buyback plans and Middle East tensions, with investors now eyeing Friday’s PCE inflation report and Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s first Jackson Hole address as chair. Darrell Fletcher of Bannockburn Capital Markets cautioned that “buying high to hope for short-term higher is a tough strategy,” while B2PRIME’s Alex Tsepaev said gold “should not be seen as a driver of supercharged returns — it’s there to act primarily as a stabilizer.”

headline: Bitcoin Briefly Tops $80,000 Before Pulling Back
body: Bitcoin broke above $80,000 for the first time since May on Tuesday, touching an intraday high of $81,160 before slipping back to around $78,624, still up nearly 22% for the week, per The Motley Fool (Aug 25). The move builds on Monday’s rebound, when CoinShares’ James Butterfill described the surge as “a macro story, not a crypto one,” tied to softer inflation and reduced rate-hike bets, and flagged “$80,000 as an important upper boundary” for the token, per Yahoo Finance (Aug 24). Traders are now watching Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s Jackson Hole speech and possible Senate crypto legislation in September for the next catalyst.

headline: Wall Street Braces for Nvidia Earnings Due After the Bell
body: Wall Street is bracing for Nvidia’s fiscal second-quarter earnings, due after Wednesday’s close, with analysts forecasting revenue of $92.18 billion (97% growth) and adjusted EPS of $2.09 (99% growth) against Nvidia’s own guidance of $91 billion and $2.04, per The Motley Fool (Aug 26). Nvidia shares — which had posted seven straight daily losses — rose 2.19% to $213.05 ahead of the report, leaving the company’s market cap near $5.0 trillion; it has beaten estimates in 22 of its last 24 quarters. Chip stocks broadly dragged on Tuesday’s session as investors awaited the results, per Yahoo Finance (Aug 25).

headline: Anthropic Investors Target $2 Trillion IPO as Fable 5 Spending Stalls
body: Anthropic’s investors are pushing for a $2 trillion valuation in an October IPO that would eclipse SpaceX’s $1.77 trillion June listing as the largest ever, with annualized revenue reaching $65 billion by late July — up from $9 billion at the end of 2025 — and backers projecting $190–200 billion by 2028, per 24/7 Wall St (Aug 24) citing Financial Times reporting. A red flag has emerged: Anthropic’s flagship Fable 5 model has “plateaued at only about 11% of spending on Anthropic’s tools” more than two months after launch, with the cheaper Opus 5 quickly overtaking it in corporate spend. The S-1 is expected to be filed by end of August, putting Anthropic in a head-to-head race with OpenAI — which is separately eyeing its own $1 trillion IPO — to go public first.

headline: Taiwan Indicts Nine, Including Nvidia Manager, Over B300 Smuggling to China
body: Taiwan’s Keelung District Prosecutors indicted nine people — including an Nvidia Taiwan manager and Super Micro employees — over a scheme that funneled Nvidia B300 AI GPU servers to China via Indonesia, Japan and Hong Kong, netting the group $21.21 million in profit, per Tom’s Hardware (Aug 24). Of 130 servers ordered, 74 had already shipped — 16 direct to China, 50 via Indonesia, 8 via Japan to Hong Kong — with the ring, dubbed Flying Tiger Tech, allegedly using fake lease and export-permit paperwork plus inside accomplices at Nvidia Taiwan and Supermicro to clear customs. Defendants face up to five years for export violations and six years on embezzlement charges, the latest sign of persistent gaps in enforcement of U.S.-driven chip export controls.

headline: XPeng’s Robotics Arm Raises $900M+ at $6.3B Valuation for Humanoid Push
body: XPeng’s robotics unit raised over $900 million in a share-purchase round at a post-money valuation above $6.3 billion, led by IDG Capital with Gaorong Ventures and strategic backing from Tencent and Alibaba, the company announced (per TechNode, Aug 25). The capital will fund mass production of XPeng’s IRON humanoid robot by the end of 2026, with commercial deployments targeted for 2027, as Chinese tech giants race to stake claims in “physical AI.”

headline: Robotics Startup Generalist Triples to $3B Valuation in New $200M Round
body: Robotics startup Generalist has raised roughly $200 million led by 8VC at a $3 billion valuation, tripling from the $2 billion mark set in its June Series B (led by Radical Ventures, backed by Nvidia, Union Square Ventures, Bezos Expeditions and Fei-Fei Li), per TechCrunch (Aug 26). Founded in 2024 by ex-Google DeepMind researchers Pete Florence and Andy Zeng plus former Boston Dynamics engineer Andrew Barry, the company recently released its Gen 1.5 foundation model, which lets robots learn new tasks from video demonstrations as short as three to twelve seconds — the latest sign investors keep pouring capital into “physical AI” despite neither Generalist nor 8VC commenting on the raise.

headline: OpenAI Pushes AI Agents Beyond Coding Into White-Collar Work
body: OpenAI is extending AI agents beyond coding into accounting, investing and medicine, wrapping its agentic Codex engine into a friendlier interface it calls a “harness” inside the $20/month ChatGPT Work tier, per TechCrunch’s interview with product lead Thibault Sottiaux (Aug 24). While 98% of OpenAI’s own staff use Codex, outside adoption lags — just 17% of organizational subscribers and under 1% of individual subscribers have taken it up, with the combined Codex/ChatGPT Work app reaching about 20 million people versus ChatGPT’s 1 billion-plus users. “ChatGPT can actually do entire, very complicated tasks for you all autonomously in a way that is delightful and safe,” Sottiaux said, while engineering lead Joe Gershenson added the goal is “to be more precise about what information the model really needs.”

headline: US Strikes Syria From Terror List as Mossad Chief Meets Damascus’s Top Diplomat
body: Washington removed Syria from its state sponsors of terrorism list after 47 years, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent saying “Treasury is following through on President Trump’s promise to give the Syrian people a chance at greatness,” per The National (Aug 25). The move followed Sunday’s US-brokered meeting in Amman between Mossad chief Roman Gofman and Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad Al Shibani, where Damascus demanded an Israeli withdrawal from the nine military posts it has set up near the Golan Heights since Assad’s fall, with envoy Tom Barrack pushing both sides toward a formal peace treaty.

headline: Iran-Pakistan Talks Aim to Ease Hormuz Crisis After New Tanker Attack
body: A projectile strike disabled an oil tanker’s engine off Oman’s coast in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday night, British maritime authorities confirmed, with the crew unharmed but no group claiming responsibility — the latest hit in a waterway carrying roughly a fifth of the world’s traded oil since the February 28 US-Israel strikes on Iran. A day later, Pakistan’s Army Chief Field Marshal Asim Munir led a delegation to Tehran, meeting Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in what Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi called “very positive and productive” talks aimed at reopening the strait and reviving US-Iran negotiations, per Spectrum News (Aug 25).

headline: Washington Locks In Sept. 24 Xi Summit Date as 7.5% China Tariff Takes Shape
body: The Trump administration is finalizing a 7.5% “overcapacity” tariff on Chinese goods — which would push total China duties to roughly 20% — timed to land before a Xi-Trump summit now set for September 24 in Washington, per Business Today (Aug 25). The tariff is meant to avoid derailing the countries’ one-year trade truce, which expires November 10, while a Section 301 probe into Chinese manufacturing overcapacity is expected to be released before the summit; China’s Washington embassy responded that “economic and trade issues should be resolved through bilateral talks,” disputing the overcapacity claims.

headline: Russia Pitches North Korea a Five-Year Military Pact as China Watches Warily
body: Russian Defense Minister Andrei Belousov, visiting Pyongyang, announced a proposed 2027-2031 military cooperation framework covering “arms transfers, technology sharing, joint training, and personnel exchanges,” saying “we have reached an agreement with the DPRK Defense Ministry to place our military cooperation on a sustainable, long-term footing,” per HNGN (Aug 25). Moscow has already received at least 150 North Korean KN-23/KN-24 ballistic missiles and millions of artillery shells, with 50,000 more troops possibly to be requested at a September summit — a deepening alliance that has pushed Beijing to break from past practice by putting military affairs on Xi Jinping’s own Pyongyang summit agenda for the first time.

headline: Over 50 Nations Press Russia for Ceasefire as Ukraine Toll Hits Wartime High
body: More than 50 UN member states, including the UK, France, Germany, Japan and Canada, issued a joint call on Ukraine’s Independence Day for Russia to accept an unconditional ceasefire, with Danish Foreign Minister Lars Loekke Rasmussen declaring “Ukraine wants peace. We want peace,” and urging Moscow to “resume talks for a comprehensive, just and lasting peace,” per The National (Aug 24). Ukraine’s UN ambassador Andrii Melnyk pressed allies over stalled air-defense transfers, asking why “missiles capable of saving hundreds of lives every day are being kept in stowages,” as the statement cited July’s 437 civilian deaths — the deadliest month since March 2022 — and more than 68,000 civilians killed or wounded since the war began.

headline: Nvidia’s Earnings Tonight Double as a Referendum on the AI Trade
body: Nvidia reports fiscal second-quarter results after today’s close, with Wall Street modeling revenue surging roughly 97% year-over-year to just over $92 billion, per The Motley Fool (Aug 25). The company has topped per-share estimates in each of its last eleven quarters, and the print is being watched as a bellwether for the broader AI-infrastructure trade that is also moving CrowdStrike, Oracle and other names into this week’s earnings cycle.

headline: CrowdStrike Heads Into Today’s Print on an Eight-Quarter Beat Streak
body: CrowdStrike also reports fiscal second-quarter results today, coming off a quarter in which annual recurring revenue reached $5.51 billion and management raised net-new ARR growth guidance to a 27.7% midpoint, per 24/7 Wall St (Aug 24). Prediction markets assign roughly an 89% probability to another earnings beat, and Wall Street coverage skews heavily bullish at 41 buy ratings against a single sell.

headline: Zoom Beats on Fiscal Q2 and Raises Full-Year Guidance
body: Zoom Communications reported fiscal second-quarter revenue of $1.277 billion, up 4.9% year-over-year, with enterprise revenue up 7.8% and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $1.55 versus $1.53 a year earlier, per StockTitan (Aug 25). Management guided full-year revenue to $5.085-$5.095 billion and non-GAAP EPS to $6.08-$6.12, and UBS and HSBC both lifted their price targets afterward, to $115 and $133 respectively.

headline: CASGEVY’s Approval Expands to Young Children as Analysts Lift CRISPR Therapeutics Targets
body: The FDA expanded CASGEVY’s approval on August 3 to children as young as two with sickle cell disease or transfusion-dependent beta thalassemia, a decision CEO Samarth Kulkarni said came just 53 days after filing and opens eligibility to roughly 5,500 additional patients, per the company’s investor release. CASGEVY generated $76 million in second-quarter revenue, up 78% from the prior quarter, and Citi followed with a price-target increase to $88 citing the CASGEVY revenue beat, with Goldman Sachs and Bank of America also revising their targets.

headline: Rackspace Launches a Multitenant Cloud Platform Aimed at AI Inference Workloads
body: Rackspace Technology unveiled Rackspace Cloud, which it describes as among the first fully managed multitenant platforms built on Broadcom’s VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1, launching first in Dallas with North Virginia and Chicago to follow, per the company’s release (Aug 25). The pitch leans on Broadcom research finding 56% of organizations now run or plan production AI inferencing in private clouds, even as public-cloud inference usage has fallen from 56% to 41% year-over-year.

headline: Oracle Trades With the AI-Infrastructure Complex Ahead of Nvidia’s Earnings
body: No Oracle-specific announcement was dated to today’s session; shares moved with the broader AI-infrastructure group as investors positioned ahead of Nvidia’s earnings later today. Oracle’s most recent concrete news was Oracle Health’s August 19 expansion of its Clinical AI Agent, adding automated coding, dictation and chart-review capabilities, part of the same enterprise-AI narrative underpinning this week’s swings across cloud and semiconductor names.

headline: Editas Rides Gene-Editing Sector Strength With No Company-Specific Trigger
body: No Editas-specific news was dated to today’s session; the move looks like sector read-across from CRISPR Therapeutics’ CASGEVY-driven rally in the same gene-editing group. Editas’ most recent update, on August 5, reported cash of $211.6 million extending its runway into the second half of 2028, alongside preclinical data for EDIT-401 showing roughly 90% mean reductions in LDL cholesterol markers in non-human primates.

headline: Coeur Mining Moves With the Silver Market; No Fresh Catalyst Identified
body: No new Coeur Mining announcement was found for the session. The company’s most recent concrete update was its August 5 second-quarter report, which posted record revenue of $1.085 billion and record adjusted EBITDA of $478 million on record gold output, against adjusted EPS of $0.12, and management initiated $121 million of share repurchases plus an inaugural $0.02-per-share dividend. Coeur remains highly sensitive to swings in spot gold and silver prices, which the company itself noted had pulled back into quarter-end.

headline: Doval-Wang Yi Talks: China’s Top Diplomat Calls India a Partner, Not a Rival
body: India’s National Security Advisor Ajit Doval met Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in Beijing for the 25th round of Special Representatives talks on the boundary question, with the 26th round now set for India in 2027. Wang Yi told Doval, “China and India are important neighbours and representatives of major developing countries,” while Doval said the two nations “are both ancient civilizations, populous nations, and important economies, and are partners, not competitors,” adding that ties “have returned to the right track” with border areas maintaining “overall peace.” Both sides reaffirmed the 2005 political guiding principles for settling the border dispute, per WION (Aug 25).

headline: Pulwama Encounter: Two Terror Associates Held, Pistol and Grenade Seized
body: Security forces arrested two suspected terror associates, identified as Latif Ahmed Deedad and Aejaz Ahmed Bajad, during an overnight cordon-and-search operation in the Yarwan forest area of Rajpora in south Kashmir’s Pulwama district on August 24-25. The joint operation by J&K Police’s Special Operations Group, 44 Rashtriya Rifles and the CRPF’s 183 Battalion recovered a pistol, 12 rounds of ammunition and a hand grenade after intercepting the pair moving from the forest toward CB Nath village; police have registered an FIR under the Arms Act and UAPA and are probing their weapon sources and contacts, per WION (Aug 25).

headline: Tamil Nadu Scraps Rs 20,000-Crore Chennai Second Airport After Farmer Protests
body: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay cancelled the Rs 20,000-crore ($2.4 billion) greenfield airport planned for Parandur in Kancheepuram district — first announced in August 2022 to handle 100 million passengers a year — after sustained farmer protests over land loss and damage to local water bodies. “Farmers are the backbone of the nation,” Vijay said, announcing that Meenambakkam airport will instead be expanded, with capacity reaching “55 million passengers per year” once the new Terminal 5 opens, while alternative sites for a future airport are identified, per WION (Aug 24).

headline: 17 Arrested as Police Link Fatal A66 Crash Near Middlesbrough to Organised Crime
body: Cleveland Police have arrested 17 people — 12 on Monday and five more on Tuesday — after a Volkswagen Passat fleeing officers drove the wrong way on the A66 and collided head-on with a marked police car, killing seven people including officers Matthew Blades, 37, and Tom Clough, 38, per Courthouse News (Aug 25). Assistant Chief Constable Wayne Fox said “this has been a fast moving and complex investigation, with significant links to serious and organised criminal activity,” noting officers had been pursuing a car with cloned number plates before abandoning the chase seconds before impact. The five other victims were all aged 17 to 23, and the case has since been referred to the police watchdog.

headline: Care Leavers Four Times More Likely to Die Young, Report Finds
body: A new report found young adults who left the UK care system are four times more likely to die between the ages of 18 and 24 than their peers, recording 112 deaths in this age group in 2025, including 22 at age 18 alone, per ITV News (Aug 25). Co-lead Ashley John-Baptiste called it a “national tragedy that so many care-experienced young people are dying so early in life,” adding that “these young lives ended far too soon.” Roughly a third of the deaths were attributed to suicide, a rate the report said could be five times higher than in the general population, blaming the loss of support networks the moment care leavers turn 18.

headline: Government Unveils Nearly £10bn for Councils to Build Affordable Homes
body: Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s government allocated almost £10 billion to councils and housing associations to build over 70,000 homes across England, part of a wider £39 billion social and affordable homes programme, per ITV News (Aug 24). Burnham said “no child should be raised in a hostel room and no family should wait 10 years for a front door,” while Housing Secretary Angela Rayner said “families can’t be left raising children without a place to call home.” Sixty percent of the new homes will be for social rent, with almost 180,000 children currently without a permanent home and regions including Greater Manchester (4,400 homes, £529m) and West Yorkshire (4,000 homes, £441m) among the biggest recipients.

headline: Around 140 Vehicles Destroyed in ‘Complex’ Car Park Fire Near Gatwick
body: A blaze at a business park in Rowfant, roughly eight miles from Gatwick Airport, destroyed approximately 140 vehicles after breaking out in a workshop on Saturday night, per ITV News (Aug 24). West Sussex Fire and Rescue Service said “this has been a complex fire involving a workshop and a significant number of vehicles and cylinders,” with crews still working to “conclude firefighting operations” days later. The fire cut power to 2,133 businesses and homes, with 57 properties still without electricity until 8:05am the next morning; a 67-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of arson and later released on bail, with no casualties reported.

headline: Qatar Condemns Israeli Defense Minister’s Incursion Into Syrian Territory
body: Qatar’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a strong condemnation of Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz’s unauthorized entry into Syrian territory, calling it a violation of Syria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. The ministry “called on the international community to move swiftly to compel the Israeli occupation to adhere to international legitimacy,” citing the 1974 disengagement agreement, and reaffirmed Doha’s full support for Syria’s sovereignty, independence and stability, per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 25).

headline: Trump Sends Saudi Civil Nuclear Deal to Congress, Ties It to Israel Recognition
body: The Trump administration formally submitted its civil nuclear cooperation agreement with Saudi Arabia to Congress on Monday, a 30-year pact worth tens of billions that would let U.S. firms build AP1000 reactors in the kingdom and let lawmakers review it for 90 session days before it can take effect. A U.S. administration official said “the agreement will only move forward if Saudi Arabia joins the Abraham Accords,” with critics noting the deal lacks the enrichment and reprocessing curbs the UAE accepted in its 2009 “gold standard” nuclear pact, per Al-Monitor (Aug 25).

headline: Qatar and Turkiye Deepen Trade and Investment Ties in Ankara Talks
body: Qatar’s Minister of State for Foreign Trade Affairs Dr Ahmad bin Mohammed Al Sayed held separate meetings in Ankara with Turkiye’s Trade Minister Omer Bolat and Treasury and Finance Minister Mehmet Simsek to expand bilateral trade, investment cooperation and supply-chain resilience, building on the two countries’ Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement implemented last year. Delegations on both sides, including Qatar’s ambassador to Turkiye and the Chairman of the General Authority of Customs, discussed strengthening business-community partnerships between the two nations, per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 25).

headline: Qatar Take on China in FIBA World Cup Qualifier
body: Qatar’s national basketball team faces China at Al Janoub Stadium on August 27 in a FIBA Basketball World Cup 2027 Asian Qualifiers fixture, per Qatar Living (Aug 23). The match is part of Qatar’s qualifying campaign and gives fans a chance to watch international-level basketball at the Al Wakrah venue.

headline: Doha Trade Fair Opens at DECC
body: The Doha Trade Fair runs August 24 through September 4 at the Doha Exhibition & Convention Center, bringing together a wide range of vendors and unique products under one roof, per Qatar Living (Aug 23). It’s billed as a shopping destination spanning multiple sectors, making it a good pick for browsing through the coming week.

headline: Rouda Al Malki Fashion Exhibition at QNCC
body: A curated pop-up exhibition from designer Rouda Al Malki runs August 28 to September 2 at the Qatar National Convention Center, showcasing women’s fashion, lifestyle products and everyday essentials, per Qatar Living (Aug 23). The multi-day event gives shoppers a browsing-friendly setting to discover new local and regional labels.

headline: ORBIT Arabian Night With Cheba Souad
body: ORBIT Arabian Night brings Algerian Raï star Cheba Souad to the Cielo Hotel in Lusail on August 28 for a live music performance, per Qatar Living (Aug 23). The evening promises a night of North African–inspired sound at one of Lusail’s hotel venues.

headline: Kids’ Gardening Workshops at National Museum
body: The National Museum of Qatar hosts hands-on gardening workshops for children on August 27, run by Hadiiqa and covering STEAM topics such as microgreens, seed mosaics and hydroponics, per Qatar Living (Aug 23). It’s a family-friendly, educational session aimed at getting kids curious about sustainable growing methods.

headline: The US removed Syria from its terror list after 47 years and tied the move to Damascus joining the Abraham Accords, hours after Pakistan’s army chief flew to Tehran for “very positive” talks aimed at reopening the Strait of Hormuz following a fresh tanker attack near Oman.

Colombia’s earthquake death toll climbed to 331 and Indonesia’s Flores quake toll passed 100, while Manila’s flood-driven leptospirosis outbreak topped 3,000 cases amid fury over a $32.4 billion flood-control scandal.

Anthropic is chasing a $2 trillion IPO even as its flagship Fable 5 model has plateaued at just 11% of enterprise AI spending, while Taiwan indicted nine people, including an Nvidia manager, over a $21 million scheme smuggling Nvidia B300 chips to China.
Nvidia reports earnings after today’s close as gold hit a three-month high, bitcoin briefly topped $80,000 and oil slid to a one-week low on doubts that new Iran sanctions will actually escalate.

Celtic blew a four-goal aggregate lead to crash out of the Champions League to LASK Linz, while Lando Norris’s second straight win at Zandvoort cut Kimi Antonelli’s F1 title lead as Pakistan’s Babar Azam trained hard ahead of an expected Lord’s return.
Congo’s Ebola Outbreak Posts Its Deadliest Week Yet
body: DR Congo recorded 317 Ebola deaths in the past week, one of the highest weekly tolls of the epidemic, pushing the total to 5,514 cases and 2,642 deaths with a 47.9% fatality rate (68.6% in hard-hit North Kivu), per ABC News (Aug 24). Congolese experts believe the true toll may be roughly three times the reported figures; the country received over 16,000 doses of the Ervebo vaccine on Friday, though its effectiveness against this Bundibugyo strain is unproven, and one resident said, “We are fed up with recording new cases of Ebola every day.”

headline: Philippine Floods Displace Over a Million, Damage 1,600 Schools
