body: Torrential monsoon rains and three tropical cyclones (Luis, Maymay, Neneng) have affected 1.01 million people in Pampanga province alone, damaging 1,616 schools and 9,597 classrooms nationwide and displacing 9,068 families into shelters, per Philstar (Aug 25). President Marcos pushed back on blaming flood-control failures alone, saying “we need to understand that this is not solely due to issues with the flood control project, but also the torrential rain,” as repair costs are estimated at P2.6 billion.

headline: Tokayev-Aligned Party Sweeps Kazakhstan’s Revamped Parliament
body: Kazakhstan’s newly formed Adilet party, led by President Tokayev’s top aides, won over 71% of the vote on 74% turnout in elections for a new 145-seat single-chamber parliament, per Al Jazeera (Aug 24). The vote followed a 2026 constitutional overhaul consolidating the legislature from two chambers into one; Tokayev, 73, said it was “too early to say” whether he’d seek another term, and announced he will name a newly created vice-president post within 7-10 days.

headline: Twin Earthquakes Rattle Tokyo and Hokkaido, Injuring Dozens
body: A magnitude-5.9 quake struck southern Ibaraki near Tokyo at 2am local time on Aug 23, injuring at least 37 people across five prefectures, followed the same night by a magnitude-6.0 quake off Hokkaido’s Urakawa coast with no reported injuries, per Tech Times (Aug 24). Japan’s Meteorological Agency confirmed no tsunami risk from either event; the first quake ruptured a water main and knocked out power to about 460 Tokyo homes, since restored.

headline: Jurel’s Century Powers India to Command in Colombo
body: India declared their first innings at 503/9 after Dhruv Jurel struck a maiden Test century from No.7 (100 off 171 balls), following Rishabh Pant’s 63, before Prasidh Krishna and Manav Suthar struck twice inside Sri Lanka’s reply to leave the hosts 8/2 at stumps, per Outlook India (Aug 24). The declaration extends India’s grip on the series-deciding second Test at Colombo’s SSC ground, a day after Padikkal’s century set the platform.

headline: Babar Azam Set to Return for Pakistan at Lord’s
body: Pakistan captain Babar Azam is set to return from a finger injury for the second Test against England at Lord’s, with opener Azan Awais — who managed a duck and 9 in the first Test — expected to make way, per Business Recorder (Aug 23). Stand-in skipper Salman Ali Agha said he would be “happy to hand over the captaincy” to Babar, as Pakistan also considers two frontline spinners and young quick Ubaid Shah after a heavy innings-and-120-run defeat at Headingley.

headline: Verstappen Explains What Caused His Zandvoort Crash
body: Max Verstappen said the car “snapped and I couldn’t catch it” as he explained the Lap 1 crash that ended his home race, adding he retreated to Red Bull’s motorhome afterward just to “watch the race for a bit,” per Yahoo Sports (Aug 24). The Dutchman conceded the error was ultimately his own, capping a “disappointing” farewell weekend at Zandvoort that Lando Norris turned into a victory.

headline: Celtic Chase Champions League Progress in Linz
body: Celtic carry a commanding 3-0 aggregate lead into today’s Champions League play-off second leg away to LASK in Linz, needing only to avoid a heavy defeat to reach the league phase for a second straight season, per Celtic News Now (Aug 24). Wednesday brings a tighter contest as Fenerbahce, featuring Romelu Lukaku, host Lyon after a 1-1 first-leg draw — the last of this week’s seven play-off ties before Thursday’s league-phase draw in Monaco.

headline: Oil Stabilizes After Iran Sanctions Rollout, Tanker Incident Near Oman
body: Brent crude held near $92.16 a barrel and WTI at $85.02 on Tuesday, steadying after both benchmarks slid more than 2% Monday as the US, led by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, rolled out expanded sanctions targeting Iran’s economy, per Business Standard (Aug 25). The US Strategic Petroleum Reserve has fallen to 289.7 million barrels, its lowest since November 1982, adding to supply concerns as the Hormuz standoff continues (see Geopolitics).

headline: Bitcoin Stalls Near $80,000 as Traders Cash In Record Profits
body: Bitcoin is consolidating after last week’s 23% surge — its strongest weekly rally since March 2023 — as holders realized $1.72 billion in profits on Friday alone, the highest level since November 2024, per FXStreet (Aug 24). Spot bitcoin ETFs still pulled in $1.92 billion of inflows for the week, the best of 2026, but an overbought RSI near 79 points to a possible pullback before another run at the $80,000 mark.

headline: Gold Hits 15-Week High as Dollar Weakens, Yields Stabilize
body: Gold futures touched $4,738.50 and spot gold hit $4,679 on Monday, both 15-week highs, extending a rally that has added roughly 5% over three straight weekly gains, per Forbes (Aug 24). The move follows a Treasury Department plan to boost buybacks of long-dated government debt plus a weaker dollar and steadying yields; ActivTrades’ Ricardo Evangelista said further gains “depend to a large extent on the U.S. dollar remaining under pressure and Treasury yields stabilizing,” while silver held near two-month highs around $69.

headline: Chip Stocks Drag Wall Street Lower Ahead of Nvidia Earnings
body: The Nasdaq fell as much as 0.38% and the S&P 500 dipped 0.18% Monday as semiconductor stocks slid — the Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index dropped 2.64% to a three-week low — even as the Dow edged up 0.28% to 53,423.60, per the Associated Press via the Spokesman-Review (Aug 24). Markets are bracing for Nvidia’s Wednesday earnings as a bellwether for the AI trade, Wednesday’s PCE inflation report, and this week’s Jackson Hole symposium (Aug 27-29), where Fed Chair Kevin Warsh delivers his first keynote with 30-year Treasury yields still above 5%.

headline: Nvidia Pays $6 Billion to License Poolside’s AI Model Software
body: Nvidia is spending $6 billion to license Poolside’s “Model Factory” software plus another $1 billion for equity, valuing the startup at $12 billion, per Forbes (Aug 24). Poolside had failed to close a $2 billion funding round four months earlier and lost access to a 40,000 GB300-chip cluster as a result; Nvidia is folding the tech into its Nemotron open-weight family as a US rival to DeepSeek, Kimi K3 and Qwen, extending its CUDA-style playbook of giving away models to drive hardware demand.

headline: OpenAI Eyes $1 Trillion IPO as Altman Admits Timeline Was Wrong
body: OpenAI is pursuing a public listing valued at up to $1 trillion after filing a confidential S-1 in May, with $40 billion in annualized revenue as of Aug 14 but a projected $14 billion loss for 2026 and breakeven not expected until 2030, per Tech Times (Aug 24). Sam Altman admitted his post-GPT-4 disruption timeline was flawed, saying the gap between what AI can do and what businesses actually deploy “may represent a permanent feature” of the technology rather than a temporary lag; prediction markets give the IPO only a 19% chance of closing before year-end.

headline: Hugging Face Explores Sale at $13 Billion-Plus Valuation
body: AI model-hosting hub Hugging Face is reportedly in talks to be acquired for roughly $13 billion or more and has enlisted bankers to field bids, per TechCrunch (Aug 24), though no buyer has been identified and no deal is final. The company last raised at a $4.5 billion valuation in 2023 and had previously turned down a $500 million Nvidia investment that would have valued it at $7 billion; CEO Clem Delangue said the platform carries a “long-term responsibility” to the community whose models and data it hosts.

headline: Nvidia in Talks to Back Perplexity at $30 Billion-Plus Valuation
body: Nvidia is discussing an investment in Perplexity at a valuation exceeding $30 billion, up from $20 billion last September, per Benzinga (Aug 24, citing The Information). Perplexity’s annualized revenue has jumped to over $750 million from under $250 million at the start of 2026, and it separately signed a $750 million Azure deal with Microsoft; CEO Aravind Srinivas said the company still plans an IPO in 2028 regardless of how OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s listings go.

headline: Alibaba Launches Wan3.0 Video Model After $10B Funding Push
body: Days after its record $10.2 billion Hong Kong share sale for AI buildout, Alibaba Cloud officially launched Wan3.0, a video-generation model producing clips up to 30 seconds and accepting DOC, XLS, PPT, PDF and Markdown files as inputs, per TechNode (Aug 24). The model brings improved instruction-following, shot consistency and audio quality, and Alibaba is offering a 30% API pricing discount on select platforms through September 23 as it positions Wan3.0 against Google’s Veo.

headline: Iran Sanctions Bite as Oil Tanker Struck Near Oman
body: The US Treasury’s “economic D-Day” campaign against Iran gained fresh urgency as an unidentified projectile struck a tanker near Oman on Tuesday, per Business Standard/Reuters (Aug 25). Iran has threatened fines and detention for 45 tankers it says are violating new Hormuz transit rules; Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent vowed to “sever every economic lifeline that sustains this tyrannical regime until Tehran stands alone,” targeting digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping and roughly 60 entities and vessels, per Al Jazeera (Aug 24).

headline: Putin Moves to Seize Russian Infrastructure Hit by Ukraine Drones
body: Vladimir Putin signed a decree letting Moscow temporarily seize energy, nuclear, industrial, and transport facilities deemed too slow to repair after Ukraine’s intensifying drone campaign, per Al Jazeera (Aug 24). Retail giants Wildberries and Ozon have together lost dozens of warehouses to strikes, the Perm oil refinery has halted operations, and fuel shortages have spread across several Russian regions — following Putin’s warning that Kyiv had opened a “Pandora’s box” by striking Russian economic targets.

headline: US Brokers Syria-Israel Talks in Jordan to Defuse Border Tensions
body: Syria’s Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani met Mossad chief Roman Gofman in US-mediated talks in Jordan aimed at halting Israeli strikes and reviving a security agreement, per Al Jazeera (Aug 24). The talks followed an Israeli strike on a Syrian airbase near the Turkish border; Israel is pushing to keep Turkish forces out of Syria and the Golan demilitarized, while Damascus is seeking an Israeli withdrawal to pre-December 2024 positions and restoration of the 1974 disengagement pact.

headline: US Eyes 7.5% China Tariff Ahead of September Xi-Trump Summit
body: The US is preparing a 7.5% tariff on Chinese goods over industrial “overcapacity,” which would push total US duties on China to roughly 20% — the level Beijing accepted under the current truce — ahead of a Trump-Xi summit set for September 24 in Washington, per Bloomberg via WION (Aug 25). The move stems from a Section 301 investigation into trading partners’ excess capacity launched in March, with both sides also racing to extend their trade truce before it expires November 10.

headline: Tesla Recalls Nearly 3 Million Vehicles in China Over Door Handles
body: Chinese regulators required Tesla to recall nearly 3 million Model 3, Y, S, and X vehicles — part of a record wave topping 4 million EVs that also swept in Xiaomi, Leapmotor, Xpeng, and Geely — to fix electronic door handles Tesla said could be difficult to operate after a severe collision knocks out the low-voltage system, alongside an over-the-air driver-monitoring update. China is banning concealed door handles on new EVs from 2027, with existing approved models given until 2029 to comply. Tesla is separately guiding 2026 capital expenditure above $25 billion for AI and autonomy projects including the Cybercab robotaxi, per The Motley Fool and TradingKey (Aug 24).

headline: Intel Upsizes Secondary Offering to $20 Billion, BofA Cuts Price Target
body: Intel priced an upsized secondary offering of 210.5 million shares, raising $20 billion for capital expenditure and working capital — roughly a third larger than the original $15 billion plan. Bank of America analyst Vivek Arya cut his price target to $145 from $160, citing 4-5% EPS dilution from the offering, even as CEO Lip-Bu Tan and a family member purchased $12 million of shares on the open market, per Benzinga and StocksToTrade (Aug 24).

headline: S&P Cuts Oracle’s Credit Rating as AI Data-Center Capex Strains Cash Flow
body: S&P Global downgraded Oracle’s credit rating to BBB-, citing long-term debt exceeding $122 billion and leverage approaching 5x EBITDA. The company’s AI data-center buildout has pushed capital expenditure above $55 billion and free cash flow to negative $23.7 billion, raising questions about converting its $638 billion order backlog into revenue amid reported delays in utility infrastructure for major data-center projects. Analysts have largely kept Buy ratings, with an average price target of $252.87, per TradingKey (Aug 24).

headline: Nvidia Slides Into Wednesday’s Earnings Amid Sector-Wide Chip Caution
body: No fresh company-specific announcement was found for Nvidia; the move tracked broader semiconductor-sector caution as investors trimmed risk ahead of its earnings report due Wednesday, August 26. The sector was further pressured after a Chinese memory-chip maker filed for an IPO, weighing on peers, and after reports that some Nvidia customers could face price increases of up to 15% amid a DRAM shortage. A broader rotation toward defensive names was reinforced by geopolitical headlines including the new Iran sanctions and stalled Canada-US tariff talks, per The Motley Fool (Aug 24).

headline: Cloudflare Prices $2.5 Billion Convertible Notes as Insiders Sell
body: Cloudflare completed a $2.5 billion offering of 0% convertible senior notes due 2031, raising dilution concerns among investors. The move coincided with open-market share sales by the company’s CFO and Chief Legal Officer, and Zacks Research downgraded the stock to Hold, citing a forward EV-to-sales multiple above 40x. Second-quarter GAAP operating losses widened to $205.7 million as the company ramped capital spending on edge AI infrastructure, per TradingKey (Aug 24).

headline: Fastly Pressured as Frontier AI Labs’ IPO Plans Threaten to Draw Investor Capital
body: Fastly came under pressure after Bloomberg reported Anthropic is preparing to file for an IPO as soon as the end of August, at a valuation that could match or exceed SpaceX’s roughly $75 billion offering; Anthropic had already raised $65 billion in May at a $965 billion valuation and reported more than $11.5 billion in preliminary second-quarter revenue. OpenAI’s CFO also signaled a possible IPO by 2027, and the prospect of frontier AI labs going public has traders discussing rotating out of enterprise software names like Fastly and into the labs directly, per Yahoo Finance/StockStory (Aug 20).

headline: Rackspace Posts Wider Q2 Loss as Public Cloud Revenue Keeps Shrinking
body: Rackspace Technology reported Q2 2026 revenue of $670 million, up 0.6% year-over-year, as 5.5% growth in Private Cloud only partly offset a 2.3% decline in Public Cloud; the net loss widened to $67.5 million ($0.27 per diluted share) from $54.5 million a year earlier. For full-year 2026 the company guides to $2.45-$2.55 billion in revenue and $285-$295 million in adjusted EBITDA. Like fellow edge/cloud-infrastructure name Fastly, the stock has been caught up in investor rotation toward directly-listed AI labs and away from traditional enterprise software vendors, per Rackspace investor relations (Aug 10).

headline: Beyond Meat Completes 1-for-30 Reverse Split After Q2 Miss and Weak Q3 Outlook
body: Beyond Meat’s 1-for-30 reverse stock split, intended to regain compliance with Nasdaq’s minimum bid price rule, took effect following Q2 2026 results that showed an adjusted loss of $0.09 per share, an adjusted EBITDA loss of $27.7 million, revenue down 8.2% year-over-year, and sales volumes down 9.5%. Management guided to an 11% revenue decline for the third quarter, and the company separately amended its 2030 convertible notes to remove restrictions on share repurchases and exchanges, per Investing.com (Aug 11).

headline: Karnataka Suspends Amazon, Instamart, BigBasket Over Poisonous Datura Sale
body: Karnataka’s Food Safety Department suspended food licences for Amazon, Instamart, and BigBasket after finding poisonous datura fruits and seeds listed for sale under valid FSSAI licence numbers, per WION (Aug 25). Amazon did not respond to inquiries, Instamart sought more time, and BigBasket said it had already halted sales — regulators deemed all three responses unsatisfactory and suspended the licences pending hearings.

headline: 27 Children Fall Ill After Mid-Day Meal in Rajasthan, Days After Bihar Scare
body: At least 27 children at a government school in Kota, Rajasthan fell ill on August 24 after eating their mid-day meal, suffering vomiting, dizziness and headaches, per WION (Aug 25). District Education Officer Roop Singh Meena said “four children had already been admitted, and a medical team was sent to attend to the others,” days after a similar Bihar incident sickened 34-40 students.

headline: India’s Sugar Stocks Hit 52-Week Highs as Government Denies Ethanol Link
body: Sugar-linked stocks surged to 52-week highs on rising prices tied to lower domestic output and festive demand, with New Delhi insisting the shortage stems from disease and weather hitting sugarcane yields, not diversion to E20 ethanol blending, per WION (Aug 24). About 32% of ethanol still comes from sugarcane feedstock versus 68% from grains, and the government is allowing duty-free imports of 1 million tonnes of raw sugar through October 31.

headline: Gurmeet Ram Rahim Walks Out of Jail Again on 21-Day Furlough
body: Dera Sacha Sauda chief Gurmeet Ram Rahim, convicted of rape and murder, was released from Haryana’s Sunaria jail on a 21-day furlough — his 17th temporary release since 2020, per WION (Aug 25). Past releases have ranged from 12 hours to 50 days under Haryana’s Good Conduct Prisoners Act, which allows up to 70 days of parole and 21 days of furlough annually.

headline: No 10 Urges Social Media Firms to Pull ‘Reprehensible’ Dangerous Driving Videos
body: Downing Street pressed TikTok and other platforms to remove videos glorifying dangerous driving after a wrong-way crash on the A66 near Middlesbrough killed Pc Tom Clough, Pc Matthew Blades and five others, per ITV News (Aug 24). PM Andy Burnham said those promoting such content are “doing something that’s truly reprehensible,” with officials warning platforms must comply with Online Safety Act requirements.

headline: Treasury Launches Review of Business Rates for Pubs and Hotels
body: The Treasury opened an independent review into how business rates are valued for pubs and hotels, led by rates expert Jerry Schurder, after steep increases at the 2026 revaluation, per GOV.UK (Aug 24). It will report by March 2027 ahead of the 2029 revaluation, building on a 20% rates cut for pubs and live music venues due from April 2027; Financial Secretary James Murray said “pubs and hotels are vital for communities and bringing growth to every postcode.”

headline: Woman Admits Breaching Anonymity Order in Jeffrey Donaldson Abuse Case
body: Donna Toman, 55, of Ballynahinch pleaded guilty to breaching a lifetime anonymity order protecting a victim of former DUP leader Jeffrey Donaldson, who was convicted of 18 historical sexual offences, per ITV News (Aug 24). The breach stemmed from a social media post made on June 26, 2026; a district judge warned the offence carries up to six months in prison, with sentencing set for October 12.

headline: Reform UK Pledges to Prioritise British-Born Workers for Social Housing
body: Reform UK unveiled plans to prioritise British-born workers under 35, veterans, and married couples with children for social housing, alongside a pledge to build 50,000 affordable homes a year, per LocalGov (Aug 24). Deputy leader Richard Tice cited 1.3 million people on waiting lists, but Shelter’s Sarah Elliott called the plan “a blatant distraction from the real cause of the housing emergency.”

headline: Qatar-Brokered Roadmap Advances DR Congo Peace Framework
body: Qatar-mediated talks in Switzerland (Aug 17-21) between the DR Congo and the AFC/M23 rebel group produced a practical roadmap to implement the November 2025 Doha Peace Framework, including activating the Expanded Joint Verification Mechanism Plus and the DRC’s release of 15 detainees, per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 24). A Qatar University expert noted “the real test of any mediation is not the signing of the agreement, but the ability to turn it into implementable steps.”

headline: Qatar’s Foreign Investment Stock Rises to $47.3bn in Q1 2026
body: Qatar’s inward FDI stock climbed 3.3% to QR172.2bn ($47.3bn) in the first quarter of 2026, while outbound investment rose 3.5% to QR221.7bn ($60.9bn), per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 24). Mining and quarrying drew 45.3% of foreign investment and financial services 31.9%, with analyst Mohammed Sohail saying Qatar is “transforming from a regional consumer of tech solutions into an active incubator for fintech, data centers, and advanced logistics.”

headline: Qatar’s First Real Cool-Down Expected From September 20 as Suhail Season Continues
body: Qatar Calendar House’s Dr Faisal Al Ansari said temperatures will noticeably decline starting September 20, roughly 26 days into the 53-day, four-phase Suhail season that began this week, per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 24). The transition also brings equal day/night length, improved planting conditions, and shifting fish behaviour as the region heads toward autumn.

headline: Tanker Set Ablaze Off Saudi Arabia After Strike by ‘Unknown Projectile’
body: A tanker caught fire after being struck by an unknown projectile roughly 63 nautical miles west of Yanbu on Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea coast, the UK Maritime Trade Operations agency said, per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 24). All crew members were reported safe with no environmental damage noted, and the fire was confined to the vessel’s main deck.

headline: Kalila wa Dimna Exhibition Opens at MIA Library
body: A new library display exploring the literature, art, architecture and nature behind the classic tale opens at the Museum of Islamic Art Library, featuring manuscript replicas and scale models inspired by Mughal design; runs through December 30.

headline: Run the Dome 2026 at Aspire Dome
body: Qatar’s first indoor running event inside the Aspire Dome, featuring a 4.8km two-level course with women’s and open races over August 28-29; free entry, open to all ages and fitness levels.

headline: Dhe Maveli Dohayil: Onam Celebration in Doha
body: A mega Onam celebration bringing together more than 20 artists for live music, DJs, folk performances and traditional Kerala percussion at Infinity Night Club, Premium Strato Hotel, on August 28.

headline: Travancore Fest: Mentalist Anandhu Live in Doha
body: “The Secret Letter” brings mentalist Anandhu’s interactive show combining mentalism, storytelling and audience participation to Regency Hall on August 28.

headline: Back to School Festival at West Walk
body: “With Knowledge and Work, We Build the Nation” is a four-day community celebration with educational, cultural, sporting and recreational activities, running August 26-29 at West Walk, free entry.

headline: An unidentified projectile struck an oil tanker near Oman as Iran threatened to fine and detain 45 ships for allegedly violating new Strait of Hormuz transit rules, escalating tensions as Washington’s sanctions campaign against Tehran entered its “economic D-Day” phase.

DR Congo’s Ebola outbreak posted its deadliest week yet — 317 deaths — pushing the total to 5,514 cases and 2,642 deaths, with experts warning the true toll may be roughly three times the reported figures.

Nvidia is paying $6 billion to license AI startup Poolside’s model software and separately discussing backing Perplexity at a $30 billion-plus valuation, while OpenAI pursues a $1 trillion IPO and Sam Altman admits his AI-disruption timeline was wrong.

India declared at 503/9 in Colombo behind a Dhruv Jurel century to seize command of the series decider, while Max Verstappen explained his Zandvoort Lap 1 crash: “the car snapped and I couldn’t catch it.”

Tesla is recalling nearly 3 million vehicles in China over door handles as part of a record 4 million-EV recall wave, while Intel upsized its share offering to $20 billion and Oracle had its credit rating cut by S&P over AI-driven debt.
DR Congo Ebola Death Toll Tops 2,500 as Outbreak Spreads ‘Exponentially’
body: The Bundibugyo-virus Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has killed more than 2,500 people and surpassed 4,665 confirmed cases, making it the largest Ebola epidemic ever recorded in the country, per Colombia One (Aug 23). UN Ebola coordinator Julien Harneis warned that “transmission is accelerating faster than the response can contain it,” and cautioned that response funding could run out “within weeks unless additional money arrives” — a particular concern since no approved vaccine yet exists for this Ebola species.

headline: Europe’s Summer Heatwaves Blamed for 30,000-Plus Excess Deaths
body: Initial tallies show Europe recorded at least 30,000 excess deaths this summer, with EuroMomo surveillance data putting the figure above 32,000 between mid-July and mid-August and a separate AFP count finding 33,000 deaths across eight countries, per The Korea Times (Aug 22). Germany was hit hardest with roughly 14,000 deaths — its worst summer toll since 2016 — followed by France (about 7,300) and Spain (nearly 4,500), with scientists pointing to man-made climate change as the driver.

headline: South Korea Designates Flood-Ravaged Geoje and Tongyeong as Special Disaster Zones
body: South Korea has formally designated Geoje and Tongyeong — slammed by record rainfall of 954.8mm and 763mm respectively on Aug 15-17 — as special disaster zones, unlocking greater central government funding for recovery, per The Korea Herald (Aug 22). The Ministry of the Interior and Safety said the designation “allows the central government to cover a larger share of local recovery costs, including repairs to roads, rivers and other damaged infrastructure,” as volunteer firefighters and Navy personnel continue debris-clearing operations across the region.

headline: Norris Wins Chaotic Dutch GP as Verstappen Crashes Out on Lap 1
body: Lando Norris won a dramatic Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort, finishing ahead of Mercedes duo Kimi Antonelli (+11.536s) and George Russell (+15.906s), while home hero Max Verstappen crashed out on Lap 1 after clipping the white line on the pit straight and slamming into the wall, triggering a red flag, per Formula1.com (Aug 23). It was Verstappen’s farewell race at Zandvoort before the circuit exits the calendar; Norris called it “probably one of my better wins — we had to fight for it well but the pace was strong.” Antonelli now leads the drivers’ championship on 242 points, 59 clear of Russell and Lewis Hamilton (tied on 183), with Norris up to 159, per RacingNews365 (Aug 23).

headline: Padikkal Century Puts India in Control on Day 1 in Colombo
body: India ended Day 1 of the series-deciding 2nd Test at Colombo’s SSC on 300 for 5 declared, built around a century from Devdutt Padikkal — dropped early before cashing in — and a fifty from captain Shubman Gill, per CrickeTimes and Oneindia (Aug 23). Yashasvi Jaiswal (45) and Ravindra Jadeja (43) chipped in, while Rishabh Pant retired hurt after being struck on the forearm by Lahiru Kumara; Asitha Fernando was Sri Lanka’s most successful bowler with 3 wickets. Day 2 play resumed Monday with India looking to press home the advantage before turning to bowl, per Outlook India (Aug 24).

headline: Szoboszlai’s 96th-Minute Penalty Rescues Liverpool at Newcastle
body: Liverpool salvaged a 2-2 draw at St James’ Park after Dominik Szoboszlai converted a stoppage-time penalty in the 96th minute, following Anthony Elanga’s opener (5’) and Joe Willock’s response (57’) either side of Cody Gakpo’s equalizer (55’), per Vavel (Aug 23). Elsewhere on Premier League Matchday 1, Enzo Maresca’s Manchester City came from behind to beat Bournemouth 2-1 through late goals from Marc Guéhi and Josko Gvardiol, while Brighton thrashed Aston Villa 4-0 in a chastening start for new Villa boss Unai Emery, per WithinNigeria (Aug 23).

headline: Babar Azam Set to Return for Pakistan at Lord’s
body: Pakistan are hopeful that Babar Azam, sidelined by a finger injury for the innings-and-103-run loss at Headingley, will be fit to return for the second Test at Lord’s, with top-order batter Azan Awais the likely man to make way if he does, per Geo News (Aug 23). Stand-in captain Salman Ali Agha admitted England “outplayed Pakistan” in the first Test as the tourists look to level the series from Thursday.

headline: Oil Dips as Traders Take Profits Ahead of New U.S. Sanctions on Iran
body: Brent crude fell 94 cents (1%) to $93.45 a barrel and WTI dropped 92 cents (1.06%) to $86.14 on Monday as investors booked profits from last week’s Hormuz-driven rally ahead of a 2 p.m. EDT press conference at which Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent was set to unveil what he has called “the toughest sanctions in history” against Iran, per Reuters (Aug 24). The pullback follows oil’s second straight weekly gain, with prices still elevated on reports that Hormuz shipping traffic remains well below normal levels amid the standoff.

headline: Bitcoin Stalls Just Shy of $80,000 as Weekend Liquidity Thins Out
body: Bitcoin touched an intraday high near $79,500 on Friday before slipping back to around $77,000, and was little changed over the weekend at $77,116 as of Sunday 10:06pm EDT (+0.08% on the day), per CoinDesk (Aug 21, Aug 23). The token is still up more than $15,000 for the week after a wave of short liquidations, though Standard Chartered’s Geoff Kendrick cautioned that “markets are reminding investors that volatility has two sides in digital assets” as ETF inflows — which hit $606 million on Aug 20 — typically pause over weekends.

headline: Fed Chair Warsh’s First Jackson Hole Speech Looms as Bond Yields Sit at Two-Decade Highs
body: Kevin Warsh will deliver his first keynote as Federal Reserve Chair at the Kansas City Fed’s Jackson Hole symposium this Friday, a speech markets are watching closely after he offered little forward guidance following July’s policy meeting, a reticence that helped push long-term Treasury yields to two-decade highs, per Bloomberg via Yahoo Finance (Aug 22). Analysts including Bloomberg Economics expect Warsh to focus on “describing the intellectual framework for his Fed reforms” rather than give concrete rate signals, even as the Fed’s preferred PCE inflation gauge is projected to show a 3.6% annual rise for July — still above target but the smallest gain in four months.

headline: Alibaba Raises $10.2 Billion in Record Hong Kong Sale to Fund AI Buildout
body: Alibaba raised HK$80 billion ($10.2 billion) in a Hong Kong share placement, the largest primary follow-on offering ever by a Hong Kong-listed company, per Investing.com (Aug 23). The company sold 710 million shares earmarked for “full stack” AI capabilities spanning chips, computing infrastructure and model development; CEO Eddie Wu said Alibaba “needed to build sufficient computing capacity before it could capture future growth.” Demand from sovereign wealth funds oversubscribed the offering, prompting Alibaba to increase its size, and the sale dragged Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index down more than 2% on Monday as investors weighed the dilution, per The Standard (Aug 24).

headline: Nvidia to Hike AI Server Prices Over 15% as Memory Costs Soar
body: Nvidia is raising prices on AI server systems built around its flagship Vera Rubin and Grace Blackwell chips by more than 15% for systems shipping in early 2027, per Fortune (Aug 22). The hikes, relayed to major cloud providers including Microsoft, Google and Oracle through contract manufacturers, stem from soaring DRAM costs — Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron control most global memory-chip production and “still haven’t caught up with surging demand” despite ramping output; Nvidia did not respond to requests for comment.

headline: Ex-DeepMind Startup’s Small AI Agent Beats Claude and GPT at Redoing Science
body: London lab Inherent said its new agent Faraday outperformed Anthropic’s Claude Opus 4.8 and OpenAI’s GPT-5.5 at independently reproducing published scientific paper findings — while running on a far smaller 27-billion-parameter Qwen 3.6 model, per TechCrunch (Aug 22). The DeepMind-alumni-founded startup, which emerged from stealth with a $50 million seed round, said the result was less about beating frontier labs than the training method; chief scientist Edward Hughes said, “What was most interesting to us about this was not so much the result of beating those frontier agents…but was actually the way we went about building this.”

headline: Starcloud Raises $250M, With Nvidia Backing, for Orbital AI Data Centers
body: Redmond-based Starcloud raised a $250 million Series A extension at a $2.3 billion post-money valuation to build a constellation of orbital AI data centers, per GeekWire (Aug 21). Nvidia joined the round as a new investor alongside Cisco Investments, and the startup plans to deploy satellites carrying Nvidia’s next-generation Vera Rubin chips under an FCC filing to operate up to 88,000 orbital data-center satellites; CEO Philip Johnston said the funding “empowers us to build the infrastructure to launch many more of Nvidia’s most advanced GPUs into space.”

headline: Iran Slaps Transit Fees on Hormuz Shipping as Bessent Launches ‘Economic D-Day’
body: Iran’s parliamentary National Security Commission approved Article 3 of its “Strategic Action to Ensure the Security and Progress of the Strait of Hormuz” plan, requiring ships from “authorised” nations to pay transit fees; commission spokesperson Ebrahim Rezaei said “fees will be charged for services including navigation, environmental, fueling under certain conditions, insurance, safety and other services we provide,” per Al Jazeera (Aug 24). Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei added, “The Strait of Hormuz is closed, despite American claims, and will not open until America corrects its behaviour.” The move came as U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent wrote in the Financial Times that Washington was launching “an economic D-Day, the single greatest financial offensive ever marshalled” against Iran, vowing to “sever every economic lifeline that sustains the tyrannical regime until Tehran stands alone,” per the Jerusalem Post (Aug 24).

headline: Tehran’s Leaders Mock US Sanctions Push as ‘Admission of Defeat’
body: Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps spokesperson Brigadier General Hossein Mohebbi dismissed Washington’s new sanctions blitz as “an implicit admission of the enemy’s humiliating defeat in the military arena,” arguing “the US would have no need to resort to economic warfare if it had achieved victory on the military front,” per Press TV (Aug 23). Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf mocked the sanctions push online, writing “A frozen foreign policy delivers a frozen economy. The only thing still moving? The Iran boomerang,” per Tribune India (Aug 23).

headline: Putin Threatens ‘Pandora’s Box’ Retaliation Over Ukrainian Strikes
body: Russian President Vladimir Putin warned of a crushing retaliation over Ukraine’s escalating drone strikes on Russian oil refineries and warehouses, saying, “The Kyiv regime set out to damage our economy. What did it do? It opened this Pandora’s box itself. Well then, expect a response targeting your most sensitive economic sectors,” per the Moscow Times (Aug 23). Russia has already hit Ukrainian Black Sea grain-export infrastructure in response, though Putin insisted “we will resolve these issues” without causing global food shortages.

headline: Nevada Clears Tesla for Up to 5,000 Robotaxis in Las Vegas
body: The Nevada Transportation Authority approved Tesla to operate a fleet of up to 5,000 fully autonomous vehicles for paid passenger service in Clark County, home to Las Vegas, one of three companies granted driverless-ride authority in the region. The approval, announced Aug 21, lands as Tesla prepares to launch its Cybercab in Austin later this month, starting with employee rides. Per The Motley Fool (Aug 21).

headline: Cloudflare Beats on Q2 and Raises Full-Year Guidance
body: Cloudflare’s Q2 2026 results topped estimates across the board: revenue of $696.1 million, up 35.9% year-over-year, with adjusted EPS of $0.29 versus a $0.27 estimate. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to $2.87 billion in revenue and $1.26 in adjusted EPS at the midpoints, and guided Q3 revenue to $736.5 million. Per Yahoo Finance/StockStory (Aug 6).

headline: Intel Posts a Seventh Straight Beat, Raises Capex, Faces New Qualcomm Challenge
body: Intel’s Q2 2026 revenue came in at $16.13 billion against a $14.33 billion forecast, with adjusted EPS of $0.42 versus a $0.21 estimate — a seventh consecutive beat — as AI-related revenue grew 70% year-over-year. The company raised 2026 capital spending above $20 billion and completed a $20 billion equity raise this month to fund expanded manufacturing capacity, even as Qualcomm’s new Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme benchmarks raised questions about Intel’s client-computing lead. Per CNBC (Aug 10).

headline: Palantir Lifts 2026 Guidance, Deepens Defense Ties via Mercury Systems
body: Palantir raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $8.15-8.16 billion after posting Q2 revenue of $1.94 billion and net income of $1.06 billion. The same day, defense contractor Mercury Systems announced a new partnership to use Palantir’s software and enterprise ontology to automate material planning and build a digital twin of factory operations for U.S. military production programs. Per Simply Wall St News.

headline: Fastly’s Fifth Straight Beat Comes With a Raised Outlook
body: Fastly’s Q2 2026 report showed revenue of $183.3 million, up 23.3% year-over-year, plus adjusted EPS of $0.15 against a $0.0663 estimate — its fifth consecutive beat. Security revenue grew 43% to $41.7 million, and the company raised full-year guidance to $732-746 million in revenue and $0.50-0.54 in adjusted EPS; CEO Kip Compton said “our platform strategy is driving business momentum, giving us the confidence to raise our full-year outlook.” Per 24/7 Wall St (Aug 10).

headline: Starbucks’ Turnaround Shows Up in Comps as Restructuring Wraps
body: Starbucks’ fiscal Q3 2026 results showed global comparable sales up 7.9% — a 4.2% rise in transactions plus a 3.5% rise in average ticket — with non-GAAP EPS of $0.85 on revenue of $9.3 billion. The company raised full-year guidance to non-GAAP EPS of $2.55-2.65 and operating margin above 11%, and this week wrapped up its restructuring with a further 224 layoffs as its “third place” revival strategy takes hold. Per Bloomberg/Yahoo Finance (Aug 20).

headline: Arm Caught in a Bond-Yield-Driven Chip Selloff, Analysts Split on Targets
body: Arm Holdings remains in the shadow of an Aug 19 semiconductor selloff triggered by rising bond yields; NFJ Investment Group’s Burns McKinney noted “every time bond yields rise, that tends to disproportionately hit the technology names.” Analyst price targets on Arm now range widely — Goldman Sachs at $125 and Morgan Stanley at $212 (both Hold) versus Rosenblatt at $250, New Street Research at $260, and Evercore ISI at $326 (all Buy) — reflecting debate over Arm’s rich valuation relative to peers like AMD and Nvidia. Per ts2.tech (Aug 19).

headline: No Fresh Catalyst for Oracle as AI-Growth and Debt Debate Continues
body: Oracle had no new company-specific news Monday; Benzinga’s market recap attributed investor attention to an ongoing debate between Oracle’s AI-driven growth opportunity and its debt-funded data-center build-out, a debate sharpened after S&P Global Ratings downgraded Oracle’s credit rating in July. No new contract, earnings, or guidance update was found to explain the session. Per Benzinga (Aug 24).

headline: Modi Urges Space Startups to Make India a Global Talent Hub
body: Addressing CEOs and founders from 20 space startups on National Space Day, PM Narendra Modi said “we need to create an aura where people worldwide feel that if they want to make a career, they should go to India,” adding “we are very competitive on cost; there is no question at all about talent.” He cited Skyroot Aerospace — India’s first space-tech unicorn, which launched the country’s first private rocket — as the sector targets one launch a month by mid-2027, per Business Standard (Aug 23).

headline: India Unveils Rs62,500-Crore Scheme to Boost Local Smartphone Brands
body: India rolled out a Rs62,500-crore Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme running through FY2030-31, targeting nearly Rs39 lakh crore in production and 60,000 direct jobs, with India already supplying 99.2% of the phones it uses domestically, per WION (Aug 23). Union IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said it “will provide a significant impetus to the development of Indian-owned mobile brands, intellectual property and design,” with incentives up to 5% for Indian brands plus a 3% bonus for domestic design and R&D.

headline: Delhi Police Deny Clearance for Anti-UGC Reservation Protest
body: Delhi Police refused permission for a demonstration against UGC equity/reservation regulations at Jantar Mantar, keeping Section 163 BNSS prohibitory orders in force across the North District banning gatherings of five or more people, per WION (Aug 23). A Delhi DCP statement said “no permission has been granted to any individual or organisation for holding any such protest/gathering at Jantar Mantar on 23 August 2026,” after the Supreme Court had already put the UGC regulatory framework in abeyance over vague provisions.

headline: Burnham Grants Mayors New Power to Override Councils on Major Developments
body: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham unveiled plans letting mayors overrule local councils on major planning projects — developments of 150-plus homes, over 15,000 sq m of commercial space, or buildings 30 metres and taller — with ten of England’s 14 devolved mayors backing the move, per ITV News (Aug 23). “Sometimes challenge does need to be made to local decision-making…it’s a two-way street,” Burnham said, as the government sits roughly a quarter of the way to its 1.5-million-homes target; Lib Dem housing spokesperson Gideon Amos called it “a direct attack on communities.”

headline: UK to Confine Released Violent Offenders to GPS-Monitored Zones
body: The UK government announced that released violent and sexual offenders will be GPS-monitored and confined to exclusion zones just a few miles wide, with victims given input into setting the boundaries, per ITV News (Aug 22). Justice Secretary Alex Norris said “offenders should carry the consequences of their crimes, not their victims,” with the move coming ahead of PM Burnham’s review of Labour’s early-release scheme when Parliament returns September 1.

headline: Fifty MPs Demand Funeral Sector Regulation After Hull Scandal
body: Fifty cross-party MPs wrote to Health Secretary Yvette Cooper demanding urgent statutory regulation of the funeral sector after Robert Bush, who ran a Hull funeral home, was jailed for 20 years in July for leaving 35 decomposing bodies and half a tonne of ashes at his premises, per ITV News (Aug 21). Cooper said “every person in every situation deserves dignity in death,” while the MPs, organised by Dame Caroline Dinenage and Mark Sewards, warned “without urgent government intervention, further cases of severe negligence and abuse are inevitable.”

headline: Qatar Stock Exchange Adopts Randomized Auction Timing
body: The Qatar Stock Exchange announced it will randomize the uncrossing mechanism for its opening and closing auction sessions, with price determination now occurring at a randomly selected moment within the final minute of each session, per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 24). The QSE said the move reflects its commitment to “maintaining fair, orderly, and efficient markets, consistent with international best practices and IOSCO principles relating to market integrity and transparent price formation.”

headline: Qatar’s Construction Sector Set for 6.7% Growth Surge in 2027
body: Qatar’s construction sector is forecast to post 6.7% real GVA growth in 2027, though Fitch Solutions projects the long-term 2026-2035 average will run at just 1% annually, “materially below pre-conflict levels” of 1.4%, per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 23). Analysts pointed to continued government capex including the Ashgal road programme and Qatar National Vision 2030 projects, while the power and renewables sector is projected to grow at a 12.6% compound annual rate through 2035.

headline: Qatar’s ‘Suhail’ Season Begins, Signaling Gradual Cooldown
body: Qatar’s 53-day ‘Suhail’ season begins August 24, marking the traditional rising of the Suhail (Canopus) star and the start of a gradual overnight cooldown after peak summer heat, per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 23). The season unfolds in four phases — Tarfah, Jabha, Zubrah and Sarfah — with the Qatar Calendar House marking it as coinciding with “the rising of the Suhail star in the Arabian Peninsula.”

headline: Colorverse Experience Continues at Katara
body: The Colorverse Experience runs through September 15, 2026 at Katara South Parking, Katara Cultural Village, an immersive show blending color, light, sound and interactive challenges. It’s open weekdays 4:00—10:00 PM and weekends 4:00—11:00 PM, with tickets from QAR 35, per Qatar Living (Aug 16).

headline: Doha Trade Fair Opens at DECC
body: The Doha Trade Fair runs August 24 through September 4, 2026 at the Doha Exhibition & Convention Center, open daily 10:00 AM—10:00 PM with free entry. The shopping exhibition brings together a wide range of retail exhibitors and products, per Qatar Living (Aug 23).

headline: Rouda Al Malki Fashion Exhibition at QNCC
body: Designer Rouda Al Malki showcases a curated collection of women’s fashion, lifestyle products and essentials at Qatar National Convention Center from August 28 to September 2, 2026, daily 10:00 AM—7:00 PM. Entry is free, per Qatar Living (Aug 23).

headline: Tasweer’s Frame and Focus Opens at Al Hosh Gallery
body: Tasweer’s second edition of “Frame and Focus” opens September 5 and runs through October 5, 2026 at Al Hosh Gallery in Doha, featuring documentary photography, portraiture and conceptual work from more than 12 photographers from Qatar and the region. The show explores themes of identity, memory, heritage, migration and belonging, per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 22).

headline: ORBIT Arabian Night Brings Raï Music to Lusail
body: ORBIT Arabian Night brings a live performance of North African Raï music to Cielo Hotel in Lusail on August 28, 2026, starting at 7:00 PM. Tickets start at QAR 100 and the event is restricted to guests 21 and older, per Qatar Living (Aug 23).

headline: Iran’s parliament voted to start charging foreign ships transit fees to cross the Strait of Hormuz, hours after the U.S. Treasury unveiled what it called “the toughest sanctions in history” against Tehran.

DR Congo’s Ebola outbreak is now the largest ever recorded in the country, topping 4,665 cases and 2,500 deaths, with the UN’s coordinator warning transmission is “accelerating faster than the response can contain it.”
Lando Norris won a chaotic Dutch Grand Prix after Max Verstappen crashed out on Lap 1 of his Zandvoort farewell; India took command of the Colombo series decider behind a Devdutt Padikkal century.

Alibaba raised a record $10.2 billion in a discounted Hong Kong share sale to fund its AI buildout, triggering a Hang Seng slide, while oil eased and bitcoin held near $80,000 ahead of the new Iran sanctions.
Nvidia is hiking AI server prices more than 15% as a DRAM shortage bites, and a London startup says its small AI agent beat Claude and GPT-5.5 at reproducing scientific research.
Congo Receives First Ebola Vaccine Shipment as Death Toll Tops 2,500
body: More than 16,250 doses of the Ervebo vaccine arrived in Kinshasa on Friday, the first installment of 70,000 pledged doses, as DR Congo’s outbreak death toll climbed past 2,500 with nearly 5,300 confirmed cases, per Al Jazeera (Aug 22). Health Minister Samuel Roger Kamba said the vaccine “had been used several times in the past, including on a very large scale” during the 2018–2020 outbreak; 20,000 of the new doses will go toward a late-stage trial testing effectiveness against the Bundibugyo strain now circulating. The UN warned transmission continues spreading “exponentially” and could reach three times its current known rate.

headline: Europe’s Summer Heatwaves Blamed for Over 30,000 Excess Deaths
body: New continent-wide tallies show Europe suffered at least 30,000 excess deaths this summer, with the EuroMomo monitoring platform recording more than 32,000 excess deaths between mid-July and mid-August alone, per The Local (Aug 22). Germany logged roughly 14,000 heat-linked deaths — its worst toll since 2016 — while France recorded 7,300 and Spain nearly 4,500; the final week of June alone accounted for almost 16,000 excess deaths, with people over 75 hit hardest. Scientists tied the recurring heatwaves to global warming “primarily caused by burning coal, oil and gas,” warning such extremes “will become more frequent, longer and more intense.”

headline: South Korea Names New Special Disaster Zones After Record Rainfall
body: President Lee approved special disaster zone status for flood-hit Geoje and two Tongyeong districts, Sanyang-eup and Bongpyeong-dong, after record rainfall of 954.8mm in Geoje and 763mm in Tongyeong triggered landslides and widespread flooding between August 15–17, per The Korea Herald (Aug 22). One person died in a Geoje landslide; the designation means Seoul will cover a larger share of local recovery costs for roads, rivers and damaged infrastructure, with Navy personnel and volunteer firefighters from Daejeon assisting debris-clearing operations.

headline: Gold Mine Landslide Kills Dozens in Central African Republic, Site Shut Down
body: Authorities shut down the Zamboye artisanal gold mine near the Cameroon border after a landslide buried miners, with an official death toll of 49 — 34 Central Africans, 13 Cameroonians and two Chadians — though local sources estimate closer to 100 dead, per Al Jazeera (Aug 19) and Africanews (Aug 21). Mines Minister Rufin Benam-Beltoungou confirmed the toll after visiting the site, with the ministry saying the disaster “highlighted the dangers of artisanal operations, particularly at sites with poor safety conditions”; rescue efforts were suspended as the site kept collapsing and heavy rains flooded lower sections, while seven injured survivors were hospitalized in Baboua.

headline: Joe Root Breaks All-Time Catch Record as England Set Sights on Lord’s
body: England’s innings-and-103-run demolition of Pakistan at Headingley was capped by Joe Root moving to 219 Test catches, passing Steve Smith for the most by a non-wicketkeeper, as his second stint as captain began “in style” — per Khaleej Times (Aug 21). Josh Tongue (8-89) and Ollie Robinson (8-80) posted career-best match figures as Pakistan collapsed to 135 in their second innings, with Mohammad Rizwan’s 41 the only real resistance. The three-match series resumes Thursday at Lord’s, where Pakistan hope an injured Babar Azam recovers in time to lead them.

headline: Gill’s India Chase Clean Sweep and WTC Boost as Colombo Decider Begins
body: India begin the series-deciding 2nd Test against Sri Lanka in Colombo today (Aug 23) chasing a 2-0 sweep and their first overseas series win in three years; a win would push them toward fourth in the WTC standings — per Telangana Today (Aug 22). Captain Shubman Gill, averaging over 73 as skipper versus 35 before taking the job, is working on his weakness against left-arm spin after twice falling to Prabath Jayasuriya in Galle. Kuldeep Yadav’s place is under threat after a wicketless, expensive outing at Galle, with Saransh Jain in contention depending on pitch conditions.

headline: Manchester United Stunned by Newly Promoted Hull City in Season Opener
body: Manchester United lost 2-0 to Hull City at the MKM Stadium as Semi Ajayi (17’) and Nobel Mendy (38’) scored on the day Hull marked their return to the Premier League after a decade away — per GiveMeSport (Aug 22). United dominated the ball (72% possession) and fired 21 shots to Hull’s 8, but managed only five on target, missing key defenders Lisandro Martínez and Matthijs de Ligt through injury. It is a jarring result to follow a summer of heavy spending under manager Michael Carrick.

headline: Man Utd Complete Medical for Carlos Baleba in £65m Deal
body: A day after their shock Hull City defeat, Manchester United pushed ahead on the transfer front, with Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba undergoing his medical on Saturday as part of a deal worth an initial £65m — per TheHardTackle (Aug 22). It marks a steep climbdown from Brighton’s £115m valuation of him a year ago, with United “privately delighted with the deal after failing to land him last summer,” per a Guardian report cited in the piece. The 22-year-old Cameroonian, capped over 100 times for Brighton since joining from Lille in 2023, is signed to fill the defensive-midfield void left by Casemiro’s exit and Manuel Ugarte’s struggles.

headline: Norris Snatches Pole From Russell Ahead of Verstappen’s Last Home Race
body: Lando Norris denied George Russell pole for Zandvoort’s farewell Dutch Grand Prix, going quickest as conditions worsened late to lock in 1:11.163, just 0.102s clear of the Mercedes — per Formula1.com (Aug 22). Max Verstappen, racing his final home Grand Prix before the circuit exits the calendar, could only qualify seventh, and finished sixth — over 10 seconds back — as Russell won Saturday’s sprint race lights-to-flag ahead of Charles Leclerc. The main Grand Prix goes off later Sunday in front of Zandvoort’s orange-clad crowd.

headline: Wall Street Rebounds Friday, Still Books a Weekly Loss
body: Wall Street closed out a turbulent week with broad gains on Friday, as the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 517.80 points (0.98%) to 53,277.00, the S&P 500 added 33.21 points (0.43%) to 7,674.37, and the Nasdaq Composite gained 113.29 points (0.43%) to 26,180.46, per Yahoo Finance (Aug 21). Despite the rebound, all three major indexes still finished the week lower after a bond-market selloff rattled technology and AI-related shares. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s pledge of expanded bond buybacks briefly eased tensions on Thursday — he said, “Part of it is signaling here to show that we believe yields don’t reflect the underlying fundamentals” — but 10-year and 30-year Treasury yields reverted higher by week’s end.

headline: Bitcoin Flirts With $80,000, Extending Best Week Since 2023
body: Bitcoin surged to roughly $79,500 on Friday, its highest level since May and a jump of about 24% from Wednesday’s low near $64,100, marking its best week since 2023 as it closes in on the $80,000 mark, per Forbes (Aug 21). Techdollar CEO Terence McMenamin noted that “Bitcoin is up more than 20% this week, spot ETFs have pulled in roughly $1.6 billion, and billions of dollars of short positions have been forced out.” Kraken global economist Thomas Perfumo added that “over the last couple of days, we’ve seen Bitcoin ETFs post net inflows that make the top-10 best days for net flows in 2026,” with the rally tied to the Treasury’s bond buyback program and newly passed crypto-market legislation.

headline: Oil Climbs for Second Straight Week as U.S.-Iran War Squeezes Supply
body: Crude oil notched a second consecutive weekly gain, with Brent settling near $93.82 a barrel and U.S. WTI holding around $86.78, per Univest (Aug 21). The report cites the stalemated U.S.-Iran conflict as the primary driver, noting it “continues to disrupt oil supply from a key Middle East producing region,” while a Gulf diplomatic deadlock has added further upward pressure. Analysts pointed to OPEC+ production discipline compounding the Middle East disruption, tightening the pool of available barrels in the global market.

headline: Fed Chair Warsh’s First Jackson Hole Speech Looms Over Jittery Bond Market
body: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh is set to deliver his first Jackson Hole keynote on Friday, August 28, with markets already pricing in a neutral tone — 69% of fund managers surveyed by Bank of America expect no hawkish surprises, per Tech Times (Aug 21). The backdrop remains tense: 30-year Treasury yields hover near 19-year highs around 5.27%, and Treasury Secretary Bessent’s bond buyback intervention “fizzled within 48 hours,” according to the report. Warsh himself described his approach as “like a blank sheet of paper,” calling this “a period of watchful thinking, not watchful waiting.”

headline: Anthropic Could File for Record $2 Trillion IPO by End of August
body: Anthropic’s IPO registration could land as soon as late August, with the AI lab reportedly targeting a $2 trillion valuation ahead of a possible October market debut, per Dataconomy (Aug 21). Bloomberg reported (Aug 20) that Anthropic executives expect the offering to match or top SpaceX’s record for the largest-ever new share sale — the very benchmark flagged in Saturday’s briefing — with annualized revenue reportedly reaching roughly $65 billion by late July, according to Tech Startups (Aug 21).

headline: GitHub CTO: Commit Volume Doubled Since April, Fix Includes New Read-Scaling Architecture
body: Following up on his ‘we let you down’ apology, GitHub CTO Vladimir Fedorov detailed the strain behind the August 17 outage, per The Register (Aug 21): monthly commits jumped from 1.4 billion in April to 2.9 billion now, with Azure handling roughly 58% of platform load. “If you were trying to ship software that day, we let you down,” Fedorov said, adding that neither August incident stemmed from a code or configuration change but from systemic limits GitHub is now addressing with tighter retry limits and an architecture meant to scale read capacity “linearly with the number of readers.”

headline: Alation Confirms Cyberattack But Still Won’t Disclose Scope
body: Alation has now confirmed “unauthorized activity in one of its systems” after Tuesday’s reported outage, but the data-catalog vendor — used by roughly half of Fortune 1000 companies — still won’t say how many customers were affected or whether data was exfiltrated, per TechCrunch (Aug 20). “We are conducting a thorough investigation of what occurred and we will provide additional information as appropriate,” the company said, leaving the scope of the breach still unknown a day after acknowledgment.

headline: Google’s Gemma Models Cross 1 Billion Downloads
body: Google DeepMind’s open Gemma model family has passed 1 billion cumulative downloads since its early-2024 launch, with developers building more than 100,000 distinct variants, per Unite.ai (Aug 20) — the first time Google has put a cumulative figure on Gemma’s adoption. Real-world deployments now span NASA/JPL running Gemma 3 4B for satellite image analysis and India’s 100-million-download Aarogya Setu 2.0 health app, which uses Gemma 4 to standardize medical reports.

headline: Trump Claims ‘American Territory’ Over Hormuz as Iran Sanctions Land
body: The new US sanctions blitz on Iran has now landed, and Tehran’s Foreign Ministry condemned it as an attempt to impose “extraterritorial sovereignty over all independent UN member states,” per Al Jazeera (Aug 22). President Trump escalated his rhetoric on the strait standoff, saying he regards “the Strait of Hormuz as an American territory right now” and that Iran is “not ready to make the right deal in my opinion,” even as shipping traffic through the chokepoint remains stalled and US gas prices climb.

headline: Israeli Strikes Cast Doubt on Gaza Disarmament Push Days After Kushner Visit
body: Days after Jared Kushner met Netanyahu to push a Hamas weapons drawdown and predicted “we could be seeing progress…in as little as 30 days,” Israeli strikes on Nuseirat and Gaza City killed at least 17 Palestinians, per PBS NewsHour (Aug 19), bringing the ceasefire-era Israeli-strike death toll to roughly 1,273. Hamas spokesperson Hazem Qassem accused the new US-backed Board of Peace of providing “cover for Israel to escalate its attacks” rather than enforcing compliance, as the sides remain deadlocked over disarmament sequencing and Israel’s withdrawal timeline.

headline: Sudan’s Kordofan Siege Grinds On as Floods Compound the War
body: More than 200,000 people have been newly displaced across Kordofan since late 2025, with displacement in el-Obeid’s Sheikan district up 25% over eight months, per Al Jazeera (Aug 20–22). The besieged city’s main power transformer has been destroyed by RSF drone strikes, crippling water pumps and hospitals for a population that has ballooned to an estimated 3.4 million, while IOM Director General Amy Pope warned “the warning signs are impossible to ignore” as seasonal floods pile onto the displacement crisis.

headline: Lee Backs Trump’s North Korea Push as Seoul and Beijing Set Sights on APEC
body: Meeting Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in Seoul, President Lee Jae-myung publicly endorsed Trump’s renewed North Korea outreach as part of an effort to “formally end the Korean War,” while the two sides agreed to build momentum toward a leaders’ meeting at November’s APEC summit, per the Korea Herald (Aug 20). A rhetorical gap persisted on denuclearization — Seoul’s foreign minister pressed for “denuclearization and peace” while Wang avoided the term, and he added that any US-North Korea summit remains “a matter for North Korea and the US to decide,” signaling Beijing won’t directly broker it.

headline: Israel, Turkey Trade Warnings as Syrian Airbase Strike Exposes New Fault Line
body: Israel struck Syria’s Abu al-Duhur airbase after intelligence indicated “Turkey sought to place a radar and an air defense system manned by Turkish troops” there, with the IDF targeting the runway specifically “to prevent Turkish troops from landing,” per the Jerusalem Post (Aug 22). Turkey dismissed the justification as “frivolous allegations” aimed at excusing “unlawful airstrikes,” while US envoy Tom Barrack called the strikes an “unnecessary escalation” and said Washington is now working to build a deconfliction mechanism between Israel, Turkey, and Syria to head off further clashes.

headline: Tesla Lands Record Einride Order for 500 Semis as Nevada Clears Driverless Robotaxis
body: Tesla secured a commercial contract with Swedish logistics firm Einride for 500 Class 8 Tesla Semi trucks, the largest single order placed for the electric freight truck to date. The company also discontinued its solar roof tile line to redirect focus toward higher-margin utility-scale storage, and Nevada’s Transportation Authority authorized Tesla, among three companies, to run driverless passenger vehicles in Clark County (Las Vegas), permitting up to 5,000 fully autonomous vehicles in the first year. Per The Motley Fool (Aug 21), the developments overshadowed earlier headwinds from Chinese safety recalls affecting the Model 3 and Model Y.

headline: Oracle Deepens VA Electronic-Health-Record Deal as Cloud Backlog Swells
body: The U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs significantly expanded its multi-year electronic health record modernization agreement with Oracle, adding long-term revenue visibility just as the company’s remaining performance obligations keep expanding on surging enterprise demand for cloud computing capacity and database services. Per TradingKey (Aug 21), investors read the deal as evidence Oracle’s heavy AI-infrastructure spending is converting into firm contract commitments, offsetting concerns after a mid-August report that a New Mexico pipeline serving its Project Jupiter data-center buildout had slipped roughly six months, and after S&P Global’s July downgrade of Oracle’s credit rating to one notch below investment grade.

headline: Palantir’s Commercial Contract Value Hits a Record as Q2 Momentum Builds
body: Palantir’s second-quarter results, still fueling momentum three weeks after release, showed revenue up 93% year-over-year to roughly $1.94 billion, with U.S. commercial revenue surging 149%. Total contract value for the quarter reached $3.373 billion, including a record $2.132 billion in U.S. commercial contract value, and management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $8.15–$8.16 billion. Per QuiverQuant (Aug 21), investors also pointed to continued defense-related contract wins and an early-August manufacturing partnership as supporting factors.

headline: Cloudflare’s AI-Agent Traffic Milestone Triggers Analyst Price-Target Hikes
body: Cloudflare’s second-quarter results showed non-human and AI-agent traffic crossing half of total network activity for the first time, alongside raised full-year revenue guidance, FedRAMP High authorization for federal security workloads, and new enterprise partnerships. Sell-side analysts responded with a round of price-target increases, including Goldman Sachs, Oppenheimer, BTIG, Morgan Stanley and Mizuho, per TradingKey (Aug 21). The company’s new convertible debt offering was also read as a move to fund infrastructure investment without diluting equity.

headline: Fastly’s AI-Traffic Re-Rating Extends as Cloud-Edge Peers Catch a Bid
body: Fastly’s rally kept building on its early-August second-quarter beat: revenue of $183.3 million, up 23.3% year-over-year and well above consensus, a fifth consecutive adjusted-EPS beat, and raised full-year revenue guidance to $732–$746 million, with its security segment up 43% to $41.7 million. No fresh company-specific announcement was found for Friday’s session; the move tracked the same AI-agent-traffic re-rating lifting fellow edge-network operator Cloudflare, per AOL (Aug 10) — a story that echoes Anthropic’s IPO-fuelled interest in AI-infrastructure peers noted in Saturday’s briefing.

headline: Fubo’s HD Streaming Upgrade Lands as Cash-Flow Questions Persist
body: Fubo shipped a video-quality upgrade verifying 1080p60 performance on its MLB.TV channels, but the release did little to quiet investor concern about cash generation after fiscal third-quarter results (period ended June 30) showed revenue of $1.482 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $19.1 million, down from $31.0 million a year earlier, even as North American subscribers grew 2% to 5.75 million. Management maintained its full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook of $90–$100 million and a 2028 target of at least $300 million, while pointing to positive free cash flow only from fiscal 2027, per ts2.tech (Aug 22).

headline: Editas Medicine Narrows Losses on Early-Stage Pipeline Progress
body: No fresh company-specific news was found for Friday’s session; the move continued to digest Editas Medicine’s second-quarter report, which showed quarterly revenue climbing to $11.89 million from $3.58 million a year earlier and a narrowed net loss of $18.23 million versus $53.24 million in the same period last year. Per Simply Wall St (Aug 7), traders treated the update as encouraging but not conclusive given the clinical-stage biotech’s continued dependence on external funding.

headline: Modi: World Sees India as ‘Bright Spot of Growth and Hope’
body: Addressing the Economic Times World Leaders Forum 2026, PM Modi said “the world views India as a bright spot of growth and hope” even as global distrust deepens elsewhere. He credited reform-driven governance for lifting roughly 250 million people out of poverty over the past decade and pointed to India’s political stability and a shift toward a “permitted unless prohibited” regulatory approach, per The News Mill (Aug 21).

headline: NIA Court Denies Bail to Pulwama Attack Accused Insha Jan
body: A Jammu & Kashmir NIA court rejected the bail plea of Insha Jan, held for over six years in connection with the February 2019 Pulwama attack that killed 40 CRPF personnel, per WION (Aug 22). Special Judge Prem Sagar cited the ongoing trial and risk of witness tampering, while directing jail authorities to provide medical care and file compliance reports every two weeks.

headline: Assam Sets Up Helplines as Shillong Violence Fallout Spreads
body: After a Khasi Students’ Union black-flag bike rally turned violent in Shillong’s Khanapara area on August 19, damaging Assam-registered vehicles, Assam issued helpline numbers for stranded residents, per WION (Aug 22). Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma raised the matter with Meghalaya CM Conrad Sangma, and three KSU leaders have been arrested over the unrest.

headline: Telangana Pharma Reactor Blast Kills 2, Injures 9
body: A reactor explosion at a pharma plant in Telangana’s Pochampally mandal (Yadadri Bhuvanagiri) killed two workers and injured nine late Friday night, per WION (Aug 22). Two of the injured suffered burns covering more than 50% of their bodies; a local recalled, “Last night around 10:30, we received a call from locals saying that a blast occurred in a pharma company.” Police have opened an investigation.

headline: Seven Dead, Including Two Officers, in A66 Police Pursuit Crash
body: Seven people died — including two Cleveland Police officers — after a wrong-way car collided head-on with a marked police vehicle on the A66 near Middlesbrough during a pursuit, per ITV News (Aug 22). Chief Constable Victoria Fuller said, “No one should leave their home and not return safely, including police officers serving their communities and protecting the people of Cleveland,” as the IOPC opened a mandatory investigation.

headline: Six-Year-Old Girl Dies After Shoreham Family Sea Tragedy
body: Saja El-Khawas, 6, died in hospital after days in critical condition, becoming the fourth fatality after her British-Palestinian family got into difficulty in the water off Shoreham Fort on August 18, per Gulf News (Aug 22, citing BBC). Her father, mother and 14-year-old sister were also pulled from the sea and died; Sussex Police say CCTV and witness accounts point to a “tragic accident.”

headline: Prince Harry, Elton John Face £34.5m Legal Bill After Daily Mail Case Loss
body: Continuing yesterday’s UK-return story, a London court ordered Prince Harry, Elton John and five other claimants to pay an initial £9.54 million toward Associated Newspapers’ total £34.5 million in legal costs, per ABC News (Aug 21, updated Aug 22). Justice Matthew Nicklin ruled the claimants’ privacy case was pursued unreasonably, its allegations resting on “speculative and inferential” grounds, while their insurance covered only £16 million of the costs.

headline: Qatar Condemns Israeli Drone Strike on Civilian Vehicle Near Damascus
body: Continuing yesterday’s wave of condemnation over Israeli strikes in Syria, Qatar’s Foreign Ministry denounced a new Israeli drone attack on a civilian vehicle in Beit Jin village, Damascus countryside, that injured civilians, per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 22). The ministry called it “an unacceptable assault, a violation of Syria’s sovereignty, and a threat to its security and safety,” urging the international community to ensure accountability.

headline: Oman, Iran Resume Hormuz Talks as Pezeshkian Says Time to End War
body: Building on this week’s Oman-Iran contacts over Strait of Hormuz navigation, Omani and Iranian foreign ministers held a fresh call to discuss resuming dialogue as Washington prepares new sanctions, per Al Jazeera (Aug 22). Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said, “It is better that we bring the war to an end now as we are in a position of power and dignity,” while Iran’s military separately warned it stands ready to retaliate.

headline: Maryam Al Naimi Becomes First Qatari Woman Licensed as Air Navigation Inspector
body: Maryam Al Naimi became the first Qatari woman to earn a Certified Inspector Licence in Air Navigation Services, capping over 15 years of experience that began in air traffic control, per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 22). She said, “Being the first Qatari woman to obtain an Air Navigation Services Inspector licence reflects the support and confidence of the wise leadership in Qatari cadres.”

headline: DRC, M23 Rebels Advance Doha-Brokered Peace Roadmap in Geneva Talks
body: Representatives of the DRC government and the Alliance Fleuve Congo/M23 movement met with international facilitators in Switzerland to advance the Doha Framework for a Comprehensive Peace Agreement signed last November, per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 22). Both sides “reaffirmed their commitment to pursue negotiations towards comprehensive peace and conflict resolution,” welcoming progress on a joint verification mechanism ahead of the first ceasefire monitoring mission set for August 24 in Minembwe.

headline: Ahmed & Ahmed Stand-Up Comedy at QNCC
body: Comedians Ahmed Hassan and Ahmed Magdy bring their stand-up show to Auditorium 3 at the Qatar National Convention Centre on Thursday, August 27, with tickets starting from QAR 175, per QIC.online.

headline: Cultural Olympiad Exhibition at 3-2-1 Museum
body: The 321 Cultural Olympiad 2026’s winning and shortlisted artworks are on free display at the 3-2-1 Qatar Olympic and Sports Museum through August 31, spotlighting themes of innovation, diversity and cultural expression, per Marhaba Qatar.

headline: John Legend Live at QNCC
body: EGOT winner John Legend performs an intimate evening of soulful ballads and global hits at the Qatar National Convention Centre on September 10 — tickets are on sale now, per Visit Qatar.

headline: Run the Dome at Aspire Dome
body: Aspire Zone Foundation launches the inaugural ‘Run the Dome’ on August 28-29, a 4.8km two-level community race through the world’s largest indoor multi-purpose dome, open to runners of all ages and fitness levels.

headline: PAW Patrol: The Big Show Rescue at Mall of Qatar
body: Nickelodeon’s PAW Patrol stage show wraps its 10-day run at Mall of Qatar’s Oasis Stage through August 29, with three free daily performances at 5pm, 6:30pm and 8pm, per Qatar Living.

headline: Trump declared he now considers the Strait of Hormuz “American territory,” escalating the standoff as new Iran sanctions landed and Tehran called it a bid to impose extraterritorial rule over UN members.
DR Congo’s Ebola outbreak topped 2,500 deaths as the first Ervebo vaccine shipment landed in Kinshasa, while a Central African Republic gold-mine landslide killed up to 100 artisanal miners.

England eye a 2-0 series lead at Lord’s after routing Pakistan at Headingley, India chase a series sweep in Colombo, and Manchester United lost to newly promoted Hull City hours before completing a £65m deal for Carlos Baleba.
Wall Street closed higher Friday but still booked a losing week as bond-market jitters persisted; bitcoin neared $80,000 and oil extended a second weekly gain on the U.S.-Iran standoff.
Anthropic’s IPO could be filed within days at a $2 trillion target valuation, GitHub detailed the strain behind its latest outage, and Google’s open Gemma models passed 1 billion downloads.
Ebola Deaths Top 2,400 as Congo Receives Vaccine Boost
body: DR Congo’s Ebola outbreak has grown to 5,208 cases and 2,476 deaths, up from 5,021 and 2,378 just two days earlier, prompting the WHO and Gavi to allocate 70,000 doses of the Ervebo vaccine — 20,000 for an ongoing late-stage trial against the Bundibugyo strain and 50,000 for frontline and health workers, backed by $13 million in Gavi funding. UN Secretary-General spokesman Stéphane Dujarric said senior Ebola coordinator Julian Harneis reported the government and partners are “scaling up the response with five operational priorities, including tripling safe care capacity, strengthening community engagement, doubling the number of safe and dignified burial teams and expanding disease surveillance,” per Al Jazeera (Aug 20).

headline: Europe’s Deadly Heatwaves Fuel Rising Political Divide
body: Europe’s brutal summer heat is deepening political rifts across the continent: June’s heatwave alone caused roughly 10,000 deaths bloc-wide, including about 395 in Austria, while far-right parties such as Austria’s Freedom Party spread climate disinformation even as leaders like Spanish PM Pedro Sánchez link the extremes directly to global warming. “There is a widening gap between the scale of Europe’s heatwaves, literally hitting every EU country, and the absence of decisive European action,” said Vula Tsetsi, co-chair of the European Green Party, per Inside Climate News (Aug 21).

headline: South Korea Declares Disaster Zones After Record Floods
body: South Korea has designated the entire city of Geoje and two Tongyeong districts as special disaster zones after record Aug 15–17 rainfall — 954.8mm in Geoje and 763mm in Tongyeong — triggered landslides, flooded homes and roads, and one death. The designation, approved by the president and announced by the Ministry of the Interior and Safety, unlocks greater national funding for local recovery after damages topped the 10.25 billion won threshold in Geoje, per The Korea Herald (Aug 22).

headline: England Thrash Pakistan by an Innings Inside Three Days
body: England bowled Pakistan out for 135 in the second innings to complete an innings-and-103-run win at Headingley, with Ollie Robinson and Josh Tongue taking five wickets apiece in the first innings and Jofra Archer adding 3/50 in the second; Harry Brook’s 91 had earlier powered England to 409. “Brilliant performance — there was clarity with how we approached this match,” said Joe Root, winning his first Test as permanent captain, while Pakistan’s Salman Ali Agha admitted, “England have outplayed us.” England lead the series 1-0 with the second Test at Lord’s from Aug 27, per telecomasia.net (Aug 21).

headline: Gill Dominates Saransh Jain in Colombo Nets as Kuldeep Sits Out
body: With India expected to hand uncapped off-spinner Saransh Jain his debut in Saturday’s series-deciding 2nd Test, Shubman Gill looked in ominous touch at the Sinhalese Sports Club, taking Jain apart in the nets while Kuldeep Yadav skipped Friday’s session entirely. Spin-bowling coach Sairaj Bahutule explained Gill’s method: “This is just his way of adapting and finding the best methods to play, defend, and, more importantly, adapt.” Jain’s net workload has only sharpened speculation he replaces Kuldeep for the Colombo decider, per Cricket Addictor (Aug 21).

headline: Verstappen Faces His Last-Ever Home Race as Zandvoort Exits F1
body: Barely a day after signing his Red Bull extension through 2030, Max Verstappen is racing his final Dutch Grand Prix — Zandvoort drops off the F1 calendar after this weekend, unable to fund the expansion modern F1 demands despite selling out every edition since its 2021 return. “Knowing it’s the last race here, I want to keep the energy positive,” Verstappen said, calling it “one of the best tracks on the calendar” while noting newer venues often “lack a bit of personality.” Red Bull arrive off the pace, with Verstappen only sixth in Friday’s sprint qualifying behind pole-sitter George Russell, per Grande Prêmio (Aug 21).

headline: Man Utd Revive £65m Chase for Brighton’s Carlos Baleba
