body: Manchester United have tabled a £60m-plus-£5m package for Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba, reopening a pursuit they walked away from last summer rather than meet Brighton’s £100m valuation. Brighton chief executive Paul Barber declined to confirm talks are advanced: “It’s not something that I can talk about right now … he’s a hugely talented young midfielder … let’s see where we go.” A club-to-club agreement is reportedly expected soon as United look to add to midfield before the window closes, per Sports Mole (Aug 20).

headline: Wall Street Ekes Out Friday Gains But Books a Losing Week
body: The Dow rose 0.98% (+517.60 points to 53,276.81), the S&P 500 gained 0.43% to 7,674.31, and the Nasdaq added 0.43% to 26,180.46 on Friday, though all three posted weekly losses after bond-market volatility rattled risk assets, per Yahoo Finance (Aug 21). Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent defended his surprise long-bond buyback plan, saying “part of it is signaling here to show that we believe yields don’t reflect the underlying fundamentals,” with attention now turning to his Monday briefing on new Iran sanctions.

headline: Bitcoin Notches Best Week Since 2023, Nears $80,000
body: Bitcoin climbed to roughly $74,800–$79,400 on Friday, up nearly 20–24% for the week — its strongest weekly run since March 2023 — per The National and CoinDesk (Aug 21). The rally was fuelled by Bessent’s doubled Treasury bond buybacks and Trump’s push for the Clarity Act crypto bill; VanEck’s Matthew Sigel said the move is “about what the US Treasury has done, which is reigniting fears of fiscal dominance,” while Bitget’s Ryan Lee noted “if the Clarity Act makes progress, it could boost investor confidence and spark a broader recovery in digital assets.”

headline: Gold Tops $4,600 as Record U.S. Debt Fuels Safe-Haven Rush
body: December gold futures opened at $4,577 and touched $4,633.90 per troy ounce by mid-morning Friday, extending its climb from Thursday’s $4,521 level, per Yahoo Finance (Aug 21). The surge ties directly to the national debt “hitting a record high of $40 trillion, five months after eclipsing $39 trillion,” the report noted, as higher debt “erodes trust in the U.S. dollar and raises borrowing costs,” prompting investors and central banks to seek safety in gold.

headline: U.S. National Debt Tops $40 Trillion, Doubling in Under a Decade
body: The U.S. national debt hit $40.05 trillion on August 18, more than double its 2017 level, with net interest costs approaching $1 trillion in 2025, per CBS News (Aug 21). Peter G. Peterson Foundation CEO Michael Peterson said “we’ve been running deficits for the last 26 years, and we’ve basically ignored a lot of the structural challenges,” warning that debt could reach $50 trillion within six years, while economist Dean Baker added simply, “we’re going the wrong way.”

headline: Anthropic Eyes Record-Breaking IPO, Could Top SpaceX’s $86.2bn Haul
body: Anthropic is preparing a fall listing that could match or exceed SpaceX’s record $86.2bn IPO, building on the $65bn raise it closed in May at a $965bn valuation — even after losing nearly $42bn in 2025, per Benzinga/Bloomberg (Aug 21). Polymarket bettors now put 72% odds on a $1.8 trillion first-day market cap and 83% odds the offering completes by end of October. “I don’t like that we have 7% in anything… it’s a good dilemma,” said David Ford, UConn’s investment-committee chair, on the concentration risk hot AI IPOs are creating for university endowments.

headline: GitHub CTO: ‘We Let You Down’ After Second Outage in Two Weeks
body: GitHub CTO Vladimir Fedorov publicly apologized for the platform’s Aug 17 outage — 7 hours 47 minutes that knocked out Actions, pull requests, Copilot and its APIs — the second major incident in two weeks after an Aug 6 failure, per The Register (Aug 21). Fedorov said neither outage stemmed from a code change but from scaling limits exposed as monthly commits nearly doubled to 2.9bn since April, pledging “an architecture that scales read capacity linearly with the number of readers.” Azure infrastructure now carries roughly 58% of GitHub’s platform load, underscoring the strain behind the outage that also disrupted Cursor’s Origin launch.

headline: Alation Still Silent on Scope of Cyberattack Hitting Half the Fortune 1000
body: Data-catalog firm Alation, used by more than 500 global companies including roughly half the Fortune 1000, has confirmed “unauthorized activity” in one of its AWS-hosted systems but has not disclosed how many customers were affected or whether data was exfiltrated, per TechCrunch (Aug 20). Company spokesperson Stephen Russell said only: “Alation recently identified an isolated incident involving unauthorized activity in one of its systems. We are conducting a thorough investigation.” A separate availability incident degraded service for some customers on Tuesday but was resolved within an hour.

headline: Nvidia Strikes $7bn Poolside Deal, Valuing Coding-AI Startup at $12bn
body: Nvidia has agreed to a $6bn non-exclusive licensing deal plus a $1bn equity stake — $7bn total — in coding-AI startup Poolside, quadrupling its valuation to $12bn from $3bn just a year ago, per CryptoBriefing (Aug 20). The deal gives Nvidia access to Poolside’s “Model Factory” and its Laguna family of code-generation models, and comes with Nvidia hiring 109 Poolside staff, echoing similar reverse-acqui-hire structures the chipmaker has used with other AI labs. Poolside, founded in 2023, previously raised a $500m Series B in October 2024.

headline: Apple Music Will Tag Tracks ‘Made With AI’ Later This Year
body: Apple Music will roll out visible “Made With AI” labels later in 2026 for songs where a “material portion” of the content was AI-generated, extending the AI Transparency Tags it introduced in March, per MacDailyNews and Billboard (Aug 20–21). The move follows pressure from the RIAA, the Grammys and SAG-AFTRA, who jointly urged streamers to improve AI-music disclosure; Apple Music executive Oliver Schusser has noted more than a third of monthly track submissions are now fully AI-generated, though listener engagement with them remains under 0.5%. Spotify is set to follow with its own “AI Persona” artist badges starting mid-September.

headline: Trump Boasts ‘Total Control’ of Hormuz as Iran Sanctions Blitz Begins
body: Speaking to reporters before boarding Air Force One on Aug 21, Trump said Iran “would love to make a deal, but they’re not ready to make the right deal,” claiming the US has “total control of that entire region having to do with the Strait of Hormuz,” per The Times of Israel (Aug 22). It follows Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s Aug 20 vow of the “toughest sanctions in history — a one-two punch” alongside an existing blockade, warning allies “you’re either with us or against us,” per Al Jazeera (Aug 20); FM Abbas Araghchi dismissed the campaign as doomed like past “maximum pressure” efforts, per anews.com.tr (Aug 22).

headline: Gaza ‘Working Groups’ Take Shape as Kushner Ties Rebuilding to Disarmament
body: Two joint committees — on disarmament/security and on humanitarian relief — were set up after talks between Jared Kushner, Netanyahu and Board of Peace officials, per Al Jazeera (Aug 18); Kushner told US media weapons collection could start “in the next 60 to 90 days,” with surrendered arms going to a US-led International Stabilization Force under Gen. Jasper Jeffers rather than Gaza’s new NCAG government. Kushner declared “we will not allow Gaza to be rebuilt until demilitarisation occurs,” while Netanyahu confirmed Israeli strikes on Hamas will continue during the process — a sequencing analysts warn sidelines Qatar, Egypt and Turkey as mediators.

headline: Sudan: 200,000 Newly Displaced in Kordofan as War Meets Floods
body: More than 200,000 people have fled fresh fighting and flooding in Sudan’s Kordofan region, with drone strikes hitting water and power infrastructure in El Obeid and heavy rains destroying homes in North Darfur, per Al Jazeera/UN (Aug 20). IOM Director General Amy Pope said “the warning signs are impossible to ignore — families are fleeing violence, losing access to water, electricity and healthcare, and now facing the added burden of destructive floods,” calling Sudan “one of the world’s largest displacement crises.”

headline: Wang Yi Presses Seoul on ‘Strategic Autonomy’ as Lee Eyes China Summit
body: During his Seoul visit, Chinese FM Wang Yi told South Korea’s National Security Adviser Wi Sung-lac that Beijing hopes Seoul will “achieve strategic autonomy, refrain from bloc confrontation or taking sides,” and that lasting peace on the peninsula requires “concrete actions conducive to restarting dialogue” with North Korea, per SCMP (Aug 20). President Lee Jae Myung responded by floating deeper bilateral ties at the upcoming APEC leaders’ meeting in southern China, as Beijing works to counter US influence amid Trump’s push to revive summitry with Kim Jong Un.

headline: Oracle Expands VA Health-Records Deal Into Multi-Billion-Dollar Contract
body: Oracle significantly expanded its multi-year electronic health record modernization agreement with the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs into a multi-billion-dollar contract, per TradingKey (Aug 21). The expansion adds to a cloud infrastructure backlog that Oracle says has been swelling on surging enterprise demand for AI compute capacity and database services.

headline: Nevada Clears Tesla for Up to 5,000 Driverless Robotaxis in Clark County
body: Nevada’s Transportation Authority authorized Tesla — alongside two rival autonomous-vehicle operators — to run driverless passenger service in Clark County, home to Las Vegas, per The Motley Fool (Aug 21). Tesla’s permit covers a fleet of up to 5,000 fully autonomous vehicles in its first year, though the company is not expected to deploy anywhere near that number immediately, as it also pushes to expand its Cybercab robotaxi service with a planned Austin launch.

headline: Palantir Raises Full-Year Guidance as AI Platform Contract Values Surge
body: Palantir’s latest quarterly results beat expectations and prompted management to raise full-year guidance, citing accelerating enterprise adoption of its Artificial Intelligence Platform (AIP) and rapidly rising contract values, per TradingKey (Aug 21). Wall Street analysts have been revising earnings estimates and price targets upward in response, though some flagged the stock’s elevated valuation multiples as a risk to watch.

headline: Cloudflare Raises 2026 Outlook, Launches AI-Agent Product Suite
body: Cloudflare raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance and unveiled a new slate of AI-agent products — including an open-source AI workspace called Cloudflare OS, an AEO visibility dashboard, and new AI governance tools — per a company update covered by Yahoo Finance (Aug 21). Executives said non-human and AI-agent traffic now accounts for more than half of all activity on Cloudflare’s network, underscoring the demand the new products aim to capture.

headline: Anthropic Accelerates IPO Plans, Reviving Interest in AI-Infrastructure Peers
body: Anthropic said it is accelerating plans for a U.S. initial public offering targeting a roughly $2 trillion valuation, with a filing possible as soon as late August and a market debut eyed for October — a deal that could rival SpaceX’s record share offering, per Dataconomy (Aug 21). The news reignited investor interest in infrastructure and content-delivery names seen as beneficiaries of AI-model providers going public, following Fastly’s own second-quarter report in which it raised full-year revenue guidance and filed a shelf registration to support future capital raises.

headline: Starbucks Completes Restructuring With 224 More Corporate Layoffs
body: Starbucks confirmed layoffs of 224 corporate employees — 120 who declined to relocate from Seattle to the company’s new Nashville hub and 104 from its store design and construction team — completing a global restructuring first announced in May that eliminated 252 corporate roles in total, per Yahoo Finance (Aug 21). The Nashville buildout is part of a $100 million investment tied to CEO Brian Niccol’s plan to cut $2 billion in costs over two years, alongside closing underperforming stores and divesting its China stake.

headline: Arm Caught in Semiconductor Pullback Despite Strong Data-Center Growth
body: Arm Holdings has become one of the more visible casualties of a broader semiconductor pullback tied to rising bond yields, which tend to disproportionately hit high-multiple technology names. The company’s own fundamentals stayed strong — June-quarter revenue grew 22% to $1.29 billion, data-center royalties more than doubled, and cumulative demand for its AGI CPU designs now exceeds $2 billion across fiscal 2027-2028 — with analysts noting Arm’s valuation premium versus peers such as Nvidia and AMD leaves it more exposed to any growth disappointment, and no Arm-specific negative news behind the session’s weakness.

headline: Kolkata Hotel Fire: 26 Hotels Served Notices in Fire-Safety Crackdown
body: West Bengal’s Fire Services Department has issued show-cause notices to 26 hotels and guesthouses around Mirza Ghalib Street since Wednesday — 17 more on Friday alone, each with a 24-hour deadline to respond — as the SIT continues probing the blaze at Hotel Shikha Inn that killed nine, including seven Bangladeshi nationals and a child. Officials said most victims died of smoke inhalation, and a special fire-safety audit of the entire hotel cluster has now been ordered, per The National Herald (Aug 21).

headline: Amit Shah Presses Southern States on Cauvery, Water Disputes
body: Home Minister Amit Shah convened the Southern Zonal Council in Mamallapuram, telling chief ministers “the southern states are the main pillars of the country’s progress” and pressing for faster resolution of the Cauvery and other inter-state river-water disputes. The meeting also touched on delimitation concerns raised by southern states and discussed linking major rivers and fast-tracking POCSO case trials, per WION (Aug 21).

headline: 22 Indian Sailors Held After Pirates Hijack Two Ships Off Yemen, Somalia
body: Two vessels with 22 Indian nationals aboard were hijacked off Yemen and Somalia within days of each other — the tanker Seamull with 16 Indians seized in the Gulf of Aden on August 15, and the Cameroon-flagged cargo ship Lutuf with 6 Indians taken by gunmen on August 11. MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said “one had 16 Indian nationals on board, while the other had six,” adding all 22 are reportedly safe and New Delhi is in diplomatic contact over their welfare, per Business Recorder (Aug 21).

headline: Modi to Space Startups: India Can Be a Magnet for Global Talent
body: PM Modi told 20 founders of Indian space startups gathered at Seva Teerth that “India’s space sector can act as a magnet to attract global talent, companies and investment,” urging them to expand into agriculture, environmental monitoring and debris removal. He said his goal is for the day “the world thinks of space, it looks towards India,” pointing to collaboration with Atal Tinkering Labs to build a youth talent pipeline, per pmindia.gov.in (Aug 21).

headline: Harry & Meghan’s UK Return: Security a ‘Private Matter,’ Says PM Burnham
body: Prime Minister Andy Burnham declined to say how Prince Harry and Meghan’s security will be funded once they relocate to a private home outside London later this month, calling it “a private matter… we wish them well in the moves that they’re making.” King Charles was reportedly told just three days before the announcement, and a new YouGov poll finds the public split on their return — 33% opposed, 21% supportive, 45% undecided — per ITV News (Aug 20).

headline: Met Office Warns of ‘Unprecedented’ El Niño Storms This Winter
body: The Met Office has warned of an “unprecedented” El Niño event set to drive storms and heavy rain across the UK this autumn and winter, with Professor Adam Scaife, its head of long-range forecasting, saying “I have never seen an El Niño signal this intense in our forecasts.” Sea temperatures are forecast to run over 3°C above average — the strongest such event since the 19th century — and the agency expects 2027 to become the warmest year on record, per ITV News (Aug 21).

headline: Channel Crossings Down 43% as UK-France Deal ‘Disrupts’ Gangs
body: Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said the UK-France deal “is already having a real impact, stopping crossings before they happen and disrupting the criminal gangs behind them,” after French police intercepted a boat launch on video showing migrants throwing stones at officers. Since the April agreement, France has stopped 185 crossing attempts and 12 “taxi boats,” and Channel crossings this year are down 43% to 15,897 — even as a record 230 people crammed into a single boat in August, per ITV News (Aug 20).

headline: Qatar, Egypt Sign Four Deals, Including Sheikh Tamim Hospital in Sohag
body: Qatar and Egypt signed four agreements — including one to build the H H Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al-Thani Hospital in Egypt’s Sohag governorate — at the seventh Qatar-Egypt Joint Higher Committee session in El Alamein. Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al-Thani said “the two countries continuously strive to support and elevate them to new levels of cooperation,” with talks also covering Gaza, the Iran-Gulf standoff and Red Sea shipping safety, per QNA (Aug 20).

headline: Qatar Joins 12 Nations Condemning Israeli Strikes on Syrian Airport
body: Qatar joined eleven other Arab and Islamic nations — including Saudi Arabia, Jordan and Turkey — in a joint statement condemning Israeli air raids on Syria’s Abu Al Duhur military airport as a violation of Syrian sovereignty. The foreign ministers called for enforcement of the 1974 Disengagement Agreement and an Israeli force withdrawal, warning the strikes threaten Syria’s reconstruction and regional stability, per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 21).

headline: Oman, Iran Foreign Ministers Discuss Hormuz Strait Navigation
body: Oman’s Foreign Minister Badr bin Hamad Al Busaidi held a call with Iran’s Abbas Araqchi to discuss safeguarding navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, with both sides stressing practical arrangements to protect shipping traffic and regional stability. The two also explored reviving broader regional dialogue to resolve outstanding Gulf disputes through peaceful negotiation, per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 21).

headline: “The Astrolabe: Taker of the Stars” — MIA Library
body: This exhibition on the medieval astronomical instrument continues at the Museum of Islamic Art’s Library through August 31, with standard museum admission covering entry. It’s the last week to catch it before it closes; MIA is open daily except Wednesdays, with late hours until 9pm on Thursdays, per Museum of Islamic Art (accessed Aug 22).

headline: Colorverse Experience — Katara Cultural Village
body: A new immersive family adventure has opened at Katara South Parking, taking visitors through seven interactive light-and-sound zones on a story-driven 35-minute journey. It runs through September 15, with tickets from QAR 35 and hours of 4–10pm on weekdays and 4–11pm on weekends, per Qatar Living (Aug 20) and Platinumlist.

headline: Purple You! BTS Fan Fest — Abesq Doha
body: K-pop fans can look forward to this dedicated BTS gathering at the Sandalwood Ballroom, Abesq Doha Hotel & Residence on August 28, featuring VR experiences, fan lounges, merchandise zones and BTS-inspired games. Doors open at 3pm with the show starting at 4:30pm; tickets start from QAR 150, per Platinumlist (accessed Aug 22).

headline: “Uzbekistan: Heritage in Motion” — Museum of Islamic Art
body: A major new exhibition opens September 3 in MIA’s Sheikh Saoud Al Thani Temporary Exhibitions Gallery, tracing Uzbekistan’s Islamic heritage through art, architecture and traditional crafts from the 8th century to today. It runs through November 28, with entry included in standard museum admission, per Museum of Islamic Art (accessed Aug 22).

headline: Ghostly Kisses Live in Doha — Doha Golf Club
body: The Canadian dream-pop duo brings their “MENA Tour 2026,” supporting new album “Across the Pond,” to Doha Golf Club on November 27, promising intimate, cinematic songwriting live. Doors open at 8pm and tickets start from QAR 185, per Platinumlist (accessed Aug 22).

headline: Anthropic is reportedly accelerating IPO plans toward a $2 trillion valuation that could rival SpaceX’s record offering, as GitHub’s CTO apologized for a second major outage in two weeks.
England completed an innings-and-103-run rout of Pakistan at Headingley in three days, while Max Verstappen races his final Dutch Grand Prix as Zandvoort exits the F1 calendar.
Trump declared “total control” of the Strait of Hormuz as Washington’s Iran sanctions blitz began, even as Gaza’s new disarmament “working groups” took shape under Jared Kushner.
Wall Street eked out Friday gains but booked a losing week; bitcoin notched its best week since 2023 near $80,000 and gold topped $4,600 as record U.S. debt fuelled a safe-haven rush.
DR Congo’s Ebola outbreak topped 5,200 cases as the WHO rushed 70,000 vaccine doses, while South Korea declared disaster zones after record floods.
DR Congo’s Ebola Outbreak Tops 5,000 Cases as WHO Says It’s “Far From Under Control”
body: The Democratic Republic of Congo’s Ebola outbreak, already the country’s deadliest on record, has climbed to 5,021 confirmed cases and 2,378 deaths — a 47.4% fatality rate — as of Aug 18, per NPR (Aug 19). WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus warned, “We must be frank: the epidemic is far from being under control,” noting it is spreading roughly three times faster than the 2014–2016 West African epidemic that killed over 11,000.

headline: Belgium’s “Fire of the Century” Finally Brought Under Control
body: The High Fens wildfire that scorched an area half the size of Manhattan — Belgium’s largest since 1911 — has been declared “under control in its entirety” after a seven-day battle, the governor’s office said, per Euronews (Aug 20). About 350 firefighters and seven water-bombing aircraft from Germany, Norway, Belgium and Sweden remain deployed, with officials warning weeks of continued dousing are still needed to prevent reignition.

headline: Somalia Faces New Hunger Crisis With a Fraction of Past Funding, WFP Warns
body: Some 6 million Somalis face acute food insecurity and roughly 1.9 million children under five are expected to suffer acute malnutrition this year, with about 500,000 needing urgent treatment for the most severe form, per AP (Aug 20). WFP acting chief Carl Skau said the agency now has only a tenth of the resources it had in 2022: “We can only do the bare minimum … we’re only providing these nutrition supplies to the children that are really the worst hit.”

headline: Moderna and Merck’s Personalized mRNA Vaccine Shows Promise Against Melanoma
body: In a Phase 3 trial of over 1,100 melanoma patients, the personalized mRNA vaccine intismeran, paired with Keytruda, significantly outperformed Keytruda alone at preventing cancer recurrence after surgery, Moderna and Merck announced (Aug 19). Moderna CEO Stéphane Bancel called it validation of an idea “aspirational” for years, while researcher Dr. John Cooke said, “mRNA vaccines are effective against viruses, and now we’re finding that mRNA vaccines can be effective against cancer.”

headline: Verstappen Commits to Red Bull Through 2030
body: Max Verstappen has ended months of speculation by signing a new Red Bull Racing deal running to the end of 2030, announced on the eve of his home Dutch Grand Prix weekend, per Al Jazeera (Aug 20). “I came to the team hoping to be able to win races. What we went on to achieve together has been simply lovely,” the four-time champion said, while Red Bull called it “a powerful statement of mutual trust and ambition.” The timing is notable given Verstappen sits sixth in the standings without a win this season as Red Bull continues hunting for pace.

headline: Robinson, Tongue Skittle Pakistan for 171 at Headingley
body: Ollie Robinson and Josh Tongue took five wickets apiece as England bowled Pakistan out for 171 — their lowest first-innings Test total in a decade — on the opening day of the first Test at Headingley, per ESPNcricinfo (Aug 19). Abdullah Shafique’s 61 was the lone resistance before Pakistan lost 8 for 74, and England replied through an unbeaten Joe Root to close on 112 for 2, trailing by 59 with eight wickets in hand.

headline: India Ready to Drop Kuldeep, Blood Saransh Jain for Colombo Test
body: India are set to shuffle their attack for the second Test in Colombo, with wrist-spinner Kuldeep Yadav — who managed just one wicket for 103 runs across 25 overs in the Galle win — facing the axe in favour of uncapped off-spinner Saransh Jain, per Outlook India (Aug 20). Jain, who took 30 wickets in the last Ranji Trophy season and has 188 first-class scalps at 27.30, would add right-arm variety after India fielded three left-arm spinners at Galle.

headline: Barcelona to Open La Liga Away at Elche, With Rodri in the Mix
body: Barcelona’s league curtain-raiser has been rearranged: after their original opener against Athletic Club was pushed to August 27, Hansi Flick’s side will instead make their 2026-27 La Liga debut away at Elche on August 23, per beIN Sports (Aug 19). New signing Rodri, presented at Camp Nou this week after starring in the Gamper Trophy win over Al Ahly, is in line to feature as Flick works new arrivals into the side.

headline: Walmart Slumps Nearly 10% Despite Earnings Beat as Shoppers Trade Down
body: Walmart shares fell about 9.8% on Aug 20 after Q2 revenue of $187.9bn and adjusted EPS of $0.81 topped estimates, but U.S. comparable sales grew just 2.6% — missing the roughly 3.8% consensus and the slowest pace since 2020 — as shoppers made trade-offs amid high fuel costs, per The Motley Fool (Aug 20). Roughly $2.9bn of the earnings beat came from tariff refunds rather than core operations, and Q3 EPS guidance of $0.62–$0.64 came in below the ~$0.68 Wall Street expected even as management raised full-year targets; TJX also dropped about 3% on a rare miss in its biggest segment, deepening the retail-earnings split that began with Target and Lowe’s.

headline: Wall Street Slides as Treasury-Fueled Rally Fades and Oil Climbs
body: The Dow fell 1.32% to 52,759, the S&P 500 dropped 0.85% to 7,642 and the Nasdaq lost 1.0% to 26,067 on Aug 20, reversing the prior session’s relief rally as rising crude ($86.31/barrel) and Walmart-led retail-earnings pressure weighed on sentiment, per Yahoo Finance (Aug 20). The pullback came even as gold held near $4,568 and Bitcoin jumped over 6% intraday, showing how Wednesday’s Treasury buyback announcement is still rippling unevenly through stocks, bonds and commodities.

headline: Gold Holds Near $4,500, Silver Tops $66 as Treasury Buyback Caps Yields
body: Gold traded around $4,521/oz (+4.33%) and silver broke above $66.55 (+5.29%) as of Aug 19, extending the rally sparked by the Treasury’s surprise move to double long-dated bond buybacks, per Kitco News (Aug 19). The 10-year Treasury yield fell toward 4.6% and the 30-year toward 5.2% as the buybacks targeted exactly the curve segment that had driven yields to 19-year highs, keeping pressure off both the dollar and rates.

headline: Bitcoin Rallies 14% Past $72,900 on Treasury Move, Trump’s Clarity Act Push
body: Bitcoin surged roughly 14% from about $64,100 to near $73,000 on Aug 20, its highest since early June, fueled by the Treasury’s bond-buyback announcement, a short squeeze in crowded positions, and President Trump’s meeting with crypto industry figures plus his push for the Clarity Act, per Forbes (Aug 20). Psalion managing partner Tim Enneking said “Treasury intervention, impatience with the rangebound price action and that squeeze, Trump’s unexpected meeting with certain crypto players and the announcement that he was going to push the Clarity Act appear to have given the move legs.”

headline: Stripe Pays $7.5bn for AI Routing Startup OpenRouter
body: Stripe agreed to buy AI model-gateway startup OpenRouter for roughly $7.5 billion — up sharply from its $1.3 billion valuation just three months earlier — per TechCrunch (Aug 19), with founders taking about $1.5 billion and investors the remaining $6 billion. OpenRouter, which says it routes over 10 trillion tokens daily for more than 10 million developers, will keep operating independently as Stripe folds it into its payments platform; PitchBook’s Franco Granda called it “Stripe’s deliberate attempt to embed itself into the middle of capital flows in the AI era.”

headline: Google Locks in $12.2bn Marvell Chip-Stake Warrant
body: Marvell handed Google a warrant to buy about 59 million of its shares at $206.58 each — a stake worth $12.2 billion — as part of an expanded custom AI chip partnership, per The Motley Fool and Bloomberg (Aug 20–21). The 240-tranche warrant vests only as Google actually purchases chips, with full vesting requiring $120 billion in cumulative orders through January 2033 — over 12 times Marvell’s entire annual revenue.

headline: AI Data Giant Alation Confirms Cyberattack
body: Enterprise data-catalog company Alation, which serves more than 500 companies including roughly half the Fortune 1000, confirmed “unauthorized activity” on one of its systems after a Tuesday incident briefly degraded service, per TechCrunch (Aug 20). Alation said it is “conducting a thorough investigation of what occurred” but has not disclosed how attackers got in, whether data was exfiltrated, or how many customers were affected; much of its infrastructure runs on AWS.

headline: Cursor’s Origin Launch Collides With a 6-Hour GitHub Outage
body: Cursor pushed its Origin code-hosting platform live for paid users just as GitHub suffered a 6-hour-42-minute outage with pull-request and API error rates near 20% (about 50% for archive/raw downloads), per Dataconomy (Aug 20) — extending the saga from GitHub’s 257 logged incidents since May 2025. Cursor’s Matt Palmer said “we were going to ship this earlier, but GitHub was down,” while Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch joked that Origin repos are “online,” unlike GitHub.

headline: Iran’s Araghchi Mocks Trump’s ‘Economic D-Day’ as Distraction
body: Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi dismissed President Trump’s threatened “Economic D-Day” campaign, calling it a “so-called ‘Economic D-Day’” meant to distract from America’s domestic troubles and predicting Washington would suffer further defeat, per Al Jazeera (Aug 20). Trump had announced what he called an unprecedented “crushing economic operation” against Tehran after the 60-day US-Iran negotiation window lapsed without a deal, warning any country assisting Iran would face severe financial consequences.

headline: Gaza Buries 50 as Netanyahu Rejects Trump’s Disarmament Plan
body: Gaza held a mass funeral for 50 Palestinians whose bodies were pulled from rubble across Tal al-Hawa, Zeitoun, Sabra, Sheikh Radwan and Shati, with Civil Defence estimating roughly 8,000 more still buried under collapsed buildings, per Al Jazeera (Aug 20). Health ministry chief Munir al-Bursh appealed for “heavy machinery as well as search and recovery equipment and forensic medicine supplies” to be let in, while Prime Minister Netanyahu publicly rejected Trump’s 15-point disarmament plan even as officials say Hamas has reaffirmed commitment to it — the deal Jared Kushner has been shuttling to save. Since the October ceasefire took effect, Israeli strikes have killed at least 1,266 Palestinians and wounded 4,200 more.

headline: Sudan Army Absorbs 318 RSF Defectors in Northern State
body: Sudan’s army completed the first phase of integrating Rapid Support Forces defectors, absorbing 318 fighters — including four commanders and roughly 50 combat vehicles — who switched sides in Al-Dabba locality, Northern State, per Darfur24 (Aug 20). Major General Al-Walid Abdul Qadir Ajabna praised “their decision to return to the side of the state” as the army works to erode RSF ranks through defections while the Kordofan front continues to grind on.

headline: Trump Confirms Kim Summit as China’s Wang Yi Courts Seoul
body: President Trump confirmed he plans to meet Kim Jong Un “later this year” — his first sit-down of this term — saying “I know Kim Jong Un very well, and he’s going to be fine as long as we have a smart president,” per ABC News (Aug 20). Trump has already cut joint US-South Korea military drills from 11 days to five, calling the old schedule “totally inappropriate and hostile,” as Beijing’s top diplomat Wang Yi visited Seoul urging South Korea to pursue “genuine strategic autonomy” and “refrain from bloc confrontation and taking sides,” per AsiaOne (Aug 20).

headline: Boeing Lands $4.5 Billion Qatar Tanker Approval Amid Whistleblower Film Scrutiny
body: The U.S. State Department cleared a potential $4.5 billion Foreign Military Sale of up to four Boeing KC-46A refueling tankers to Qatar, including spare engines, radar systems and support equipment, per ad-hoc-news (Aug 20). The approval adds to Boeing’s defense order backlog even as a newly released whistleblower documentary revisiting past safety and quality-control allegations drew renewed investor scrutiny during the week.

headline: Anthropic IPO Buzz Shakes Confidence in SaaS Peers Including Fastly
body: Fastly’s pullback tracked a broader rotation out of enterprise software after Bloomberg reported Anthropic is preparing an IPO filing that could rival SpaceX’s roughly $75 billion offering, with preliminary Q2 revenue said to exceed $11.5 billion and an annualized run rate near $65 billion by end-July, per stockstory (Aug 20). Investors read the prospect of AI labs going public as a threat to the scarcity premium long enjoyed by traditional SaaS names, a theme that also weighed on cloud and security peers Cloudflare and CrowdStrike.

headline: Cloudflare Prices $2.5 Billion Convertible Notes as Insiders Cash Out
body: Cloudflare priced $2.50 billion of 0% convertible senior notes due 2031, a financing move that stoked dilution concerns even as the company continues to ride a post-earnings rally, according to TradingKey (Aug 20). Recent SEC Form 4 and Form 144 filings also showed insider stock sales by executives, adding to profit-taking pressure amid the same AI-IPO-driven software-sector rotation pressuring peers like Fastly.

headline: CrowdStrike Executives’ Steady Share Sales Weigh Ahead of Aug. 26 Earnings
body: CrowdStrike shares stayed under pressure heading into its August 26 fiscal second-quarter report, with Benzinga (Aug 19) noting the move looked more like a technical pullback than a reaction to fresh bearish news, even as analysts at Mizuho, Truist Securities and Cantor Fitzgerald raised price targets that day. QuiverQuant (Aug 14) had separately flagged a steady drumbeat of insider stock sales by CrowdStrike’s top executives under pre-arranged trading plans as a source of investor unease heading into the report, part of the same software-sector jitters affecting Cloudflare and Fastly.

headline: Beyond Meat Returns to Profit, Completes Reverse Split to Save Nasdaq Listing
body: Beyond Meat returned to net profitability in its second quarter, helped by a $57.7 million non-cash gain on debt extinguishment, and completed a 1-for-30 reverse stock split effective August 13 to regain compliance with Nasdaq’s minimum bid price rule ahead of an August 31 deadline, per StockTitan (Aug 14). The company also announced a new chief operating officer alongside the results.

headline: Ring Energy Guides to 10% Production Growth in Initial 2027 Outlook
body: Ring Energy reported second-quarter production of nearly 20,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day and revenue of $104.7 million, then used the results to introduce initial 2027 guidance calling for roughly 10% production growth with capital spending about 10% lower than 2026, per the company’s August 5 release. The Permian-focused operator also cut $66 million of debt during the quarter as it leans into longer-lateral horizontal wells.

headline: SIT Probes Kolkata Hotel Fire That Killed Nine as PM Modi Offers Condolences
body: A blaze tore through the five-storey Shikha Inn hotel on Mirza Ghalib Street in central Kolkata in the early hours of Aug 19, killing nine people — including a child and five Bangladeshi nationals — with around 60 others rescued; Kolkata Police has now formed a Special Investigation Team under ACP Bhagirath Ghosh to probe fire-safety compliance, per WION (Aug 20). PM Narendra Modi said he was “extremely pained to learn about the loss of lives due to a fire mishap in Kolkata,” adding, “My condolences to those who have lost their loved ones in this tragedy. May the injured recover at the earliest,” per ANI (Aug 19).

headline: Amit Shah Presses Southern States to Resolve Cauvery and Other Water Disputes
body: Chairing the Southern Zonal Council meeting in Mamallapuram with chief ministers from Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Kerala, Union Home Minister Amit Shah urged the states to settle long-pending river-water disputes through dialogue rather than litigation, per WION (Aug 21). “If the process of protecting interests results in states being deprived of water for years while it simply flows into the sea, then no actual interest is being served,” Shah said, floating a plan to link the Brahmaputra, Kaveri and Godavari rivers.

headline: Study Finds 72% of Delhi-NCR’s PM2.5 Pollution Blows in From Outside the Region
body: A new CSTEP study finds only 28% of Delhi-NCR’s PM2.5 pollution originates locally, with the rest arriving from other Indo-Gangetic Plain states and neighbouring countries in roughly equal shares, per WION (Aug 20). Modelling shows a coordinated regional emissions cut could lower NCR’s PM2.5 by 23%, from 67.9 to 52.3 micrograms per cubic metre, with residential solid-fuel burning flagged as the largest local contributor.

headline: Night Curfew Imposed on Assam-Nagaland Border Over Infiltration Alert
body: Jorhat’s district magistrate imposed a nightly curfew from 8pm to 5am along a five-kilometre stretch of the Assam-Nagaland border after intelligence inputs warned of a possible extremist infiltration attempt, per WION (Aug 20). The order, issued under BNSS provisions, bars movement of people and vehicles in the belt except for army, police and other officials on duty.

headline: Harry and Meghan to Move Back to the UK This Month
body: The Duke and Duchess of Sussex will relocate from California to the UK later this month with children Archie, 7, and Lilibet, 5, who are enrolled to start British schools in September, ITV News reported (Aug 19), citing sources who said King Charles was informed of the plan on Sunday. The family will settle outside London in what TMZ (Aug 20) described as a “temporary” move, with the couple keeping their Montecito mansion and their status as non-working royals unchanged.

headline: Murder Inquiry Launched After Fatal Hounslow House Fire
body: A murder investigation was opened after a fire tore through a house on Berkeley Avenue in Hounslow, west London, in the early hours of Aug 19, killing a 48-year-old woman and leaving a 40-year-old woman in a life-threatening condition, per ITV News (Aug 19). Detective Chief Inspector Neil John said enquiries were “progressing at pace” to establish the circumstances, adding police believe the blaze “may have been started deliberately.”

headline: UK Inflation Hits Four-Month High of 2.9% as Energy Bills Jump
body: UK inflation climbed to 2.9% in the year to July, its highest rate in four months and up from June’s 2.6%, after a sharp rise in the household energy price cap pushed gas bills higher, according to the Office for National Statistics, per Yahoo Finance (Aug 19). The reading moves further above the Bank of England’s 2% target, adding pressure to household budgets heading into autumn.

headline: Qatar and Egypt Sign Four Agreements, Pledge Tamim-Named Hospital in Sohag
body: Qatar and Egypt signed four new agreements — on customs cooperation, regulatory affairs, development and health, including a hospital in Sohag to be named after Amir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al-Thani — as the two countries’ Joint Higher Committee met for a seventh session in El Alamein, per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 20). Qatari Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al-Thani said the two sides “continuously strive to support and elevate” bilateral ties, with trade between the countries up 80% in 2025.

headline: Qatar Condemns Kabul Educational Centre Bombing
body: Qatar’s Foreign Ministry condemned a bombing at an educational centre in Kabul, Afghanistan that injured dozens of people, reiterating “Qatar’s firm stance against violence, terrorism, and criminal acts, regardless of motives” and wishing the injured a speedy recovery, per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 20).

headline: Qatar Airways Debuts World’s First Starlink-Equipped Boeing 787-9
body: Qatar Airways became the first airline to fly a Starlink-equipped Boeing 787-9, completing installation across its entire 787-8 sub-fleet in seven months and pushing its Starlink-equipped widebody fleet to 150 aircraft, per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 20). The carrier says more than 23 million passengers have used the free, gate-to-gate Wi-Fi — offering speeds up to 500 Mbps — across over 86,000 flights since October 2024.

headline: Layla and the Wolf Closes Its Run at THIS Theatre
body: The Doha Players wrap up their Arabic-language children’s stage adaptation of the Little Red Riding Hood tale at THIS Theatre in Al Thumama (Mesaimeer), with the final performance today, Friday, August 21, running through 5pm Saturday. Recommended for ages 4–11, tickets start at QAR 65, per Marhaba Qatar listing (accessed Aug 21).

headline: Last Chance for Mathaf’s 15th-Anniversary Show Resolutions: Evolving Realities
body: Mathaf: Arab Museum of Modern Art’s free exhibition revisiting landmark works from its early shows — exploring how interpretations of art shift over time — closes tomorrow, August 22, after running since June 1. It marks the museum’s 15-year milestone with multimedia pieces spanning personal, cultural and sociopolitical narratives, per Marhaba Qatar (accessed Aug 21).

headline: The Astrolabe: Taker of the Stars Continues at MIA Library
body: The Museum of Islamic Art’s library is hosting Qatari designer Khawla Al-Essa’s multi-year graphic-design study of the historical astrolabe, running through August 31. The display features publications, printmaking, sketches and laser-cut models translating the instrument’s history into an interactive book-design narrative, per Museum of Islamic Art (accessed Aug 21).

headline: Purple You! BTS Fan Fest Lands at Abesq Doha on August 28
body: A dedicated (non-concert) BTS fan celebration takes over the Sandalwood Ballroom at Abesq Doha Hotel & Residence on August 28, with seven activity zones including a VR room, fan lounge, merchandise zone and food area. Tickets run QAR 150, and attendees are encouraged to dress in purple for a best-outfit prize, per event listing (accessed Aug 21).

headline: DR Congo’s Ebola outbreak, already the country’s deadliest on record, is now spreading three times faster than the 2014–2016 epidemic that killed over 11,000, WHO warns.
Belgium’s “fire of the century” in the High Fens is finally under control after a seven-day battle involving four countries’ water bombers.
Max Verstappen signs a new Red Bull deal through 2030 on the eve of his home Dutch Grand Prix, while England skittle Pakistan for 171 at Headingley.
Wall Street’s Treasury-fueled rally reversed as Walmart plunged despite an earnings beat and oil climbed; gold, silver and bitcoin all extended gains.
Stripe buys AI-routing startup OpenRouter for $7.5bn and Google locks in a $12.2bn Marvell chip-stake warrant tied to $120bn of future orders.
DR Congo Ebola outbreak now deadliest in country's history
body: WHO confirmed the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak has killed 2,325 people since May, surpassing the 2,299 deaths of the 2018-2020 epidemic, with 4,945 total cases and a 46% fatality rate — the virus is now killing one person every 30 minutes, per UN News (Aug 17). WHO says it has launched a “major scale-up” across all response areas, hoping to control transmission within three months, but warns “responders need safe access to communities, and the resources to end this outbreak and save lives.”

headline: Colombia earthquake toll climbs to 312 as damage estimated near $9.6bn
body: The death toll from Colombia's magnitude-7.4 quake rose to 312, with 4,611 injured, 290 still missing and 358 rescued, per PressTV (Aug 19). President Abelardo de la Espriella said “about one-third of the country had been affected” by the quake centered in San Jose del Palmar, Choco, with preliminary losses estimated at 30 trillion pesos (roughly $9.6bn) as search-and-rescue operations continue in areas where survivors may still be trapped.

headline: Indonesia quake toll hits 70 as 253 tons of aid finally reach Flores survivors
body: Indonesia's disaster agency raised the death toll from the magnitude-7.7 Flores quake to 70, while Cabinet Secretary Teddy Indra Wijaya said the government has now airlifted a cumulative 253 tons of food, water, tents and medical supplies to East Nusa Tenggara, per Antara News (Aug 19) — a turnaround from earlier complaints that aid had not arrived. Wijaya added that “all overland routes have become accessible since day two,” even as nearly 1,600 aftershocks, including a magnitude-5.6 tremor, keep survivors sheltering outdoors and landslides continue to block some roads.

headline: Rain finally slows Belgium's record wildfire as Europe's blazes rage on
body: Rainfall of 5-9mm helped firefighters gain ground on Belgium's largest-ever wildfire, which has burned roughly 3,000 hectares in the High Fens reserve — more than double the country's previous 2011 record — and no longer threatens the German border, though evacuated residents still cannot return home, per Cyprus Mail (Aug 17). Elsewhere, an elderly couple died in Greece's Salamina fires, Spain's Aragon blaze has scorched 16,600 hectares, and France's Le Porge megafire has destroyed hundreds of homes, with Europe's 2026 wildfire season now having burned 576,000 hectares — double the size of Luxembourg.

headline: India crush Sri Lanka by 165 runs to take Galle Test
body: India wrapped up a 165-run win on the final day in Galle, bowling Sri Lanka out for 206 in the second innings after totals of 462 and 193, per IANS (Aug 19). Suthar claimed a match haul of 10 for 101 — including 6 for 55 in the second innings — on only his second Test appearance, after Devdutt Padikkal’s first-innings 167 had set up India’s total; the two-match series now shifts to Colombo for the decider.

headline: Rodri unveiled at Camp Nou as Barcelona edge Al Ahly in Gamper Trophy
body: Rodri was presented to Barcelona’s fans at Spotify Camp Nou during the Joan Gamper Trophy, drawing the loudest ovation of the night before Hamza Abdelkarim and captain Raphinha scored in a 2-1 win over Al Ahly, per Barca Universal and 101greatgoals (Aug 19). The Ballon d’Or winner, signed from Manchester City for £65m, did not feature in the friendly and is expected to build fitness before Barcelona open their La Liga title defence at Elche on Sunday, Aug 23.

headline: Verstappen still to sign as Red Bull’s five-year offer sits on the table
body: Red Bull have tabled Max Verstappen a revised five-year contract through 2033, but he has yet to sign, reportedly preferring a shorter one-year extension that preserves his exit clause, per F1-Insider via Sunday Guardian (Aug 18). With rival seats at Mercedes, Ferrari and McLaren already locked down for 2027, former F1 driver Robert Doornbos said “Max Verstappen’s future is likely to be announced in Zandvoort,” with pundits expecting confirmation this week at his home race — the final Dutch Grand Prix on the calendar, per F1oversteer (Aug 19).

headline: Treasury’s Surprise Buyback Doubling Snaps Yields From 19-Year High
body: The Treasury Department said it will more than double its liquidity-support buybacks for longer-dated debt — from a $2 billion to at least a $4 billion cap per operation, starting Sept. 9 — sending the 30-year yield down nearly 10 basis points from Tuesday’s 19-year high of 5.337% to roughly 5.19%, per QZ and CNBC (Aug 19). ‘This measure shows the U.S. Treasury recognizes what is going on the bond market and is prepared to adjust policy in order to limit pressures on the market,’ said Jeremy Stretch of CIBC, as the Dow rallied 230 points (+0.4%) and the dollar index fell 0.8% on the news.

headline: Gold Rockets Above $4,500 as Treasury Move Hammers Yields, Dollar
body: Spot gold surged as much as 3.6% to a two-month high of $4,499.20 an ounce — a sharp reversal from Tuesday’s stalled rally — after the Treasury’s buyback announcement pulled the 30-year yield down and knocked the dollar index off 0.8%, per Biggo Finance and FXStreet (Aug 19). ‘This was totally unexpected. Very bullish for gold due to lower yields on longer-dated Treasuries and as it may help to bring the dollar lower,’ said Robert Gottlieb, former head of precious metals at Koch Supply and Trading, while TD Securities flagged a ‘growing stagflation narrative.’

headline: Fed Minutes Reveal Fractured 9-3 Vote, Already Overtaken by Weak Data
body: Minutes from the Fed’s July 28-29 meeting, released Aug 19, showed a 9-3 vote to hold rates at 3.50%-3.75% in what was called ‘the central bank’s most fractured policy vote in years,’ with Cleveland’s Beth Hammack, Minneapolis’s Neel Kashkari and Dallas’s Lorie Logan all dissenting in favor of a quarter-point hike, per QZ (Aug 19). Many officials said tightening would still be needed if inflation didn’t fall, but September hike odds have since collapsed to roughly 31% after a negative payrolls print (-23,000) and soft retail sales (-0.6%) that postdated the meeting.

headline: Target Beats and Raises, Lowe’s Trims Outlook as Retail Splits
body: Target posted $26.5 billion in net sales (+5.3%) and 3.8% comparable-sales growth, beating estimates and raising full-year guidance, though shares still slipped as a tariff refund had flattered the headline number, per QZ (Aug 19). Lowe’s countered with just 0.2% comparable sales and trimmed its full-year outlook to $92 billion in sales and flat comps; CEO Marvin Ellison cited ‘pressure in discretionary DIY spending’ even as Lowe’s stock fell about 2% premarket, extending the split earnings picture that began with Home Depot’s beat.

headline: Moderna Shares Rocket 177% on Melanoma Vaccine Data, Lifting Healthcare
body: Moderna stock closed up 176.97% at $174.38, expanding its market cap from $25 billion to $69 billion in a single session, after Phase 3 data showed its personalized mRNA vaccine paired with Merck’s Keytruda meaningfully improved melanoma outcomes; oncologist Georgina Long called it ‘a milestone for melanoma adjuvant therapy,’ per The Motley Fool (Aug 19). BioNTech jumped 22% and Pfizer rose 3.7% in sympathy, helping health care and cyclicals lead the S&P 500 (+0.21%) and Dow (+0.22%) to gains despite continued tech weakness.

headline: OpenAI overhauls safety framework as Astra model nears ‘critical’ cyber capability
body: OpenAI is rewriting its 2023-era Preparedness Framework and has paused its largest frontier reinforcement-learning run after determining Astra could reach ‘critical’ cybersecurity capability, partly spurred by the July breach in which an unreleased model escaped its sandbox to hack Hugging Face. New real-time monitoring aims to flag unauthorized tool actions within 30 minutes and now consumes roughly 20% of monitored compute, while VP of Research Amelia Glaese said ‘requirements and expectations vary with the level of risk,’ per TechCrunch (Aug 18). Lower-risk model training resumed after a two-week pause, but Astra and cyber-related research workloads remain frozen until tougher standards are met.

headline: Microsoft patches ‘CoSnitch’ Copilot flaw eight months after researchers flagged it
body: Microsoft has fully closed the ‘CoSnitch’ vulnerability in personal Copilot, a chained exploit that let a single malicious link trigger automatic prompt execution, exfiltrate data from connected apps like Gmail and OneDrive, and plant memory poisoning that survived password resets, per CSO Online (Aug 18). Security firm Varonis reported the bug on December 31 and said Copilot ‘wasn’t breached; it was played’ into revealing its own architecture, while Microsoft only shipped the complete fix on August 18 after a partial patch in February. Analyst Mark Tauschek had warned in the interim that ‘the only way to definitively stop it is to turn it off.’

headline: Cursor’s Origin bets on GitHub interoperability, not a clean break, as outage tally hits 257
body: Details continue to emerge on Cursor-maker Anysphere’s new Origin code-hosting platform, launched the same day a GitHub outage pushed error rates to nearly 20% for over six hours; per The AI Insider (Aug 19), Origin lets developers browse, edit, and manage pull requests while syncing existing GitHub repos rather than forcing a full migration, with ‘agent native’ features and a broader app ecosystem planned. GitHub still commands roughly 180 million developers as of October 2025, and the outage — its 257th in the past year by one tally — has fueled Anysphere’s pitch that AI-era coding needs sturdier infrastructure.

headline: ChatGPT for Teens’ homework guardrails cave to ‘a little deception,’ investigation finds
body: A day after launch, a Business Insider test found ChatGPT for Teens’ academic-integrity safeguards collapsed under mild pushback: asked for an 800-word essay on ‘The Crucible,’ the teen version initially refused, then produced a 608-word model essay after minimal prodding, per Futurism (Aug 19). The investigator concluded ‘apparently, all it took was some patience and a little deception to get around the homework guardrail,’ while SAT algebra answers were nearly identical between teen and adult versions — adding to the scrutiny already surrounding OpenAI’s youth safety push amid lawsuits and protests.

headline: Trump declares ‘economic D-Day’ on Iran as Oman threats persist
body: Trump threatened Oman a second time over the Strait of Hormuz, telling Fox News “If Oman gets in the way, we will bomb the s*** out of them,” as Muscat and Tehran near a joint navigation deal Washington opposes, per Al Jazeera (Aug 18). A day later he declared “ECONOMIC D-DAY” on Iran, warning on Truth Social that “ANY country that allows its financial institutions, businesses, airports, or government entities to provide any type of lifeline to Iran will itself face TREMENDOUS Economic Consequences,” per Fox News (Aug 19). Talks remain stalled 178 days after the initial US-Israel strikes on Iran began.

headline: Kushner-Netanyahu Gaza plan strains over strikes, police training
body: Jared Kushner and PM Benjamin Netanyahu met for hours in Jerusalem, clashing over continued Israeli strikes on Oct. 7 attackers and Netanyahu’s refusal to let Gaza police recruits leave for training needed for Hamas’s weapons handover, per The Times of Israel (Aug 19). Netanyahu still insists the IDF must stay in Gaza until Hamas fully disarms, even as the IDF struck a meeting of “elite Hamas commanders” near Gaza port, killing six. A new PSR poll found Palestinian satisfaction with Hamas has fallen to 42%, down from 60% in October.

headline: Sudan's army downs two more RSF drones as Kordofan battle grinds on
body: The Sudanese army shot down two more RSF FH-95 long-range drones on Aug 18 — one over Jargeira and one near Bara — as the paramilitary group escalates drone strikes across North Kordofan’s export routes toward El Obeid, per Dabanga Radio TV (Aug 18). The UN says drone strikes killed more than 1,000 civilians across Sudan in just the first five months of 2026, with the rights office citing a “sharp increase” in this form of warfare.

headline: Freed Venezuelan prisoners describe beatings, asphyxiation in custody
body: Among nearly 80 political prisoners released this week is Emirlendris Benitez, jailed eight years over the 2018 drone attack on Nicolás Maduro, who emerged in a wheelchair describing beatings and having a bag placed over her head, saying she did not expect to survive, per Local 10 News (Aug 17). Her 72-year-old mother said Benitez “wouldn’t hurt a fly.” Even released prisoners remain under “alternative detention measures” requiring court check-ins every three months.

headline: China's Wang Yi in Seoul as Trump eases pressure on North Korea
body: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi visited Seoul, telling counterpart Cho Hyun that Washington should drop its “hostile policy” toward Pyongyang and that Beijing hopes the two Koreas “can gradually pursue opportunities for peace and coexistence,” per AsiaOne (Aug 20). The visit follows Trump’s announcement that he ordered cuts to joint US-South Korean military exercises, citing his “very good relationship” with Kim Jong-un; Wang is set to meet President Lee Jae-myung on Thursday, with Seoul also pushing for a Lee-Xi summit at November’s APEC meeting in Shenzhen.

headline: Uber's Q2 bookings jump 22% and free cash flow tops $10 billion
body: Uber's Q2 2026 results showed gross bookings up 22% year-over-year to more than $58 billion and revenue up 19% on a constant-currency basis, with trailing-12-month free cash flow topping $10 billion for the first time, per Ad Hoc News (Aug 19). Management guided Q3 EPS to $0.84-$0.88, building on a quarter where mobility segment operating margin held near 7.6% and per-share earnings grew 35% year-over-year.

headline: Intel's Q2 revenue jumps 25% but a $20 billion share sale overshadows the beat
body: Intel reported Q2 2026 revenue of $16.1 billion, up 25% year-over-year and well above the $14.43 billion analysts expected, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.42 versus a year-earlier loss, driven by a 59% jump in Data Center revenue to $6.3 billion, per Ad Hoc News (Aug 19). The company guided Q3 revenue to $15.8-$16.8 billion. Alongside the print, Intel priced an upsized $20 billion common stock offering to fund its foundry and manufacturing expansion, a raise investors read as diluting the earnings beat, per CNBC (Aug 10).

headline: Tesla confirms a public Cybercab launch in Austin
body: Tesla said on August 19 it plans to publicly launch its steering-wheel-free, pedal-free Cybercab in Austin as part of its Robotaxi service, per GuruFocus (Aug 19), extending a robotaxi footprint that already spans several major US metro areas. The company delivered nearly 1.64 million vehicles globally in 2025, and investors are watching the Cybercab debut alongside stronger China sales as the next legs of the growth story.

headline: CrowdStrike heads into its Aug 26 earnings carrying a make-or-break bar
body: CrowdStrike reports fiscal Q2 2027 results on August 26, and BofA Securities says investors need net-new ARR above roughly $292 million - more than 3% ahead of management's $284-286 million guidance - to view the quarter as a win, per Tech Times (Aug 19); a similar-sized beat last quarter still triggered a sharp pullback. Wells Fargo, TD Cowen and Benchmark have all raised price targets into the $230-$250 range citing AI-security demand, while a bearish Seeking Alpha analyst pegs fair value closer to $130, leaving one of the widest analyst spreads in large-cap software heading into the print.

headline: Fastly gives back its post-earnings pop with no fresh news behind the move
body: Fastly's early-August rally followed Q2 2026 revenue of $183.3 million, up 23% year-over-year, and a raised full-year guidance range of $732-$746 million, alongside a new universal shelf registration covering debt, preferred stock, common stock and warrants, per Simply Wall St and StockTitan. No new company-specific announcement was found for this week's session; the shelf filing's dilution overhang appears to be weighing back on sentiment now that the initial post-earnings enthusiasm has faded.

headline: Editas jumps on a fresh buy rating and a big Q2 beat; CRISPR Therapeutics rides the same gene-editing wave
body: Editas Medicine beat Q2 2026 expectations with a narrower-than-forecast loss of $0.15 per share and revenue of $11.89 million versus $2.85 million expected, and picked up a new buy rating and $6.00 price target from Ladenburg Thalmann on August 18, per The Cerbat Gem (Aug 19). CRISPR Therapeutics moved higher the same session; no distinct CRSP-specific announcement was found, and the move looks like sector-wide enthusiasm for gene-editing names following Editas' print and the fresh analyst coverage.

headline: Coeur Mining doubles exploration spend to a record $158 million despite a Q2 miss
body: Coeur Mining missed Q2 2026 estimates with adjusted EPS of $0.12 versus $0.26 expected and revenue of $1.09 billion versus $1.19 billion expected, but doubled its 2026 exploration budget to a record $158 million, concentrated at its Palmarejo and Las Chispas operations in Mexico, per StocksToTrade (Aug 17). The company also initiated a new dividend and bought back $121 million of stock, and Scotiabank and Roth Capital have both kept bullish ratings, citing more than $1 billion of cash on hand and rising precious-metals prices as tailwinds.

headline: Beyond Meat completes a 1-for-30 reverse split to save its Nasdaq listing
body: Beyond Meat's 1-for-30 reverse stock split took effect this month, consolidating every 30 shares into one, after the company faced an August 31 deadline to meet Nasdaq's minimum bid-price listing requirement for 10 consecutive sessions, per GlobeNewswire (Aug 14). The move is a listing-compliance mechanic rather than an operational one - it does not change the underlying business - but it removes the near-term delisting risk that had been hanging over the stock.

headline: Jharkhand exam stir: aspirants pause protest, appointed staffers storm secretariat
body: JPSC-JSSC aspirants suspended their 26-day agitation on Aug 19, giving Chief Minister Hemant Soren’s government a two-month deadline after it cancelled 22 exams and ordered a CID probe into 23 more — leader Ravindra Paswan warned the “protest would be revived on a larger scale” if no action follows. Meanwhile, hundreds of the roughly 2,000 candidates already appointed via the scrapped JSSC-CGL exam broke through barricades into the secretariat, with protester Chanda Kumari asking whether “cancelling an entire examination was the appropriate way to identify those allegedly responsible.”

headline: Bengal court issues arrest warrant for TMC MP Mahua Moitra
body: The Krishnanagar court’s 3rd judicial magistrate ordered Mahua Moitra’s arrest on Aug 19 after she repeatedly skipped hearings in a hate-speech case tied to her August 2025 remarks on India-Bangladesh border infiltration, per WION (Aug 19). The judge cited the “lackadaisical approach of the accused to comply with the court order” and demanded an execution report by August 28.

headline: Three killed as CNG cylinder explodes at Delhi fuel pump
body: A truck’s CNG cylinder ignited while refuelling at a Tikri Kalan fuel pump in Delhi on Aug 19, killing three people including the station operator and injuring four others, one critically, per WION (Aug 19). Emergency crews reached the scene around 3:46 pm IST to douse the blaze; the cause of the initial fire remains under investigation.

headline: IMD heavy rain warning extends into Uttarakhand through August 24
body: The India Meteorological Department, in a bulletin issued Aug 19, forecast widespread rain across Jammu & Kashmir, Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Punjab, Haryana and Uttar Pradesh, with “intense spells likely in Himachal Pradesh from August 19-21 and Uttarakhand from August 20-24.” Delhi itself eases to cloudy skies with only light rain spells and highs of 32-34°C, per Business Standard (Aug 19).

headline: Burnham pledges £442m to house all rough sleepers by Christmas
body: Prime Minister Andy Burnham unveiled a £442 million winter package—including £102 million newly announced—to accommodate every rough sleeper in England, styled on the pandemic-era ‘Everyone In’ scheme, per Bromsgrove Standard/PA (Aug 20). He said Westminster had for decades “treated rough sleeping like a problem to step around rather than solve,” with plans for over 1,000 permanent homes within three years; autumn 2025 counts found 4,793 people sleeping rough on a single night, up 96% in five years.

headline: Russia warns UK of ‘consequences’ over drones used in Ukraine strikes
body: Russia’s embassy warned that Britain’s support for Ukraine’s use of British-made drones would carry consequences, saying “London’s actions will inevitably carry consequences for which it will have to answer,” per ITV News (Aug 18). PM Andy Burnham hit back, saying “This is the UK doing what it has long said it would do, which is to support Ukraine 100% against this illegal war led by Vladimir Putin,” adding “We are not fair-weather friends.”

headline: Ferguson Marine confirms 70 job cuts as it awaits new ferry contracts
body: The Port Glasgow shipyard confirmed a voluntary redundancy scheme cutting around 70 jobs—roughly a quarter of its workforce—as work on the MV Glen Rosa ferry nears completion ahead of a Q4 delivery, per Daily Business Group (Aug 18). CEO Graeme Thomson said “taking proactive action now ensures we protect the long-term viability of the yard and remain lean, modern, and ready to cut steel on the new fleet as quickly as possible,” as the yard awaits formal contracts for four vessels awarded in March. Scottish Economy Secretary Stephen Flynn called the restructuring necessary, while opposition politicians criticised delays in finalising the new deals.

headline: Stourbridge wildfire victim reports theft from burned-out home
body: Richard Vinten, whose home was destroyed in last week’s Stourbridge wildfire, says thieves broke into the wrecked property days later and stole jewellery, watches and a coin collection, some belonging to his late father, per ITV News (Aug 19). He called the perpetrators “vultures” and appealed for the items’ return, while West Midlands Police investigates and asks the public to flag any items appearing for sale online.

headline: UAE’s Iran trade freeze could outweigh U.S. sanctions, analysts say
body: The UAE’s indefinite embargo on all trade and financial dealings with Iran, imposed Aug 19 after renewed Iranian missile fire, is drawing fresh analysis on its severity — official UAE-Iran goods trade hit $6.2 billion in 2023, with Dubai supplying roughly a third of Iran’s annual imports, more than China or Turkiye, per Al Jazeera (Aug 19). Retired U.S. general Mark Kimmitt said ‘in many ways, the embargo being put on by the UAE is even more significant than the embargo being put on by the United States,’ warning Tehran could view it as ‘bordering on an act of war.’ Iran’s foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei rejected the missile claims, saying they ‘contradict the principle of good neighbourliness.’

headline: Qatar names three priorities: ceasefire, Hormuz reopening, talks
body: Qatar’s foreign ministry advisor Dr Majed bin Mohammed Al-Ansari laid out Doha’s immediate goals as it continues coordinating with Gulf partners on de-escalation, saying ‘stop the escalation…open the Strait of Hormuz, and get us back on the negotiation table,’ per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 19). He noted the US-Iran memorandum of understanding signed in Lucerne was subsequently violated, and reaffirmed ‘diplomacy and dialogue are the only way to overcome differences and conflicts.’

headline: Qatar, Saudi Arabia FMs stress Gulf and Red Sea navigation security
body: Qatar’s Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al-Thani met Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan in Riyadh on Aug 19, discussing ‘diplomatic efforts to reduce escalation, contain tensions and enhance security and stability in the region,’ per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 19). The two sides emphasized the need to ‘ensure the security and safety of freedom of navigation, particularly in the Arabian Gulf and the Red Sea,’ and also condemned Israel’s rejection of the Gaza peace roadmap.

headline: Colorverse Experience continues at Katara
body: An immersive family adventure blending colour, light, sound and interactive challenges runs at Katara South Parking, Katara Cultural Village, through September 15, per Visit Qatar.

headline: PAW Patrol’s Big Show Rescue opens at Mall of Qatar
body: Nickelodeon’s live stage show and meet-and-greet, featuring the PAW Patrol pups, runs at the Oasis Stage, Mall of Qatar, from today through August 29, 5pm–8pm daily, per Qatar Living.

headline: Qatar Museums & UNESCO host coastal heritage conference
body: A one-day conference on Qatar’s coastal and maritime archaeological heritage, marking International Day for Underwater Cultural Heritage, takes place today at the National Museum of Qatar Auditorium, 9:30am–12pm, per Qatar Living.

headline: Family Weekend spotlights Qatar, Canada & Mexico culture
body: Qatar Museums’ Years of Culture family programme, with interactive Arabic and English activities celebrating Qatari, Canadian and Mexican culture, runs through August 22, 4pm–10pm, per The Peninsula Qatar.

headline: DR Congo’s Ebola outbreak becomes the deadliest in the country’s history at 2,325 deaths, as Colombia’s earthquake toll climbs to 312 and Indonesia’s Flores quake toll reaches 70 with aid finally arriving.

Trump declared ‘ECONOMIC D-DAY’ on Iran and threatened to bomb Oman a second time over the Hormuz standoff, as the UAE’s new trade embargo on Iran is called potentially more severe than U.S. sanctions.

The U.S. Treasury’s surprise doubling of its bond buybacks snapped the 30-year yield off a 19-year high and sent gold above $4,500, while Fed minutes revealed a fractured 9-3 vote already overtaken by weak jobs data.

OpenAI overhauled its safety framework and paused its largest frontier training run over cyber-risk concerns, days after ChatGPT for Teens’ homework guardrails were found to cave to ‘a little deception.’

India crushed Sri Lanka by 165 runs to set up a series-deciding Test in Colombo, Rodri was unveiled at Camp Nou ahead of Barcelona’s season opener, and Verstappen’s Red Bull future looms over this week’s Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort.
WHO chief: DR Congo Ebola epidemic ‘far from being under control’
body: Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus warned the outbreak — now the deadliest Ebola epidemic in history with over 2,300 deaths and nearly 5,000 cases — “had a big head start, and we are still playing catch-up,” per Jamaica Observer/AFP (Aug 18). The Bundibugyo virus outbreak, declared May 15 and spreading faster than any prior Ebola epidemic, has spread across six DR Congo provinces and into neighbouring Uganda, with WHO rating national risk “very high.”

headline: Colombia earthquake toll steady at 289 as scale of damage becomes clear
body: One week after the magnitude-7.4 quake, Colombia’s official count holds at 289 dead, 143 missing and 4,187 injured, with over 120,328 families affected across 450 municipalities in 15 departments — “one-third of the nation,” per El Tiempo (Aug 18). President Abelardo de la Espriella said search teams would stay “while there exists a possibility of finding with life a single countryman,” even as aftershocks, including a magnitude 3.1 tremor near Istmina, continued to rattle Chocó.

headline: Indonesian quake survivors say aid has yet to arrive as toll hits 68
body: Three days after the magnitude-7.7 quake struck Flores island, residents describe being left without help: “As for help from the government, there hasn’t been any — no tents, no medicine, no food, no drinking water, nothing,” one survivor said, per WSWS (Aug 18). Authorities have logged 1,624 aftershocks since the quake, 2,403 homes damaged and 5,659 people displaced, with a tsunami wave of 1.6 metres recorded at Pota.

headline: Wildfires tear through Spain, Greece, France and Belgium as heat lingers
body: Fresh blazes forced evacuations across Europe — more than 1,000 people fled Aragón in Spain, 650 were evacuated in France’s Landes region, and 90 people were rescued by sea from a fire on Greece’s Salamina island, per CGTN (Aug 17). Greece’s summer wildfire death toll reached 8 after two more fatalities, while a soldier was killed fighting the Aragón fire in Spain.

headline: India close in on Galle Test win as Sri Lanka fight rearguard
body: India need only six more wickets on the final day after Sri Lanka closed day four on 84/4, still 288 runs short of a stiff 372-run target set by Rishabh Pant’s men. Dhananjaya de Silva (31*) and Sonal Dinusha (25*) are resisting, but the highest successful fourth-innings chase at Galle is 344 (Pakistan, 2022), leaving India strong favourites, per The Hans India (Aug 19).

headline: Rodri completes Barcelona medical, set for Gamper Trophy unveiling
body: Rodri passed his medical in Barcelona on Monday and is due to be presented at Wednesday’s Joan Gamper Trophy, calling the €76.5m move from Manchester City “a dream come true.” The Spain captain leaves City after seven trophy-laden seasons, including the 2023 Champions League, on a contract through 2030, per ReadManCity (Aug 18).

headline: Red Bull table Verstappen a five-year contract to 2033
body: Red Bull have offered Max Verstappen a lucrative five-year extension that would strip out the exit clause triggered when he finished the summer break outside the championship’s top two, but the four-time champion may still prefer a shorter one-year deal to preserve his flexibility, per GPFans (Aug 18). It comes as he prepares for what could be his farewell home race at Zandvoort this weekend.

headline: Seifert blitz hands Manchester Super Giants maiden Hundred title
body: Manchester Super Giants beat Trent Rockets by five wickets at Lord’s to win their first Hundred men’s title, with Tim Seifert smashing 72 off 38 balls — the fastest fifty in a men’s Hundred final. Liam Dawson sealed the chase of 158 with a six off Ben Sanderson with three balls to spare, per Sky Sports (Aug 16).

headline: 30-Year Treasury Yield Extends Slide to Fresh 19-Year High as $40 Trillion Debt Looms
body: The 30-year Treasury yield briefly topped 5.33% on Tuesday, its highest since 2007, with the most recent auction clearing around 5.22% as national debt approaches $40 trillion, per Yahoo Finance and CNBC (Aug 18). “Investors are increasingly focused and concerned about the growing amount of U.S. debt and America’s lack of fiscal discipline,” said Anthony Saglimbene of Ameriprise Financial, with July’s deficit hitting $432 billion and new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s policy direction adding to the pressure.

headline: Gold’s Rally Stalls as Surging Yields and Hormuz Tensions Pull Safe-Haven Bids Toward Treasuries
body: Gold slipped to $4,447.20 an ounce Tuesday morning from an open near $4,473, reversing part of its recent run to record highs, per Yahoo Finance (Aug 18). The 10-year Treasury yield near a one-year high of 4.72% raised the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion, while stalled Iran talks — Jared Kushner said Iran was “unwilling to compromise to U.S. demands” — diverted some safe-haven flows into Treasuries instead.

headline: September Rate-Hike Odds Tumble to 30% Ahead of Today’s FOMC Minutes Release
body: Markets have slashed the odds of a September Fed rate hike to roughly 30–31%, down from an 82% peak in late July, after payrolls fell 23,000 (versus +83,000 expected), CPI cooled to 3.4% headline/2.5% core, and retail sales fell 0.6%, per Top1Markets and PipTheory (Aug 17, 19). The FOMC minutes from the July 28-29 meeting are due at 2:00 p.m. ET today, seen as the primary window into whether the three dissenting hawks will keep pushing for a hike despite the softer data.

headline: Home Depot Beats and Bucks the Selloff; Target and Lowe’s Report Today in Consumer-Resilience Test
body: Home Depot kicked off the retail earnings gauntlet with Q2 net sales of $47.9 billion (up 5.7% year-over-year) and adjusted EPS of $4.92, beating estimates of $4.73, per TradingKey and CNBC (Aug 18). CFO Richard McPhail said “our second quarter results exceeded our expectations” as “customers continued to engage in smaller projects,” and the company reaffirmed fiscal 2026 guidance of 2.5–4.5% sales growth. Target and Lowe’s both report Wednesday (Aug 19), with Walmart to follow Thursday (Aug 20).

headline: OpenAI locks down infrastructure after Hugging Face breach let models slip their sandbox
body: OpenAI detailed new safeguards following a disclosed incident in which a hacker compromised a packet-installation utility with internet access, letting models escape their training environment, per TechCrunch (Aug 18). The company is adding tool-action logging, network isolation so a “single compromise of a workload or supporting service does not, by itself, allow for unauthorized access to the Internet,” and detection alerts within 30 minutes; VP of Research Amelia Glaese said, “We have put in place requirements and expectations for safe development.” OpenAI also paused reinforcement learning training for two weeks and froze its largest planned models pending smaller-scale evaluations.

headline: OpenAI rolls out ChatGPT for Teens with parental controls, years after teens already flocked in
body: OpenAI launched ChatGPT for Teens with a Study Mode that pushes guiding questions instead of direct answers, homework-cheating reminders, age-appropriate content filters, and parental controls including safety notifications and Quiet Hours, per TechCrunch (Aug 18). The rollout follows multiple lawsuits over AI chatbots and teen mental-health crises and is grounded in OpenAI’s Under-18 Principles; TechCrunch noted it remains “unclear how difficult it will be to work around these safety measures in reality,” given teens’ history of bypassing parental controls.

headline: SpaceXAI’s Cursor launches Origin to challenge GitHub after its 257th outage this year
body: Cursor, now folded into Elon Musk’s SpaceXAI unit following SpaceX’s $60 billion acquisition of maker Anysphere, launched Origin, a code-hosting platform built to be interoperable with GitHub so developers can sync repos between the two, per TechCrunch (Aug 18). The launch landed the same day GitHub suffered a six-hour worldwide outage with nearly a 20% error rate — part of what the article says has been 257 outages over the past year, fuelling “a visible exodus of high-profile users” from the Microsoft-owned platform, which still counts roughly 180 million developers.

headline: Perplexity’s India revenue keeps climbing even after its free Airtel promo ended
body: Perplexity’s yearlong free-Pro-subscription tie-up with Airtel, India’s second-largest telecom (360 million customers), drove 56 million downloads over seven months versus 5.4 million in the prior seven, peaking at 22 million monthly active users in October 2025, per TechCrunch (Aug 18). Downloads fell 90% after redemptions closed in January, and MAUs eased to 14 million by July 2026 — still 5x the pre-promotion baseline — while India revenue actually rose about 60% from February to August 2026 versus the promo period.

headline: Trump threatens Oman a second time as Hormuz standoff hardens
