body: With the 60-day US-Iran memorandum now expired, Trump told Fox News on Aug 17, “If Oman gets in the way, we’ll bomb the s*** out of them,” even as Tehran and Muscat announced they are nearing a new shipping-mechanism agreement for the strait — directly contradicting Washington’s demand that Iran cede control, per Al Jazeera (Aug 18). An IRGC spokesman dismissed Trump’s claim of direct backchannel talks as “merely fantasies caused by the delusions and nightmares he has suffered as a result of defeat and desperation.”

headline: Kushner-Netanyahu Hamas disarmament plan advances, but gaps remain
body: A day after Kushner met Hamas leader Khalil al-Hayya in Egypt, Kushner and Netanyahu agreed Monday to set up working groups on Hamas “demilitarization,” under which weapons would move via the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza to an International Stabilization Force for destruction under American oversight, per HNGN (Aug 18). Hamas is still demanding Israel halt attacks and pull back to the Yellow Line first, a condition Israel has rejected, with more than 1,250 Palestinians killed since the October ceasefire began.

headline: UNIFIL logs 137 projectiles a day into Lebanon as strikes intensify
body: UNIFIL said it has “documented an average of 137 projectiles fired into Lebanon from Israel daily over the past two weeks,” with Aug 18 alone bringing shelling near Majdal Zoun, raids on homes around Shebaa, and drones over Beirut’s southern suburbs, per Antiwar.com (Aug 18). A UN spokesperson called the pace “alarming,” citing a weekend strike on Ansar and Deir al-Zahrani that killed at least 11 people and wounded 19, and warning of a shift toward direct civilian targeting.

headline: Sudan’s army downs two more RSF drones in North Kordofan
body: Sudan’s military said air defences destroyed two RSF FH-95 drones on Aug 17 — one over the Jureijikh area and another near the town of Bara — bringing to seven the number of RSF drones downed in the Kordofan region since June, per Sudan Tribune (Aug 17). The RSF has stepped up drone strikes to pressure the army’s hold on export corridors toward El Obeid after losing ground in a July 25 offensive that secured the Khartoum-El Obeid highway.

headline: Venezuela’s freed political prisoners emerge with torture accounts
body: Nearly 80 more political prisoners have been released in Venezuela as part of negotiations toward free elections following Nicolás Maduro’s removal from power, per Local10/AP (Aug 17). Among them, Emirlendris Benitez — jailed eight years over an alleged 2018 drone plot against Maduro — said she “was beat, kicked and had a bag placed over her head until she could no longer breathe,” leaving her needing a wheelchair after delayed medical care; many released still face court check-ins every three months under “alternative detention measures.”

headline: Oracle’s AI-driven debt load draws fresh scrutiny after credit downgrade
body: S&P Global cut Oracle’s credit rating to BBB—one notch above junk—in July, and credit default swap spreads have since climbed to roughly 219 basis points, their highest in years, as the company’s AI data-center buildout outpaces revenue growth; per TheStreet (Aug 14), long-term debt rose from $85.3 billion to $122.3 billion over the past year, with free cash flow negative $23.7 billion in fiscal 2026. Oracle’s CFO has said the company expects to raise roughly $40 billion more in debt and equity in fiscal 2027 to keep funding its data-center expansion.

headline: Intel prices upsized $20 billion share sale to fund foundry turnaround
body: Intel upsized a planned common-stock offering to roughly $20 billion, selling about 210.5 million new shares at $95 each with a $2.25 billion overallotment option, earmarking proceeds for capital expenditure and working capital as it funds its semiconductor foundry ambitions; per Timothy Sykes News (Aug 18), the raise is explicitly framed as funding for the company’s turnaround.

headline: Meta faces California trial as 29 state attorneys general seek child-safety damages
body: Meta is contesting a California trial brought by attorneys general from 29 states, who accuse the company of improperly collecting children’s data and misrepresenting the safety of its platforms; per Yahoo Finance (Aug 18), damages estimates cited in the case range from roughly $200 billion to as high as $1.4 trillion. The litigation adds legal overhang just as Meta’s AI infrastructure spending is projected to reach $145 billion this year.

headline: Arm flags slowing smartphone royalty growth as chip-sector rotation deepens
body: Arm Holdings management signaled a sequential deceleration in smartphone royalty growth, citing rising component costs squeezing handset makers, while regulatory filings show more than $39 million in insider selling over the past year with no offsetting purchases; per TradingKey (Aug 18), several Wall Street firms have trimmed price targets, though the average still sits above $273.

headline: Johnson & Johnson lifts full-year guidance as sales near $100 billion milestone
body: Johnson & Johnson reported second-quarter sales of $25.31 billion, up 6.6% year-on-year, with adjusted earnings of $2.90 per share, and raised its 2026 outlook to roughly $101.1 billion in revenue and $11.68 in adjusted EPS at the midpoint; per Yahoo Finance (Aug 18), the results put the company within reach of the $100 billion annual sales mark few healthcare giants have crossed.

headline: Rackspace swings to wider loss as legacy cloud business shrinks
body: Rackspace Technology posted second-quarter revenue of $670.1 million, roughly flat year-on-year, but swung to a net loss of $67.5 million from a small first-quarter profit as non-GAAP gross margin slipped to 18.6% from 19.8%; per Simply Wall St (Aug 12), management now expects full-year revenue to decline around 7% as legacy public-cloud operations shrink during the company’s AI-infrastructure transition.

headline: Coeur Mining misses Q2 targets despite record output
body: Coeur Mining reported second-quarter earnings of $0.12 per share against a $0.26 estimate, on revenue of $1.09 billion versus $1.24 billion expected, a shortfall the company tied to softer precious-metals pricing; per StocksToTrade (Aug 18), gross margins still held near 67% and free cash flow came in around $388 million for the quarter.

headline: Beyond Meat completes 1-for-30 reverse split as it fights to keep its Nasdaq listing
body: Beyond Meat’s 1-for-30 reverse stock split took effect August 14 as the company works to satisfy a Nasdaq minimum-bid requirement that must hold for 10 consecutive trading days by August 31; per ts2.tech (Aug 15), second-quarter revenue fell 8.2% year-on-year to $68.8 million, with gross margin down to 8.5% and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $27.7 million.

headline: Figma posts third straight quarter of accelerating growth, raises full-year outlook
body: Figma’s second-quarter revenue reached $370.1 million, up 48% year-on-year, marking a third consecutive quarter of accelerating growth, with net dollar retention of 136% and customers spending $10,000-plus in annual recurring revenue growing 34%; per StockTitan (Aug 5), the company raised full-year revenue guidance to $1.463–$1.467 billion. CEO Dylan Field pointed to rapid uptake of Figma’s AI agent tools as a driver of the acceleration.

headline: Chamoli tunnel search ends, death toll rises to 10
body: The five-day search operation at the THDC tunnel in Uttarakhand’s Chamoli district concluded on Tuesday after SDRF and NDRF teams recovered the last missing workers’ bodies, raising the death toll to 10 from the Aug 13 landslide-triggered collapse near the Birhi river, per ANI (Aug 18). SDRF Inspector Karn Singh said, “The bodies of all three missing persons have been recovered… despite difficult and challenging conditions.” Uttarakhand CM Pushkar Singh Dhami has ordered a magisterial inquiry and compensation for the victims’ families.

headline: Jharkhand scraps JSSC-CGL exam, students call off gherao
body: The Jharkhand cabinet cancelled the JSSC-Combined Graduate Level exam and all recruitment processes run by TSR Data Processing Pvt Ltd since 2014, prompting student leader Devendra Mahto to end his 15-day hunger strike and drop the planned Aug 20 gherao of CM Hemant Soren’s residence, per WION (Aug 17). Soren said, “We have always taken tough decisions to protect the interests, future, and trust of my young companions from Jharkhand,” as his government ordered a CID-led Special Investigation Team probe into the alleged paper leaks.

headline: IMD extends heavy rain warning for Delhi, north India to Aug 20
body: The India Meteorological Department’s Tuesday bulletin kept heavy-rain warnings active across Haryana, Chandigarh, Delhi, Punjab, Jammu-Kashmir, Ladakh and Uttarakhand through August 20, alongside a red alert for very heavy rainfall in Jharkhand, per Business Standard (Aug 18). Delhi itself was forecast generally cloudy with light to moderate rain and temperatures between 23 and 34 degrees Celsius, continuing the wet spell that has already pushed the capital past its August rainfall average.

headline: Afghan envoy hails ‘shared past,’ deeper ties with India
body: At Afghanistan’s first Victory Day reception held in New Delhi, Chargé d’Affaires Noor Ahmed Noor said stronger India-Afghanistan political trust and economic partnership “will not only benefit both countries, but will also make an important contribution to regional stability,” per WION (Aug 17). He thanked External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar for supporting “protecting and respecting the international rights of the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan,” even as India withholds formal recognition of the Taliban government.

headline: Stourbridge Wildfire Recovery Continues as Residents Return Home
body: More than a week after wildfire tore through Stourbridge, at least eight of the 19 destroyed homes have now been viewed by their owners and around 106 of the roughly 130 affected properties have reopened, per ITV News Central (Aug 17). Chief Fire Officer Simon Tuhill said “the smoke was extensive and the fire was travelling rapidly,” while local MP Cat Eccles cautioned that recovery “is not going to be linear” as investigators continue working to establish the blaze’s cause. Community fundraising has topped £125,000.

headline: Ferguson Marine to Cut Quarter of Workforce Amid Contract Delays
body: Ferguson Marine, Scotland’s state-owned shipyard on the Clyde, will cut up to 70 jobs — nearly a quarter of its 283-strong workforce, including 34 apprentices — citing an “inevitable gap in workload” while it awaits confirmation of four promised government ferry contracts, per STV News (Aug 18). GMB Scotland secretary Louise Gilmour asked, “Shipbuilders needs ships to build so where are those promised to Ferguson Marine?” while Cabinet Secretary Stephen Flynn called the redundancies “necessary to help secure a viable future for the yard.”

headline: Disabled Bus Pass Holders to Get 24/7 Free Travel From 2027
body: Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced that disabled people in England will get free bus travel around the clock from April 2027, scrapping the current time restrictions on concessionary passes, per GOV.UK (Aug 17). The £60 million policy will end what Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander called “this postcode lottery, so disabled people can travel on buses for free whenever they need.” Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden added the change would help disabled people “access jobs, training, and other opportunities at any time.”

headline: UAE suspends all trade and financial transactions with Iran
body: The UAE announced it has suspended all trade, commercial exchanges and financial transactions with Iran “until further notice,” per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 19). Foreign ministry spokesperson Afra Al Hameli said the move responds to regional escalations that “undermine regional and international peace and security,” while the UAE reaffirmed its commitment to “dialogue, cooperation, and regional integration” and to safeguarding the international financial system.

headline: Qatar renews push to reopen Strait of Hormuz, cites ongoing Gulf coordination
body: Qatar’s Foreign Ministry used its weekly briefing to reiterate calls for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, with spokesperson Dr Majed Al Ansari stressing “the necessity of opening the Strait of Hormuz” and safeguarding freedom of navigation, per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 18). He said “Gulf coordination continues at various levels to deal with the potential repercussions of the crisis,” adding that “diplomacy and dialogue are the only way to overcome differences and conflicts.”

headline: Qatar says invitation for Iran to review pilot search-and-rescue details ‘remains open’
body: Qatar’s Foreign Ministry said its offer for Iran to send a technical team to review search-and-rescue details for its downed pilots “remains open,” spokesperson Dr Majed Al Ansari said, per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 18). He said the Iranian aircraft involved “had entered Qatari airspace and targeted the city of Doha, and were dealt with according to the known rules of engagement,” adding that the remains of one pilot were recovered and handed to Iranian authorities for funeral rites.

headline: Qatar condemns strikes on Kurdistan Regional Government offices in Erbil
body: Qatar’s Foreign Ministry issued a strong condemnation after strikes hit the Kurdistan Regional Government prime minister’s office and the residence of the region’s intelligence chief in Erbil, calling them “a blatant violation of the sovereignty of the Republic of Iraq and the Kurdistan Region,” per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 18). Doha reaffirmed “full solidarity with Iraq and the Kurdistan Region of Iraq” and its support for measures to safeguard their sovereignty.

headline: Colorverse Experience continues at Katara
body: This immersive walkthrough of seven interactive zones — blending colour, light, sound and projection — runs at Katara Cultural Village’s South Parking through September 15, with tickets from QAR 35. It remains one of Doha’s most popular family outings this summer, per Qatar Living’s weekly roundup (Aug 16) and Marhaba Qatar.

headline: Tasweer marks World Photography Day today
body: Qatar Museums’ Tasweer photo festival hosts “Together in Photography: World Photography Day” at Fire Station Cinema today, August 19, from 6:30–8:30pm, announcing the winners of the 2026 Tasweer Awards. The ceremony, streamed live on Tasweer’s digital platforms, brings together photographers and the public to mark the day, per Gulf Times (Aug 12) and Qatar Living (Aug 16).

headline: PAW Patrol: The Big Show Rescue opens at Mall of Qatar
body: Nickelodeon’s free live stage show, featuring Chase, Marshall, Skye and Ryder in interactive rescue missions, runs at Mall of Qatar’s Oasis Stage from August 20–29 with three 30-minute shows daily. No tickets are required and seating is first-come, first-served, per Qatar Living (Aug 16).

headline: Evening karting sessions at Lusail International Circuit
body: Lusail International Circuit is running evening karting sessions from August 19–22, 6–11pm, at QAR 125 per 12-minute session — a popular pick for this week’s calendar, per Qatar Living’s events roundup (Aug 16).

headline: Hala Summer Shopping Festival raffle draws continue
body: Visit Qatar’s Hala Summer Shopping Festival, spanning nine malls and restaurants including Villaggio, runs through August 31, with shoppers spending a minimum of QAR 200 eligible to enter raffle draws for prizes. The next Villaggio raffle draw is set for August 21 at 8:30pm, per Qatar Living (Aug 16) and The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 14).

headline: WHO chief warns DR Congo’s Ebola outbreak is ‘far from being under control’ as deaths near 2,300, while Colombia’s earthquake toll holds at 289 and Indonesian quake survivors report no government aid has arrived.
Trump threatened to ‘bomb’ Oman a second time as the Hormuz standoff hardens, while Kushner and Netanyahu advanced a Hamas disarmament plan and UNIFIL logged 137 daily strikes into Lebanon.
OpenAI disclosed a hacker exploit that let its models escape their training sandbox via a Hugging Face breach, as the 30-year Treasury yield hit a fresh 19-year high and gold’s rally stalled.

The UAE suspended all trade and financial transactions with Iran ‘until further notice,’ as Uttarakhand’s Chamoli tunnel search ended with the toll at 10 and Jharkhand scrapped its JSSC-CGL exam after student protests.

India closed in on a Galle Test win over Sri Lanka, Rodri prepared for his Barcelona unveiling at the Gamper Trophy, and F1 returned to Zandvoort for a sprint weekend that could be Verstappen’s home-race farewell.
DR Congo’s Ebola Outbreak Becomes Deadliest on Record
body: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has become the country’s deadliest ever, with 2,325 deaths among 4,945 confirmed cases — a 46% fatality rate that has now surpassed the previous record of 2,299 deaths set in 2018-2020, per UN News (Aug 17). The WHO warned the outbreak is “outpacing the response,” saying “responders need safe access to communities, and the resources to end this outbreak and save lives,” as it launches a major scale-up backed by a $54.5 million OCHA allocation and vaccine trials now underway in the UK and Canada.

headline: Zambia’s Hichilema Wins Second Term Amid Fraud Allegations
body: Zambia’s electoral commission declared President Hakainde Hichilema the winner of a second term with roughly 60% of the vote to challenger Brian Mundubile’s 38%, per Al Jazeera (Aug 18). The count that resumed after Sunday’s violence and ballot theft remained contested, with police arresting 11 people — including opposition figures — in a raid involving gunfire, while Mundubile alleged manipulation of results forms and demanded an independent investigation that Hichilema’s campaign dismissed as false.

headline: Colombia Shifts From Rescue to Recovery as Earthquake Toll Hits 289
body: Colombia’s death toll from the magnitude-7.4 earthquake rose to at least 289, with 143 people officially unaccounted for, as authorities began winding down search-and-rescue in favour of reconstruction, per Al Jazeera (Aug 17). “Certain search-and-rescue operations are no longer necessary, and we have now moved on to a phase in which reconstruction, demolition, and other types of operations… will begin,” said Sergeant Joel Bustamante, as officials work to house more than 120,000 affected families, many now sheltering in converted stadiums and community centres.

headline: Indonesia Quake Toll Climbs to 68 as Survivors Report No Government Aid
body: The death toll from Indonesia’s magnitude-7.7 Flores earthquake rose to 68, with more than 200 injured and roughly 12,800 people still displaced, per Al Jazeera (Aug 17). “Our houses are no longer liveable because many have collapsed and are full of cracks,” said survivor Junaidin, adding “as for help from the government, there hasn’t been any — no tents, no medicine, no food,” even as the military airlifted 13 tonnes of emergency supplies to the island.

headline: Suthar-Jadeja Spin Web Hands India 178-Run Lead at Galle
body: India were bowled out for 462 on the third morning at Galle — Devdutt Padikkal’s maiden Test century (167), KL Rahul’s 82 and Dhruv Jurel’s 51 built the total — before Manav Suthar and Ravindra Jadeja shared seven wickets to dismiss Sri Lanka for 284, per ESPNcricinfo (Aug 17). Sonal Dinusha made a maiden century and Niroshan Dickwella added 80 in a defiant middle-order stand, but India closed day three 178 runs ahead with two days left and rain still threatening the Test, per Outlook India (Aug 17).

headline: Rodri Completes £65m Move to Barcelona From Man City
body: Manchester City have accepted Barcelona’s bid of roughly £65.4m ($88.5m) for Rodri, with the 2024 Ballon d’Or winner signing a four-year deal after seven seasons and 298 appearances in Manchester, per Al Jazeera (Aug 17). The 30-year-old World Cup winner won 12 major honours at City — including four Premier League titles and the Champions League — and now joins Barcelona’s midfield after Frenkie de Jong’s expected lengthy injury lay-off helped open the door for the move.

headline: Zandvoort’s Farewell: Verstappen Chases History Amid Winless Run
body: Formula 1 resumes after its summer break at Zandvoort for what organisers confirm is the circuit’s final race on the calendar, with Max Verstappen chasing a fourth home win to match Jim Clark’s record and end a winless run stretching back to June, per GPblog (Aug 17). “I just want to enjoy it with the fans,” Verstappen said of the farewell weekend, as Honda debuts an upgraded power unit tested during the summer break at Aston Martin’s Hungaroria filming day.

headline: Salah Makes Trabzonspor Debut After Shock Liverpool Exit
body: Mohamed Salah made his full debut for Trabzonspor as a 58th-minute substitute in a 1-1 draw at Kasimpasa, days after completing a free transfer from Liverpool that ended his eight-year spell at Anfield, per beIN Sports (Aug 15). The 34-year-old fired his best chance over the crossbar in the 70th minute as Noah Saviolo’s opener for Trabzonspor was cancelled out by an Adrian Benedyczak penalty, marking one of the transfer window’s biggest surprises.

headline: 30-Year Treasury Yield Hits Highest Level in Nearly 20 Years
body: The 30-year Treasury yield climbed to its highest level in almost two decades — last seen around 2006, “when there was no iPhone and Lehman Brothers was a Wall Street titan” — as bond markets price in persistent deficits, inflation risk and long-term uncertainty, per Yahoo Finance (Aug 17). “Growth is cooling, the consumer is pulling back, and the bond market wants more money to wait,” the report noted, with the sell-off compounded by crude near $83 and the Strategic Petroleum Reserve sitting at 43-year lows.

headline: China’s July Data Misses Across the Board as Stimulus Fades
body: China’s industrial output grew just 4.5% year-on-year in July, down from 5.3% in June and below the 4.8% forecast, while retail sales rose only 0.6% — far short of the 1.5% expected — per Reuters via Investing.com (Aug 17). Fixed-asset investment fell 6.7% over the first seven months versus a forecast 6.0% drop, with Citi analysts noting subsidy-linked daily sales dropped to 6.3 billion yuan ($934.8 million) in July from 9 billion in June, as three typhoons and a tenth straight month of falling auto sales added to the drag.

headline: VIX Hits 2026 Low Just as Strategists Warn of Seasonal Sell-Off Risk
body: The Cboe Volatility Index (VIX) fell to 14.2 last Friday, its lowest reading since 2026 began, even as Wall Street sits at record highs, per BigGo Finance (Aug 17). “We are entering a window that has historically been prone to downside volatility, and we are doing so with the market at record highs and the VIX at year-to-date lows,” said BTIG chief market technician Jonathan Krinsky, while IG’s Axel Rudolph added “the market is starting to look a little too comfortable” — strategists point to a pattern since 1990 of at least a 7% equal-weight S&P 500 pullback between mid-August and mid-October in midterm election years.

headline: Walmart, Target, Home Depot and Lowe’s Earnings This Week to Test Consumer Resilience
body: Four major retailers — Walmart and Target (both Q2) plus Home Depot and Lowe’s — report earnings this week, arriving right after Americans “unexpectedly pulled back on retail spending in July by the biggest amount in more than a year,” per Fortune (Aug 17). The reports land with the S&P 500 near record highs and retailers grappling with “stubbornly high inflation and customers that are laser focused on prices,” making the results a direct read on whether the consumer-fatigue signal from last week’s retail sales report is broadening.

headline: Gold Extends Rally to $4,440 as Weak Data Keeps Fed Hike Odds Fading
body: Spot gold opened at $4,440.10/oz Monday, up 2.4% on the week and 32.7% year-over-year, after July retail sales fell 0.6% — far worse than the 0.1% gain economists expected — and August consumer sentiment slid 8%, per Yahoo Finance (Aug 17). Softer data continues to erode the odds of a September Fed rate hike and a weaker dollar (the Dollar Index dipped 0.2%) added further support, even as lingering Middle East tensions keep an inflation risk in the background.

headline: Nvidia Guarantees Up to $105 Billion for OpenAI’s Ohio Data Center
body: Nvidia agreed to guarantee up to $105 billion in lease obligations for OpenAI’s planned 8-gigawatt AI campus in Pike County, Ohio — built on the site of a former Cold War uranium-enrichment plant — with capacity coming online in phases from 2028, per Unite.AI and Bloomberg (Aug 17). Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said “AI is becoming infrastructure — the foundation for intelligence in every industry — and land, power and shell have become vital in the age of AI,” with Nvidia on the hook to cover any shortfall if OpenAI defaults, deepening the circular financing ties binding the two companies; Nvidia is separately investing $1.5 billion in the project’s developer, SB Energy.

headline: Stripe Finalizes $7 Billion-Plus OpenRouter Acquisition
body: Stripe closed its purchase of AI model-routing startup OpenRouter for more than $7 billion, confirming last week’s reported talks, per Dataconomy (Aug 17). OpenRouter, which lets developers tap over 400 AI models through one gateway to avoid vendor lock-in, serves 8 million users and had raised its Series B at just a $1.3 billion valuation in May — a more than five-fold markup in three months; OpenRouter’s CEO has described the platform as “the equivalent of Stripe for AI.”

headline: Amodei Defends His AI Messaging, Anthropic Details Claude Watermarking
body: A day after calling the AI backlash a “crisis of trust,” Dario Amodei pushed back on investor Gavin Baker’s claim that his own risk warnings fueled anti-AI sentiment, arguing distrust stems from “a broader, long-standing crisis of trust in corporations and government” rather than AI executives’ warnings, while conceding the “most legitimate criticism” of firms like Anthropic is their failure to deliver tangible benefits so far, per The AI Insider (Aug 17). Anthropic also published details of a new Claude text-watermarking system built for EU AI Act compliance, using subtle, SynthID-Text-style word-choice patterns “undetectable to readers without a decoding key” that survive light editing but not full rewrites.

headline: Meta’s $420 Billion in Off-Balance-Sheet AI Debt Draws Scrutiny
body: Days after Zuckerberg’s AI manifesto met public skepticism, a Wall Street Journal analysis found Meta carries roughly $420 billion in off-balance-sheet AI infrastructure commitments — nearly five times its reported $83.7 billion in debt — including $347 billion in future lease obligations and a Blue Owl Capital-backed joint venture financing its Hyperion data center that Ernst & Young flagged as a “critical audit matter,” per Tech Times (Aug 17). Meta’s free cash flow collapsed 91% to $784 million in Q2 despite strong revenue growth, prompting former Facebook investor Roger McNamee to call the spending spree “manufacturing appearance” rather than substance.

headline: Fourth Woman Sues xAI Over Grok-Generated Child Abuse Images
body: A Wyoming woman, identified as Jane Doe 4, joined an expanding lawsuit against xAI alleging her stepfather used Grok’s “Imagine” feature to turn a childhood photo of her into explicit images; he died by suicide two days after investigators found the images, per Engadget (Aug 17). She joins three Tennessee teenagers already suing over Grok-generated sexualized deepfakes distributed on Discord and Telegram, in a case that could cover “at least thousands of minors,” as California’s attorney general and EU regulators separately investigate X over AI-generated child sexual abuse material.

headline: Trump Threatens to ‘Bomb’ Oman as US-Iran Hormuz Deadline Expires
body: The 60-day US-Iran memorandum of understanding on reopening the Strait of Hormuz expired Monday without a deal, prompting President Trump to warn on Fox News, “If Oman gets in the way, we’ll bomb them,” per The Jerusalem Post (Aug 17). Trump also confirmed a direct US backchannel to Iran’s Revolutionary Guard Corps and said he is in no rush for a deal, even as Iran’s foreign ministry said Tehran and Oman had reached “an understanding” on a Hormuz transit map letting ships pass near Iran and exit near Oman fee-free during an interim period, per The Times of Israel (Aug 17).

headline: Kushner and Netanyahu Agree US General Should Oversee Hamas Disarmament
body: A day after his rare direct Cairo talks with Hamas chief Khalil al-Hayya, Jared Kushner met Netanyahu in Jerusalem, and an Israeli official said the two agreed “no redeployment or reconstruction would take place in the Gaza Strip before Hamas is disarmed,” with the first step requiring Hamas to “hand over its weapons for decommissioning under the supervision of an American general,” per Courthouse News Service (Aug 17). Analysts read the Hamas outreach as a shift in Washington’s posture — scholar Adel Shadid said “Hamas is no longer the problem in the American reading, but rather part of the solution,” per Al Jazeera (Aug 17) — even as Netanyahu, facing an Oct 27 election, keeps publicly rejecting elements of Trump’s 15-point roadmap.

headline: UNIFIL: Lebanese Civilians ‘Paying the Highest Price’ as Israeli Strikes Intensify
body: UN peacekeeping force UNIFIL said Israeli forces fired an average of 137 projectiles a day into Lebanon between Aug 5-16 — peaking at 208 on Saturday and 185 on Sunday — despite the June 26 ceasefire, warning that “civilians are once again paying the highest price, with many families displaced or forced to change their daily routines because of insecurity and uncertainty,” per Al Jazeera (Aug 17). The death toll from Israeli strikes on Lebanon since March 2 has reached 4,346, including 11 people killed in two separate air raids on Saturday alone.

headline: Venezuela Frees Nearly 80 More Political Prisoners, Some Reporting Torture
body: Venezuela’s transitional government released close to 80 more political prisoners on Aug 17, days after an initial batch of 131, per Local10/AP (Aug 17). Among them was Emirlendris Benitez, freed after eight years’ detention over an alleged 2018 drone attack on Nicolás Maduro, who says she was beaten and suffocated in custody and now uses a wheelchair from untreated medical complications; her mother said Benitez “wouldn’t hurt a fly.” Many newly freed prisoners still face restrictions, such as periodic court appearances, rather than full freedom, as the reconciliation process continues.

headline: Sudan’s Army Downs Second RSF Drone This Month as Kordofan Fighting Rages
body: Sudan’s military said it shot down an RSF-operated FH-95 drone over Gereikh in North Kordofan state on Aug 17 — the second advanced drone its air defences have downed in the region this month — per Sudan Tribune (Aug 17). The clash follows a late-July army offensive that reclaimed large swathes of North Kordofan, including a key export route, pushing the RSF westward and helping secure El Obeid and a land corridor to Omdurman.

headline: Meta Faces Up to $1.4 Trillion in Potential Damages as California Child-Safety Trial Opens
body: A trial brought by 29 state attorneys general opened in California, alleging Meta illegally collected children’s data and designed addictive product features, with potential damages cited in a range of $200 billion to $1.4 trillion; the case follows a New Mexico verdict that already ordered Meta to pay $942 million combined. Wall Street trimmed price targets on the stock as the trial began — UBS to $715, Baird to $750 and Goldman Sachs to $725 — though the consensus rating held at Buy. Per Benzinga (Aug 17).

headline: Morgan Stanley Warns Hyperscaler AI Spending Is Outrunning Revenue
body: Morgan Stanley flagged that the gap between AI capital spending and the revenue it generates is pressuring near-term cash flow across the hyperscalers, projecting industry capital spending will rise 57% in 2026 versus 2025 and warning some companies may need to raise additional debt at higher rates to bridge the gap. Microsoft, which has outlined roughly $190 billion of AI infrastructure investment, was named among the group under scrutiny, though the report noted the company holds $77 billion in cash against $129 billion in debt and is expected to generate about $67 billion in free cash flow this year. Per Yahoo Finance/The Motley Fool (Aug 17).

headline: Oracle’s AI Backlog Swells to $638 Billion, but Investors Want Proof It Converts to Revenue
body: Oracle disclosed that its remaining performance obligations — future contracted revenue including commitments from clients such as OpenAI and Meta — surged to $638 billion in its fiscal fourth quarter, up 363% year over year. Analysts said the market is assigning little valuation premium to that backlog until it converts into booked revenue, with JPMorgan maintaining an Overweight rating and a $200 price target; the disclosure landed in the same week Morgan Stanley questioned whether hyperscalers’ AI spending is outrunning their cash generation. Per TradingKey (Aug 16).

headline: Twilio Gives Back Part of Its Post-Earnings Rally as the Software Trade Cools
body: No new company-specific announcement was found for the session; Twilio’s pullback came a week and a half after it beat Q2 estimates and raised 2026 guidance alongside a completed $1.2 billion buyback. The retreat tracked a broader cooling in richly valued software names, following both the hyperscaler AI-financing warnings that hit Microsoft and Oracle and a step back from the M&A-driven software rally sparked by Silver Lake’s reported $51 billion approach for Workday. Per TheStreet (Aug 17).

headline: Boeing Deliveries Lose Momentum Against Airbus as Regulators Order New 737 Max Inspections
body: Boeing delivered 53 aircraft in July, down from 60-64 a month in the prior two months and behind Airbus’s 67, leaving Boeing at 367 deliveries year-to-date versus Airbus’s 418; the company did register 38 new orders in the month, including from AerCap, Luxair and Uganda National Airlines at the Farnborough Airshow. The delivery slowdown compounds an FAA directive requiring crack inspections on 471 737 Max jets after reports of a structural bear-strap issue on older Next-Generation 737s, with the rule taking effect September 10. Per AeroTime (Aug 12) and ABC News (Aug 7).

headline: Rackspace’s Losses Deepen Even as Revenue Holds Steady
body: Rackspace Technology reported Q2 2026 revenue of $670.1 million, essentially flat year over year, but its net loss widened to $67.5 million from $54.5 million a year earlier, with non-GAAP gross margin slipping to 18.6% from 19.8%. The company swung from a profitable first quarter into a loss-making second quarter, underscoring pressure on profitability even as its AI infrastructure pivot continues. Per Simply Wall St (Aug 12).

headline: Beyond Meat Completes 1-for-30 Reverse Split to Save Its Nasdaq Listing
body: Beyond Meat’s 1-for-30 reverse stock split took effect at the close of trading on August 13, consolidating every 30 shares into one and cutting authorized common stock from 3 billion to 100 million shares, with convertible notes, warrants and award prices adjusted proportionately. The company said the move was intended to regain compliance with Nasdaq’s $1.00 minimum bid price rule ahead of an August 31 deadline. Per GlobeNewswire (Aug 14).

headline: Fortress Biotech Grows Revenue 14% and Boosts Cash Pile via Crystalys Financing
body: Fortress Biotech reported Q2 2026 revenue of $18.7 million, up 14% from $16.4 million a year earlier and driven mainly by Journey Medical’s dermatology sales of $17.8 million, though it posted a net loss of $2.5 million versus net income in the prior-year quarter. Cash climbed to $196.6 million from $79.4 million at year-end after subsidiary Crystalys secured $130 million in Series B financing, while partner AstraZeneca reported a 62% improvement in survival in a subgroup analysis of anselamimab for cardiac amyloidosis. Per StockTitan (Aug 13).

headline: Hydrofarm’s Q2 Revenue Nearly Halves as Oversupply and Brand Exits Bite
body: Hydrofarm Holdings reported Q2 2026 revenue of $23.2 million, down 40.9% from $39.2 million a year earlier and well short of consensus, which the company attributed to industry oversupply and the discontinuation of certain distributed brands; adjusted loss per share also missed estimates. Gross margin nonetheless improved to 20.0% from 19.2%, and the company applied proceeds from the $16 million sale of its Aurora Peat Products unit, completed July 31, toward debt reduction. Per Investing.com (Aug 14).

headline: Jharkhand Students Set Aug 18 Ultimatum Ahead of Aug 20 Gherao of CM Soren’s Residence
body: On the 22nd day of their agitation, JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch leaders gave Chief Minister Hemant Soren an Aug 18 deadline to act on alleged exam-paper irregularities, warning that “lakhs of students and youths” would march on his Ranchi residence on Aug 20 if he does not comply, per Organiser (Aug 17). Soren used his Independence Day speech to promise an impartial probe and tech-secured exams, but protest leader Ravindra Paswan said the CM must resign unless a CBI or judicial probe, cancellation of the JSSC-CGL and JPSC results, and reinstatement of whistleblower Santosh Kumar Mastana are delivered.

headline: Chamoli Tunnel Search Enters Fourth Day as Toll Holds at 8, Two Still Missing
body: Rescue teams from the NDRF, SDRF and ITBP kept pumping water from the flooded THDC tunnel at Pipalkoti for a fourth straight day, still searching for Jharkhand’s Lucas Topno and Chhattisgarh’s Chetan Poyam after the Aug 13 landslide, with the death toll steady at eight and twelve workers already hospitalised, per The Hitavada (Aug 17). A magisterial inquiry ordered into the disaster’s cause remains ongoing as authorities have yet to reach the two men still trapped.

headline: IMD Warns of Heavy Rain Sweeping North India Through Aug 22, Delhi Braces for Aug 18 Downpour
body: The India Meteorological Department extended its heavy-to-very-heavy rainfall warning through Aug 22 as a Bay of Bengal low deepens into a depression, with Odisha, Gangetic West Bengal, Chhattisgarh, Uttarakhand and Jharkhand hit hardest on Aug 16–17 and the wet spell expanding to Delhi-NCR, Haryana and Punjab from Aug 18, per Business Today (Aug 17). Flash-flood and waterlogging risk is flagged for Odisha districts including Angul, Bargarh and Cuttack, with West Madhya Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand staying vulnerable through the outlook period.

headline: Reform UK Details $68bn Welfare Cuts, Targeting Foreign Nationals and PIP
body: Reform UK published its blueprint to strip roughly $68 billion a year from Britain’s welfare bill, split between about $28.5bn saved by ending universal credit, housing and disability payments for foreign nationals — including EU citizens with settled status — and $29.8bn from scrapping PIP for a more restrictive disability payment, per UPI (Aug 17). Work-and-pensions spokesman Danny Kruger said he would understand “if the Europeans decided to apply the same principle… to deny our nationals access to their welfare system,” while Labour MP Rachael Maskell warned the disability cuts would stop people playing “a full role in our society.”

headline: Stourbridge Wildfire Investigation Under Way as Daily Briefings Continue for Residents
body: Four days after wildfires destroyed 19 homes and damaged 18 more across roughly 500 acres of Stourbridge, investigators are still working to establish a cause while Dudley Council runs daily 2pm briefings — online and in person at the town hall — to update affected residents, per Birmingham Dispatch (Aug 17) and Express & Star (Aug 15). Councillor Ed Lawrence said the sessions give residents “a dedicated opportunity… to hear the latest updates and ask questions,” as the Prime Minister visited the town to thank fire crews and pledge recovery support.

headline: Qatar’s Amir Discusses Bilateral Ties in Call With Bahrain’s King
body: Qatar’s Amir received a phone call from the King of Bahrain, with the two leaders discussing “fraternal relations between the two countries and ways to support and strengthen them in various fields,” alongside regional and international issues of shared concern, per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 17).

headline: Qatar’s PM Pushes Hormuz De-escalation in Calls With Saudi, Jordanian, Syrian Counterparts
body: Qatar’s Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al-Thani held back-to-back calls with the foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia, Jordan and Syria, stressing “the importance of all parties committing to dialogue and diplomacy” on implementing the US-Iran memorandum of understanding and safeguarding freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, per Xinhua (Aug 17). Qatari Foreign Ministry spokesperson Majed Al Ansari separately reiterated Doha’s denial of detaining Iranian pilots, saying the country was “surprised by these misleading statements at this particular time.”

headline: World Bank Report Ranks Qatar Among Economies Leading the AI Frontier
body: The World Bank’s World Development Report 2026 placed Qatar alongside Singapore, Sweden and the UAE among economies advancing fastest on artificial intelligence, citing its “sustained investment in digital infrastructure” as it builds a knowledge-based economy, per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 16). The report found AI could lift productivity in 18.7% of jobs in high-income countries versus 16.2% in developing economies, while automation risk from generative AI is estimated at 14.2% and 4.5% respectively.

headline: Colorverse Experience Lights Up Katara Through Mid-September
body: Katara Cultural Village is hosting Colorverse, a 45-minute immersive family attraction running July 15–Sept 15, with tickets from QR35. Visitors move through seven interactive zones to help “restore red, green and blue colours” to the fictional world of Colorama, with hands-on science activities, character meet-and-greets and workshops for ages four and up, per The Peninsula Qatar (Jun 6).

headline: PAW Patrol: The Big Show Rescue Rolls Into Qatar Mall
body: Nickelodeon’s PAW Patrol brings a live stage show, “The Big Show Rescue,” to Qatar Mall from Aug 20–29, with multiple free showtimes daily aimed at younger children and families, per Qatar Living’s events roundup (Aug 16).

headline: Lusail Karting Sessions Return for the Week
body: Lusail International Circuit is running public karting sessions Aug 19–22, 6pm–11pm, at QAR 125 for a roughly 12-minute session on its 900-metre track, per Qatar Living (Aug 16). The program, aimed at drivers 13 and up (minimum height 153cm), uses 270cc karts capable of 50–60 km/h, with bookings online-only and non-refundable.

headline: Hala Summer Shopping Festival Raffle Hits Villaggio This Week
body: Visit Qatar’s Hala Summer Shopping Festival runs across nine malls — including Villaggio, Place Vendôme, Doha Festival City and Mall of Qatar — through Aug 31, with Villaggio’s weekly raffle draw set for Aug 21 at 8:30pm. Shoppers spending a minimum QR200 get receipts stamped for raffle entry into prizes given out throughout the month, per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 14).

headline: Al Wakra Beach Cleanup Invites Volunteers on Aug 22
body: The Ministry of Municipality’s ongoing coastal cleanup drive stops at Al Wakra Public Beach on Aug 22, with two free volunteer sessions from 6–9am and 3–5pm, per Qatar Living (Aug 16). It’s part of a wider series of beach and island cleanup campaigns the ministry has been running through the summer to promote environmental awareness.

headline: DR Congo’s Ebola outbreak becomes its deadliest on record with 2,325 deaths, as Zambia’s Hichilema claims a contested second term and Colombia shifts from earthquake rescue to recovery with the toll at 289.
Trump threatened to ‘bomb’ Oman if it ‘gets in the way’ of a Hormuz deal as the US-Iran deadline expired, while Kushner and Netanyahu agreed a US general should oversee Hamas’s disarmament.
Nvidia guaranteed up to $105 billion for OpenAI’s new Ohio data-centre lease as the 30-year Treasury yield hit its highest level in nearly 20 years and Stripe closed its $7bn-plus OpenRouter buy.
Reform UK unveiled a $68bn welfare-cut blueprint targeting foreign nationals and PIP claimants, as Jharkhand students set an Aug 20 deadline to gherao Chief Minister Soren’s residence.
Rodri sealed a £65m switch to Barcelona from Manchester City as India took a 178-run lead over Sri Lanka at Galle, with F1 returning to Zandvoort for Verstappen’s home-track farewell.
Colombia Earthquake: Girl, 3, and Man, 75, Pulled Alive From Rubble After 100 Hours
body: A three-year-old girl and a 75-year-old man were rescued alive from the rubble of Colombia’s magnitude-7.4 earthquake more than 100 hours after it struck — well past the 72-hour window rescuers typically rely on — per Al Jazeera (Aug 16). Search teams say 320 people remain unaccounted for as recovery operations continue in hard-hit Cali and Buenaventura.

headline: Indonesia Earthquake Death Toll Climbs to 51 as Thousands Are Displaced
body: The death toll from the magnitude-7.7 earthquake that struck off Indonesia’s Flores Island rose to at least 51, with about 5,000 people evacuated and more than 1,300 homes damaged, per Al Jazeera (Aug 16). “The quake was massive, the shock was so strong… there were 13 of us inside the house, and we all ran to save ourselves,” said Nona, a 51-year-old resident of Talibura village, per Reuters.

headline: Zambia Vote Count Resumes After Violence, Ballot Theft Suspend Tallying
body: Vote counting in Zambia’s presidential election was briefly suspended after reports of ballot theft and violence, including the killing of a 57-year-old polling agent, before resuming once the electoral commission contained the “security threat,” per Al Jazeera (Aug 16). Partial results from 49 of 226 constituencies show incumbent Hakainde Hichilema leading with 52.6% to challenger Mundubile’s 42.1%, amid observer reports of intimidation and abductions across five provinces. European Parliament observer Reinhold Lopatka said, “Even one loss of life is one too many.”

headline: Deadly Flash Flooding Hits US State of Indiana, at Least Five Dead
body: At least five people died after storms dumped more than 280mm (11 inches) of rain over two days in Indiana, sending the White River over its banks in Indianapolis in what Mayor Joe Hogsett called the worst flooding in over 30 years, per Al Jazeera (Aug 15). The dead include a 58-year-old woman who drove into floodwaters and a 4-year-old struck by a falling tree, as Governor Mike Braun urged residents to “continue to take flooding seriously and stay away from floodwaters.”

headline: Europe’s Rivers Hit Record Lows as Drought Grips Half the Continent
body: New satellite imagery shows roughly half of Europe’s land is now in drought, with 9% of areas at alert level, as the Loire, Po, Rhine and Danube rivers all hit record-low levels this month, per Al Jazeera (Aug 16), citing the EU’s Global Drought Observatory. The European Commission’s Joint Research Centre confirmed the Loire reached record lows in August, following the hottest June-July on record for Western Europe.

headline: Padikkal's Maiden Century Puts India in Command at Galle
body: India closed day two on 460 for 9, powered by Devdutt Padikkal’s career-best 167 — his maiden Test century, made from No. 3 — with support from KL Rahul (82) and Dhruv Jurel (51), per ESPNcricinfo (Aug 16). Left-arm spinner Prabath Jayasuriya took 4 wickets as turn began creeping into the Galle surface, and with an 83% chance of rain forecast for day three, per Prokerala (Aug 16), India’s bowlers face a race against the weather in the five-day Test running through Aug 19.

headline: Manchester Super Giants Win Maiden Hundred Title in Lord's Thriller
body: Tim Seifert blitzed 72 off 38 balls — the fastest fifty in a men’s Hundred final, reached in 24 deliveries — to power Manchester Super Giants to a five-wicket win over Trent Rockets, chasing down 158 as Liam Dawson struck the winning six with three balls left, per Sky Sports (Aug 16). Captain Jos Buttler called it a ‘mixture of emotions’ after the tense finish, while earlier at Lord’s, Trent Rockets claimed the women’s title, bowling out SunRisers Leeds for just 91 as Kim Garth took two wickets in three balls.

headline: Barcelona Agree €76.5m Deal With Man City for Rodri
body: Barcelona and Manchester City have struck a deal worth roughly €76.5m ($87m) for World Cup-winning captain Rodri, capping a chase that had run past a 48-hour deadline, per beIN Sports and ESPN (Aug 16). A Barcelona source said ‘in the coming days there will be a statement and (the transfer) will become official,’ with the move partly driven by Frenkie de Jong’s expected multi-month injury lay-off; Rodri, 30, would follow Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi to Camp Nou this summer.

headline: Verstappen Chases Home Win at Zandvoort Amid Longest Drought
body: Max Verstappen returns from F1’s summer break leading the drivers’ championship by 78 points with 10 rounds remaining, but arrives at his home Dutch Grand Prix winless since Spain on Jun 23 — his longest drought in four years — with just one podium since, per Reuters via Flashscore (Aug 17). Mercedes has won three of the last four races, with Lewis Hamilton taking two of the last three, while McLaren has closed to within 42 points of Red Bull in the constructors’ standings; Verstappen makes his 200th F1 start at Zandvoort on Aug 23, calling it ‘always a fantastic atmosphere’ for the home fans.

headline: Romero Vows to 'Write My Name' Into Atletico History
body: Cristian Romero was officially unveiled by Atletico Madrid after his €40m (£34.2m) move from Tottenham on a five-year deal through 2031, per Goal.com (Aug 15). ‘I know the only way is by winning trophies, so I come with that mentality and I will give everything until the last day to achieve it,’ the Argentina defender said, adding that the club’s style ‘fits me perfectly.’

headline: Japan's Q2 Growth Badly Misses Forecasts, Complicating BOJ Timeline
body: Japan’s economy expanded just 0.3% quarter-on-quarter (1.1% annualized) in Q2, far under the 2.0% forecast and down from 1.9% growth in Q1, as capital expenditure contracted 1.2% and private consumption stayed flat, per InvestingLive (Aug 16). The miss complicates the Bank of Japan’s rate-hike path even as inflation runs at 2.6% y/y, and Asian markets opened cautiously Monday — the Nikkei up just 0.13%, Hang Seng futures up 0.6%, and Korea’s Kospi closed for a holiday — with the yen near 159.24 per dollar and traders awaiting China’s retail sales and industrial output data, per CNBC-TV18/TradingView (Aug 17).

headline: US Retail Sales Post Steepest Drop in a Year as Consumers Show Fatigue
body: US retail sales fell 0.6% in July to $763.6 billion, with online sales tumbling 2.2% and auto sales down 1.8% — the steepest monthly drop in over a year, per The Korea Times (Aug 15). The University of Michigan’s consumer sentiment gauge slid roughly 8% in August as inflation expectations rose to 4.3%, prompting Navy Federal Credit Union’s chief economist to say “American consumers are showing signs of fatigue—July retail sales were disappointing on all levels.”

headline: September Fed Rate-Hike Odds Plunge to 25% After Cooler Inflation Data
body: Wall Street odds of a Fed rate hike at the September FOMC meeting collapsed to 25% from 60% in early August, after June CPI fell 0.4% and July CPI rose just 0.1%, per 24/7 Wall St (Aug 16). But the Cleveland Fed’s core PCE model still shows inflation running at 3.3%, well above target, with gasoline prices up 27-38% year-over-year, leaving three more inflation reports before the FOMC meeting that could yet revive hike bets under new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh.

headline: Gold Holds Near $4,400 as Rate-Hike Fears Fade, Silver Tops $67
body: Spot gold traded around $4,394/oz Monday, up 9.6% over the past month and 32% year-on-year, after cooling US CPI data pushed futures briefly toward $4,500 last week, per TradingEconomics (Aug 17) and Intellectia (Aug 13). Silver has outperformed, surging past $67/oz, with persistent central-bank buying — particularly from China — and Fed rate-hike odds sliding to 25% continuing to support safe-haven demand.

headline: Brent Holds Near $89 as Hormuz Tanker Traffic Stays Crippled
body: Brent crude traded at $88.58/barrel Monday, roughly 33% higher than a year ago, with Strait of Hormuz transits still running at only about 10 vessels a day versus roughly 130 before the US-Israel-Iran war, per TradingEconomics (Aug 17) and Al Jazeera (Aug 12). “Markets have not completely lost hope for a deal, but confidence is clearly eroding,” one analyst told Al Jazeera, as Houthi attacks on shipping and stalled reopening talks keep a war-risk premium baked into prices.

headline: Stripe reportedly to acquire AI gateway startup OpenRouter for over $7 billion
body: Stripe is in talks to buy OpenRouter, which lets developers route requests across 400-plus AI models and claims 8 million users, per TechCrunch (Aug 16). The deal values OpenRouter far above the $1.3 billion mark it hit in a May Series B; a Stripe spokesperson declined to comment on the “rumors or speculation.”

headline: DeepSeek’s steep API price hikes take effect
body: DeepSeek’s new pricing for V4-Flash and V4-Pro kicked in Aug 16 at 16:00 UTC, replacing its flat-rate model with peak and off-peak billing that raises costs by 50% to over 1,100% depending on usage, per Quartz (Aug 13). The shift marks the end of the aggressive price war DeepSeek itself helped start in the API market.

headline: Anthropic’s Amodei says AI backlash is ‘a crisis of trust’
body: Responding to investor criticism that his own warnings fueled anti-AI sentiment, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said “I think it is fundamentally a crisis of trust,” per TechCrunch (Aug 16). He argued that “ordinary people don’t trust companies, governments, or the tech industry” and conceded AI firms, including Anthropic, have “not yet delivered on our big promises to benefit the world.”

headline: Zuckerberg’s AI manifesto meets public skepticism
body: Days after Mark Zuckerberg’s 6,500-word manifesto promising personal AI agents that “understand you, your goals, and everything you care about,” analysts say the pitch isn’t landing, per TechCrunch (Aug 16). Commentators noted the messenger problem given Meta’s social-media legacy of “ragebaiting and advertisements, not connection,” and pointed out Meta’s flagship Glimmer and Muse Spark products require specific hardware, undercutting the “for everyone” framing.

headline: Anthropic IPO chatter escalates from $2 trillion to $3 trillion
body: Just days after reports of a $2 trillion October IPO target, some investors are now floating $3 trillion, arguing that at “the incredibly low end” Anthropic’s growth justifies “30 times revenue… $3 trillion isn’t just defensible, it’s cheap,” per The Irish Times (Aug 15). Investors now expect Anthropic’s revenue run-rate to hit $100-120 billion by year-end, up from $47 billion in June, with valuations increasingly pegged to revenue multiples rather than profit.

headline: Ukraine Pounds Moscow With Record Drone Barrage as NATO Downs Russian Drone Over Romania
body: Ukraine launched one of its largest drone attacks of the war on Moscow, with Russia’s defence ministry claiming it downed 822 drones nationwide overnight while Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said 201 were destroyed over the capital region alone, per Al Jazeera (Aug 16). Russia’s retaliatory missile strikes killed a woman in Kryvyi Rih, while a Spanish F-18 on NATO air-policing duty shot down what alliance spokesman Martin O’Donnell called a drone that ‘appears to be Russian’ over Romania — the fourth such incursion into Romanian airspace this year.

headline: Kushner Holds Rare Direct Talks With Hamas Chief in Cairo Ahead of Netanyahu Meeting
body: Jared Kushner met Hamas leader Khalil al-Hayya in Cairo on Sunday, a rare direct US-Hamas contact aimed at reviving the stalled 15-point Gaza plan, per NPR (Aug 16). A Hamas official said the group is ‘committed and waiting for mediators to start the 14-day negotiation period,’ though it is still tying full disarmament to a path toward Palestinian statehood; Kushner, Tony Blair and Board of Peace director Nickolay Mladenov are due to meet Netanyahu Monday to press implementation.

headline: Iran Ties Hormuz Reopening to US Compliance as Israel Hits Lebanon in Deadliest Strikes Since Truce
body: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran is ‘continuing talks with Oman on shipping routes’ through the Strait of Hormuz but that any reopening still hinges on Washington honoring June’s memorandum of understanding, per Al Jazeera (Aug 16). Separately, Israeli strikes on Lebanon killed at least 11 people, the deadliest single episode since the June ceasefire with Hezbollah took effect.

headline: Venezuela’s Interim Government Frees 131 Political Prisoners in US-Brokered Reconciliation Push
body: Venezuela’s transitional government released 131 people classified as political prisoners on Aug 14 under a ‘Program for Peace and Democratic Coexistence,’ part of talks brokered since Nicolás Maduro’s ouster in January, per Al Jazeera (Aug 15). US Secretary of State Marco Rubio called the releases ‘a crucial step for the nation’s reconciliation process,’ though opposition figure Juan Pablo Guanipa said roughly 391 political prisoners remained held as of Aug 10 and demanded their release ‘without exception, without delay.’

headline: RSF Seizes Parts of Blue Nile’s Geisan as Sudan’s War Widens Into New Fronts
body: RSF fighters and allied SPLM-N forces stormed Geisan in Blue Nile state with artillery and drones, capturing the main market before Sudan’s army beat back some advances with its own strikes, per Sudan Tribune (Aug 11). The UN’s OCHA reported roughly 2,500 people displaced by the fighting and renewed its call on ‘all parties to protect civilians and civilian infrastructure, and to allow aid to reach people quickly, safely and without obstruction,’ per UN News (Aug 12), as this year’s $3bn Sudan aid appeal remains only 41% funded.

headline: Cloudflare lifts revenue guidance on AI-traffic milestone, then prices $2.175bn convertible notes
body: Cloudflare's second-quarter revenue rose 36% year-over-year to $696.1 million, prompting management to raise full-year guidance to a range of $2.86 billion to $2.87 billion, per Investing.com (Aug 10). The company also said non-human, machine-to-machine AI traffic has now crossed 50% of everything moving across its network, a milestone it points to as validating its push into agentic AI infrastructure. Days later Cloudflare priced a $2.175 billion convertible debt offering, with options for up to $2.5 billion, to fund further expansion — a raise several analysts, including Goldman Sachs, Wells Fargo, TD Cowen and UBS, treated as dilutive even as they lifted their price targets.

headline: Oracle plans fresh layoffs as AI data-centre capex balloons to $55.7bn
body: Oracle is preparing another round of job cuts this month, with some teams facing double-digit percentage reductions, as it manages the financial strain of its AI data-centre build-out, per Yahoo Finance (Aug 12). The cuts follow a prior fiscal year in which about 21,000 employees — 13% of the workforce — were let go, leaving headcount near 141,000; the company has already booked $1.8 billion in restructuring charges and expects up to $2.1 billion. Fiscal 2026 capital-expenditure guidance has been raised to $55.7 billion from an earlier $21.2 billion estimate as Oracle borrows heavily to finance the data-centre capacity it is building for AI customers.

headline: Twilio posts record $1.5bn quarter and lifts full-year growth outlook to 18%
body: Twilio reported second-quarter revenue of $1.499 billion, up 22% year-over-year and a company record, with non-GAAP diluted earnings per share of $1.47, per its Aug 6 results (via The Motley Fool, Aug 9). Organic growth accelerated to 17% from 16% in the prior quarter, and management raised full-year guidance for reported revenue growth to 18-18.5% and organic growth to 13-13.5%, up from a prior 9.5-10.5% organic outlook. Dollar-based net expansion reached 116%, meaning existing customers grew their spend at a double-digit clip even before counting new logos.

headline: CrowdStrike investors trim positions ahead of Aug 26 earnings amid stretched valuation
body: CrowdStrike saw elevated volatility this week as profit-taking swept through high-multiple growth software names ahead of the company's Aug 26 quarterly report, per TradingKey (Aug 14). Its price-to-sales ratio has expanded well above historical norms even as Wall Street holds an average price target of $193.61, and the report flagged heavy insider selling in recent months running alongside continued buying from quantitative funds. The activity looks like positioning into the print rather than a reaction to any new disclosure from the company itself.

headline: Beyond Meat completes 1-for-30 reverse split days after swinging back to profit and hiring a new COO
body: Beyond Meat's 1-for-30 reverse stock split took effect at 11:59pm ET on Aug 13, consolidating every 30 shares into one and cutting authorized shares from 3 billion to 100 million, a move the company says is meant to help it regain compliance with Nasdaq's minimum bid-price rule ahead of an Aug 31 deadline, per its GlobeNewswire release. The reset followed second-quarter results in which Beyond Meat posted sales of $68.83 million and swung to net income of $16.4 million, alongside the appointment of food-industry veteran Brijesh Krishnaswamy as chief operating officer and founder Ethan Brown's return to the board, per Yahoo Finance (Aug 9). Management guided third-quarter net revenue to $60-65 million.

headline: Sensus Healthcare revenue falls 68% as unit sales slow, though 8 shipped units await financing sign-off
body: Sensus Healthcare reported second-quarter revenue of $2.3 million, down from $7.3 million a year earlier, as unit shipments fell to 11 from 19, per its Aug 13 results (via StockTitan). Gross margin narrowed to 34.8% from 39.7%, and the company posted a net loss of $8.7 million, or $0.53 per share, versus a $1.0 million loss in the year-ago quarter, with negative adjusted EBITDA of $3.0 million. Management said eight units already shipped but pending financing approval should be recognized as revenue in the third quarter, and the company ended the period with $15.2 million in cash and no debt.

headline: Hydrofarm stays volatile in the wake of its $16m Aurora Peat divestiture
body: Hydrofarm Holdings completed the sale of its Aurora Peat Products division to Raven Holdings for $16 million, including a $5 million promissory note, with proceeds earmarked to pay down term-loan debt, per StocksToTrade (Aug 5). The company retained a long-term supply and distribution relationship with the divested unit and launched ‘Project Agility,’ a pivot toward an asset-light logistics and controlled-environment-agriculture services model. No fresh company-specific announcement was found for the session; as a thinly traded micro-cap, the stock has continued to swing sharply in the weeks since the divestiture rather than on any new news today.

headline: Doval reveals Modi's vow after Pahalgam: 'We will not forgive'
body: In an upcoming Discovery docuseries, "Declassified: Operation Sindoor," National Security Advisor Ajit Doval revealed PM Modi’s reaction after the Pahalgam terror attack, quoting him as saying, “We will go after them… whether they are on earth, in the sky or in hell, wherever they are. We will not forgive them,” per WION (Aug 16). Doval added that Operation Sindoor’s message was that India’s fight against terror continues “till the last terrorist is eliminated,” and that Pakistan needed to understand that supporting terrorism was intolerable to India.

headline: Chamoli tunnel toll holds at 8 as inquiry ordered, two still missing
body: Search operations for two workers — Lucas Topno of Jharkhand and Chetan Poyam of Chhattisgarh — entered a fourth day at the flooded THDC tunnel in Pipalkoti, Chamoli, with the toll steady at eight dead and twelve injured already rescued, per ThePrint (Aug 16). District Magistrate Gaurav Kumar has ordered a magisterial inquiry into the causes of the Aug 13 landslide that flooded the tunnel, as NDRF, SDRF and ITBP teams keep pumping out water to reach the trapped men.

headline: Jharkhand students vow August 20 gherao of CM Soren's residence
body: Marking the 23rd day of their agitation over alleged JPSC-JSSC exam irregularities, protesting students said they will gherao Chief Minister Hemant Soren’s residence on Aug 20 and burn effigies of Soren and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi at 24 district headquarters, per WION (Aug 16). “We seek his resignation as both the JMM and the Congress are playing politics with us,” said Ravindra Paswan of the JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch, as the state government cancelled three exams and brought in the Enforcement Directorate but resisted handing the case to the CBI.

headline: Reform Unveils £50bn Welfare Overhaul Targeting PIP
body: Reform UK will publish a 50-page welfare blueprint on Monday proposing £50bn in annual savings by scrapping PIP and the Universal Credit health element for working-age adults, changes that would hit 2.89 million of the UK’s 6.9 million disability benefit claimants, per Yahoo News (Aug 16). Treasury spokesman Robert Jenrick said “dumping our young people onto welfare isn’t compassion; it’s neglect,” while Labour branded the costings “fantasy economics” and the Conservatives accused Reform of trying to “distract attention” from the party’s ongoing donations probe.

headline: Stourbridge Families Return Home as Wildfire Cordons Lift
body: Three days after wildfires tore through Stourbridge in the West Midlands, fire crews significantly lifted cordons, letting eight families view homes destroyed in the blaze and 13 more households with partial damage return, alongside 85 evacuated households whose properties were unaffected, per Express & Star (Aug 16). Dudley council chief executive Balvinder Heran urged residents not to speculate about the fire’s cause while investigations continue, as community fundraising for affected families topped £125,000.

headline: Energy Bills Set to Reignite UK Cost-of-Living Squeeze
body: UK inflation is forecast to climb to 2.9% in July, up from 2.6%, after household energy price caps rose 13%, with the Bank of England warning headline inflation could hit 3.2% by year-end or as high as 4.5% by mid-2027 if Middle East tensions escalate, per The British Eye (Aug 16). RSM UK chief economist Thomas Pugh said “the cost of living squeeze is set to return to the headlines,” even as a government VAT cut due in October is expected to trim average electricity bills by about £45 a year.

headline: Qatar PM, Saudi FM Discuss Hormuz De-escalation
body: Qatar’s Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al-Thani held a phone call with Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan, stressing “the importance of all parties committing to dialogue and diplomacy” on implementing the US–Iran memorandum of understanding and preserving freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 16). The call came the same evening as separate Qatari calls with the foreign ministers of Jordan and Syria on de-escalating regional tensions.

headline: Qatar Joins 8 Nations Condemning Israel’s Gaza Roadmap Rejection
body: Qatar and the foreign ministers of seven other Arab and Islamic states — including Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Jordan, Egypt, Turkey, Pakistan and Indonesia — issued a joint statement condemning Israel’s rejection of a roadmap to implement the US-backed Gaza peace plan under UN Security Council Resolution 2803, per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 16). The ministers said “Israel now bears responsibility for obstructing the efforts to bring peace in Gaza” and reaffirmed calls for a two-state solution based on 1967 borders with East Jerusalem as its capital.

headline: Iran Demands Qatar Allow Pilot Investigators
body: Iran formally asked Qatar to admit an air force fact-finding team to probe the fate of three fighter pilots missing since Doha downed two Iranian jets on Mar 2, with military official Mohammad Bagherzadeh saying the unit has “been waiting for months for permission to enter Qatar,” per Middle East Monitor (Aug 16). The request follows Qatar’s Aug 15 denial that it is detaining any Iranian pilots, deepening a diplomatic rift that has also drawn in Kuwait over four additional detained Iranians.

headline: Colorverse Experience Continues at Katara
body: This immersive family exhibition blending colour, light, sound and interactive challenges runs at Katara South Parking, Katara Cultural Village, through Sep 15, open 4pm–10pm on weekdays and until 11pm on weekends, per Platinumlist (Aug 17). Tickets start at QAR 35 for the roughly 35-minute journey through seven interactive zones designed to “restore the primary RGB colors.”

headline: Tasweer Marks World Photography Day at Fire Station
body: Tasweer hosts “Together in Photography: World Photography Day” at Fire Station Cinema on Aug 19 from 6:30pm–8:30pm, unveiling the winners of the 2026 Tasweer Awards, per Gulf Times (Aug 12). The evening also explores photography’s role in preserving memory and will be live-streamed on Tasweer’s digital platforms for international audiences.

headline: PAW Patrol: The Big Show Rescue Hits Qatar Mall
body: A free family stage show brings Nickelodeon’s PAW Patrol characters to the Oasis Stage at Qatar Mall from Aug 20–29, per Qatar Living’s weekly roundup (Aug 16). It’s one of several family-friendly picks in this week’s “events to check out” list alongside museum activities and workshops around Doha.

headline: A 3-year-old girl and a 75-year-old man were pulled alive from Colombia’s earthquake rubble after more than 100 hours, as Indonesia’s Flores Island quake toll climbs to 51 and Zambia’s vote count resumes after ballot theft and a polling agent’s killing.

Stripe is reportedly buying AI-routing startup OpenRouter for over $7 billion — five times its May valuation — as Anthropic’s Dario Amodei calls the industry’s public backlash ‘fundamentally a crisis of trust.’

Ukraine hit Moscow with one of its largest drone barrages of the war as a NATO jet downed a Russian drone over Romania — the fourth such incursion this year — and Kushner held rare direct talks with Hamas’s chief in Cairo.
Modi’s NSA Ajit Doval revealed the PM’s vow after Pahalgam to hunt terrorists ‘on earth, in the sky or in hell,’ as Chamoli’s tunnel toll holds at eight with two workers still missing.
September Fed rate-hike odds have collapsed to 25% and gold holds near $4,400, while Oracle plans fresh layoffs even as it lifts AI data-centre capex guidance to $55.7 billion.
Flores Island Quake Toll Rises to 20 as Indonesia Lifts Tsunami Warning
body: The confirmed death toll from Monday’s magnitude-7.7 earthquake off Flores Island climbed to 20 across four towns, per Manila Times (Aug 16), with rescue official Fathur Rahman saying “20 people have died, six are injured, and two are still buried.” Two people remained trapped under rubble in Manggarai regency; the initial tsunami warning has been lifted, though authorities continue monitoring sea levels.

headline: Colombia Earthquake Death Toll Nears 290 as Missing Count Falls to 140
body: The toll from last Monday’s magnitude-7.4 quake climbed to around 290 dead and nearly 4,000 injured, while the missing count fell to 140 as more bodies were recovered, per The Jerusalem Post (Aug 16). Cali fire captain Alberto Hernandez said “we have only one site where there are signs of life — at the other locations, we are unfortunately in the phase of recovering bodies,” while Cali Mayor Alejandro Eder vowed to keep searching “as if those 70 people were still alive — miracles do happen.”

headline: Fresh Heat Wave Pushes Into France, Italy and Spain as Germany’s Toll Hits 12,500
body: A new wave of extreme heat is forecast to push temperatures past 35°C for more than 135 million people across France, Italy and Spain, per Al Jazeera (Aug 13), even as Germany’s cumulative 2026 heat-death toll passed 12,500 — already 40% above its previous annual record and approaching Italy’s 2022 all-time national high of 18,010. Roughly 9,600 of Germany’s deaths occurred in a single week in late June when temperatures topped 40°C, and a Robert Koch Institute spokeswoman cautioned “the true toll may be higher.”

headline: Zambia Resumes Vote Count After Violence Halted Election Tally
body: Zambia’s Electoral Commission resumed counting on Aug 15 after suspending it a day earlier over “attacks on polling staff and stolen ballot papers,” per The Peninsula (Aug 15), with chairperson Mwangala Zaloumis saying “the security threat to the electoral process has been contained.” Opposition leader Brian Mundubile still claims outright victory based on his party’s parallel vote count, alleging intimidation “orchestrated and exploited by elements associated with the state,” while the ECZ’s own partial tally so far shows incumbent Hakainde Hichilema ahead in the few constituencies counted.

headline: Japan’s Chiba Region Reels From Heaviest Rainfall Since Records Began
body: The Japan Meteorological Agency formally named the disaster the “August 2026 Chiba Heavy Rain” after 351mm fell in a single day — smashing the prior record of 259.5mm set in 1996 and marking the highest daily total since 1966 — per The Watchers (Aug 14). Eight people have died across Chiba City, Ichikawa, Kashiwa, Sakura and Yachiyo, with 36,063 residents under Level 4 evacuation orders and about 19,600 homes still without power.

headline: Barcelona's Rodri chase enters its final 48 hours
body: Barcelona have given themselves a 48-hour deadline to seal a Rodri transfer worth up to €80m, with the two sides discussing a compromise around a €70m fixed fee plus bonuses and club president Joan Laporta prepared to step directly into the negotiations, per Goal.com (Aug 14). The World Cup-winning midfielder has ruled out Real Madrid and wants only Barcelona, who hope to have terms agreed with Manchester City by Monday in time to parade him at the Joan Gamper Trophy.

headline: Rain interrupts Galle Test as Padikkal's maiden century holds firm
body: Persistent rain delayed the start of day two at Galle, with India resuming on 288/2 — Devdutt Padikkal unbeaten on a maiden Test century of 131 and Rishabh Pant not out on 27 — per Cricket News (Aug 16). KL Rahul retired hurt with cramps after making 77, and Sri Lanka will lean on Prabath Jayasuriya, who has taken 81 wickets in 11 Tests at this ground, to break the stand once play resumes.

headline: Trent Rockets face Super Giants and SunRisers in Hundred double-header at Lord's
body: The Hundred's Finals Day arrives at Lord's today: table-topping Trent Rockets face Manchester Super Giants in the men's final at 6pm, after the Super Giants beat SunRisers Leeds by 20 runs in Friday's eliminator, per Sky Sports (Aug 15). Trent Rockets' women meet SunRisers Leeds at 2:15pm, with Phoebe Litchfield — the tournament's leading scorer with 293 runs at a strike rate of 169.3 — chasing a Lord's double.

headline: Cristian Romero completes £34.2m Atletico Madrid move
body: Tottenham captain Cristian Romero has confirmed his exit after five seasons, with Atletico Madrid paying £34.2m (€40m) and Spurs retaining a 15% sell-on clause, per Sky Sports (Aug 15). “Today, I say goodbye to a place that, for five seasons, was much more than a club,” Romero wrote on Instagram, reflecting on 124 appearances and a trophy won during his time in north London.

headline: Verstappen unveils farewell Zandvoort helmet as F1 gears up to return
body: Max Verstappen unveiled a white-and-blue ‘Delfts Blauw’ helmet for what he called his “last home race,” with 2026 marking Zandvoort's final appearance on the F1 calendar after the sport confirmed in 2024 it would drop the circuit, per GPFans (Aug 14). “Final home race, a special helmet, a homage to The Netherlands and Zandvoort,” Verstappen wrote on social media, ahead of a track where he has podiumed in all five editions since 2021 — while trailing championship leader Kimi Antonelli by 50 points as F1 resumes August 21-23.

headline: Silver Lake’s Workday buyout talks deepen, deal now valued near $51B
body: Silver Lake’s talks to take Workday private deepened through the week, with the HR-software maker now valued near $51 billion after shares surged nearly 18% to close at $206.45, per Axios (Aug 14). Silver Lake is weighing bringing in additional investors — echoing its $55 billion Electronic Arts take-private with Saudi Arabia’s PIF and Affinity Partners — with Constellation Research’s Holger Mueller noting “Workday is a cheap stock, with a market cap of roughly 20% of SAP.” Reuters cautions “the talks are ongoing and there is no guarantee a deal will materialize.”

headline: Databricks’ $5B round closes as CEO says AI token costs ‘freaked out the CFOs’
body: Databricks’ oversubscribed $5 billion round — which drew $15 billion in demand against an initial $1 billion target — closed at a $190 billion valuation led by Coatue, with Blackstone, MGX, T. Rowe Price and Sixth Street Growth joining, per TechTimes (Aug 14). CEO Ali Ghodsi said surging AI token costs have “freaked out the CFOs,” pushing enterprises toward cheaper Chinese models, which have captured up to 46% of routed tokens since February.

headline: Brent holds near $89 as Hormuz transits stay crippled at 10 ships a day
body: Brent crude eased slightly to $88.88 a barrel Friday after spiking near $90 earlier in the week, with Strait of Hormuz transits still crippled at roughly 10 vessels daily versus about 130 before the conflict, per Al Jazeera (Aug 12) and Rio Times’ Aug 15 markets briefing. KCM Trade’s Tim Waterer said “markets have not completely lost hope for a deal, but confidence is clearly eroding,” while the EIA doesn’t expect Middle East output to normalize until early 2027.

headline: Gold jumps to $4,461 as cool CPI locks in bets the Fed holds rates
body: Gold jumped 1.78% to $4,461/oz Friday, a two-month high, as July’s in-line 3.4% CPI reading cemented bets the Fed holds its 3.50%-3.75% rate in September, per Rio Times’ Aug 15 economic briefing and Motley Fool (Aug 12). Morgan Stanley’s Ellen Zentner said “in-line inflation will keep the ‘no need to hike rates’ narrative that took hold after last week’s jobs report intact,” with CME FedWatch pricing roughly 62% odds the Fed stays on hold.

headline: Kospi hits three-week high as SK Hynix, Samsung ride AI chip demand
body: South Korea’s Kospi surged 2.42% to 6,977.94 Friday — a three-week high and its fifth straight advance, up nearly 25% from its July 30 low — as SK Hynix (+3.26%) and Samsung Electronics (+2.43%) rallied on AI chip demand and SanDisk’s bullish long-term revenue outlook, per the Korea Times (Aug 14). Foreign investors poured a net 3.03 trillion won into Korean shares, while LG Electronics gained after LG Group chief Koo Kwang-mo met Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to “advance their partnership in physical AI.”
